\noindent[\textbf{14 AD}]\index{Subject}{Rado's selection lemma} (Depends on $k\in\omega, k\geq 2)\ P(k)$: If $X$ is a set and $P$ is a property of subsets of $X$ of finite character (that is, $\forall y\subseteq X(P(y)$ iff $\forall z\subseteq y(z$ finite $\rightarrow P(z))))$, then if every finite subset of $X$ can be partitioned into $k$ or fewer $P$-sets (that is, sets $z$ such that $P(z)$), then $X$ can be partitioned into $k$ or fewer $P$-sets. Cowen \cite{bib:1982}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AE}] For any distributive lattice $D$ with zero and unit, any ideal $J\subseteq D$ and $a\not\in J$, there is a prime filter $F$ such that $a\in F$ and $F\cap J=\emptyset$. Banaschewski\index{Author}{Banaschewski} \cite{bib:1981}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AF}] Disjoint Transversal axiom\index{Subject}{linking axiom} (2,3): If $X$ is a set, $\mathcal{U}$ is a subset of $\{y\subseteq X:|y|\leq 2\}$ and $\mathcal{V}$ is a subset of $\{y\subseteq X:|y|\leq 3\}$ and if for each two finite subsets $\mathcal{U}_{0}\subseteq \mathcal{U}$ and $\mathcal{V}_{0}\subseteq \mathcal{V}$ there are transversals $Y_{1}$ and $Y_{2}$ for $\mathcal{U}_{0}$ and $\mathcal{V}_{0}$ respectively such that $Y_{1}\cap Y_{2}=\emptyset$, then there are disjoint transversals $X_{1}$ and $X_{2}$ for $\mathcal{U}$ and $\mathcal{V}$ respectively. $(Y\subseteq X$ is a transversal for $\mathcal{U}$ if for all $y\in \mathcal{U},\, y\cap Y\neq(\emptyset.)$ Schrijver\index{Author}{Schrijver} \cite{bib:1978}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AG}] Topological Rado Lemma: Let $\{T_{i}:i\in I\}$ be a family of compact Hausdorff spaces and suppose for each finite $F\subseteq I$, there is a set $\Phi(F)$ of partial choice functions on $I$ whose domains include $F$ and such that (a) $F_{1}\subseteq F_{2}$ implies $\Phi(F_{2})\subseteq\Phi(F_{1})$ and (b) the set $\{\phi|F:\phi\in\Phi(F)\}$ is closed in $\prod\{T_{i}:i\in F\}$ in the product topology. Then there is a choice function $f$ on $I$ satisfying for any finite $F\subseteq I,\,\exists\phi\in\Phi(F)$ such that $f$ and $\phi$ coincide on $F$. Rav\index{Author}{Rav} \cite{bib:1977}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AH}] Principle of Consistent Choices: Let $\{T_{i}:i\in I\}$ be a family of compact Hausdorf spaces and suppose $R$ is a symmetric binary relation defined for all pairs of elements belonging to distinct $T_{i}$ and such that for all $i\neq j$ in $I$, the set $E(i, j)=\{(x, y):x\ R\ y$ and $x\in T_{i}$ and $y\in T_{j}\}$ is closed in $T_{i}\times T_{j}$. Furthermore suppose that for every finite subset $F\subseteq I$, with at least two elements, $\exists\phi\in\prod\{T_{i}:i\in F\}$ such that $\phi(i)\ R\ \phi(j)$ for all $i\neq j$ in $F$. Then $\exists f\in\prod\{T_{i}:i\in I\}$ such that $f(i)\ R\ f(j)$ for all $i\neq j$ in $I$. Rav \cite{bib:1977}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AI}] Engelers Lemma:\index{Subject}{Engelers lemma} Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a family of functions whose domains are subsets of a set $S$ with range $\subseteq\{0,1\}$ and such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] For every finite $F\subseteq S,\,\exists\phi\in \mathcal{E}$ with domain F.
\item[(b)] The restriction of any function in $\mathcal{E}$ to any subset of its domain is in $\mathcal{E}$.
\item[(c)] If $\phi$ is any function with domain $\phi\subseteq S$ such that the restriction of $\phi$ to any finite subset of its domain is in $\mathcal{E}$ then $\phi\in \mathcal{E}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\exists f\in \mathcal{E}$ whose domain is $S$. Rav \cite{bib:1977}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AJ}] Robinson's Valuation Lemma:\index{Subject}{Robinson's valuation lemma} Let $\{\phi_{x}:x\in X\}$ be a family of partial valuations on a set $S$. $(\phi$ is a partial valuation on $S$ if the domain of $\phi \subseteq S$ and the range of $\phi \subseteq\{0,1\}.)$ Suppose $\mathfrak{B}$ is a filter base on $X$ such that for every finite $F\subseteq S$ and for every $B\in \mathfrak{B}$ there is $x\in B$ such that $F\subseteq$ dom $\phi_{x}$. Then there is a total valuation $f$ on $S$ (that is, dom $f=S)$ such that for all finite $F\subseteq S$ and all $B\in \mathfrak{B},\,\exists x\in B$ such that $F\subseteq$ dom $\phi_{x}$ and $f|F=\phi_{x}|F$. $(\mathfrak{B}$ is a filter base means $\forall B_{1},\,B_{2}\in \mathfrak{B},\,\exists B_{3}\in \mathfrak{B}$ such that $B_{3}\subseteq B_{1}\cap B_{2}$.) Rav \cite{bib:1977} and Cowen \cite{bib:1973}. Compare with [14
I].

\noindent[\textbf{14 AK}] Let $X$ be a set and $\mathcal{D}=\{Y_{i}:i\in I\}$ a family of finite pairwise disjoint subsets of $\mathcal{P}(X)$. Suppose for every finite subset $\{a, b, \ldots, k\}$ of $I,\,\exists s\in I$ such
that $Y_{s}\subseteq Y_{a}\wedge Y_{b}\wedge\ldots\wedge Y_{k}$ (If $Y$ and $Z$ are finite pairwise disjoint sets then $Y\wedge Z= \{A \cap B:A\in Y$ and $B\in Z$ and $A \cap B\neq\emptyset\}.)$ Then there is a choice function $\mu$ whose domain includes $\mathcal{D}$ such that the family $\{\mu(Y_{i}):i\in I\}$ (where $\mu(Y_{i})\in Y_{i})$ of subsets of $X$ is closed under finite intersections. Rav\index{Author}{Rav} \cite{bib:1977}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AL}]\index{Subject}{Rado's selection lemma} The radical of a proper ideal $A$ in a commutative ring $R$ with identity is the intersection of all prime ideals in $R$ containing \emph{A}. (The \emph{radical} of $A= \{x\in R$: for some $m\in \omega,\, x^{m}\in A\}.)$ Rav \cite{bib:1977} and note 80.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AM}] Let $A$ be a subring of a commutative ring $R$ and $p$ a prime ideal in $A$ such that $p=Rp\cap A$. Then there is a prime ideal $J$ in $R$ such that $p=J\cap A$. Rav \cite{bib:1977} and note 80.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AN}] In every commutative ring with identity, every proper ideal is included in some prime ideal. Rav \cite{bib:1977}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AO}] Suppose $R$ is a commutative ring, $A$ is a proper ideal in $R$, and $S$ is a multiplicative semigroup in $R$ not meeting $A$. Then there is a prime ideal $p$ in $R$ such that $A\subseteq p$ and $p\cap S=\emptyset$. Rav \cite{bib:1977} and note 80.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AP}] Suppose to each finite subset $F$ of a set I there corresponds a set $\Phi(F)$ of functions whose domains are subsets of $I$ including $F$ and such that (a) $F_{1}\subseteq F_{2}$ implies $\Phi(F_{2})\subseteq\Phi(F_{2})$ and (b) $\forall i\in I,\,\big\{\phi(i):\phi\in\bigcup\{\Phi(F):F$ finite and $F\subseteq I\}\big\}$ is finite. Then there is a function $f$ with domain $I$ such that for all finite $F\subseteq I,\,\exists\phi\in\Phi(F)$ such that $\phi$ and $f$ coincide on F. Rav \cite{bib:1977}, Cowen\index{Author}{Cowen} \cite{bib:1973} and note 80.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AQ}] Strong Rado Lemma 1: Let $T$ be a family of finite sets and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a collection of finite subsets of $T$ satisfying

\noindent(1) $(\forall K\in T)(\exists S\in \mathcal{F})(K\in S)$

\noindent(2) $(\forall S_{1}, S_{2}\in \mathcal{F})(\exists S_{3}\in \mathcal{F})(S_{1}\cup
S_{2}\subseteq S_{3})$

\noindent Assume there is a function $\phi$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ such that for each $S\in \mathcal{F},\,\phi(S)= \phi_{S}$ is a function with domain $S$ and satisfies $(\forall K\in S)(\phi_{S}(K)\in K)$. Then there is a function $f$ with domain $T$ and with the following property: For all $S\in \mathcal{F}$ there is an $S^{\prime}\in \mathcal{F}$ such that $S\subseteq S^{\prime}$ and $f$ and $\phi_{S^{\prime}}$ agree on $S$. Howard\index{Author}{Howard} \cite{bib:1993}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AR}] Patching Lemma: Let $L$ be a local system of $S$ (that is, $L\subseteq \mathcal{P}(S)$ and for each finite $E\subseteq S$, there exists $H\in L$ such that $E\subseteq H$). Let $F$ be a set and $n$ a positive integer. Suppose that for each $H\in L$, there is a function $f_{H}:H^{n}\rightarrow F$ and $\{f_{H}(x):H\in L\}$ is finite for each $x\in S^{n}$. Then there is a function $f:S^{n}\rightarrow F$ such that for any finite subset $K\subseteq S^{n}$, there is an $H\in L$ with $K\subseteq H^{n}$ and $f$ and $f_{H}$ agree on K. Hickin/Plotkin\index{Author}{Hickin/Plotkin} \cite{bib:1976} and note 83.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AS}] Let $\mathfrak{A}$ and $\mathfrak{B}$ be (universal) algebras of type $r$ where $\mathfrak{A}$ and $\mathfrak{B}$ have underlying sets $A$ and $B$ respectively and $B$ is finite. Suppose for every finite $C\subseteq A$ there is a partial $r$ homomorphism from $\mathfrak{A}$ into $\mathfrak{B}$ with domain $C$. Then there is an $r$ homomorphism from $\mathfrak{A}$ into $\mathfrak{B}$ . van Benthem\index{Author}{Benthem} \cite{bib:1975}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AT}] Assume $D$ and $E$ are sets and for all $d\in D,\,d$ is finite. Suppose that for every finite $F\subseteq D$, there is an $S$ such that $(\forall f\in F)(f\cap S\in E)$. Then there is an $S$ such that $(\forall d\in D)(d\cap S\in E)$. van Benthem \cite{bib:1975}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AU}] If $Z$ is a real vector lattice with order unit 1 then the set of all positive linear functionals $u$ on $Z$ with $u(1)=1$ is a convex set that has an extreme point. See H. Rubin/J. Rubin\index{Author}{H. Rubin/J. Rubin} \cite{bib:1985}, pages 177 and 182 for definitions. Also see Gardiner\index{Author}{Gardiner} \cite{bib:1974}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AV}] Every Boolean algebra has a 2-valued measure. Pincus\index{Author}{Pincus} \cite{bib:1972c} and note 147.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AW}] The Compactness Theorem for Propositional Logic: If $\Sigma$ is a set of formulas in a propositional language such that every finite subset of $\Sigma$ is satisfiable, then $\Sigma$ is satisfiable. Henkin\index{Author}{Henkin} \cite{bib:1954b}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AX}] Structural Completeness Theorem for Propositional Logic: Assume $At$ is a set of propositional variables and $S$ is the set of propositional formulas generated by \emph{At}. Assume $X\subseteq S$ and $a\in S$ satisfy the following: For any function $e:At\rightarrow S$ if $Cn(\{b[e]:b\in X\})\subseteq Cn(\emptyset)$ then $a[e]\in Cn(\emptyset)$. Then $a\in Cn(X)$. $(Cn(Y)$ is the deductive closure of $Y\ \cup$ all substitutions of axioms for the classical predicate calculus and for $a\in S,\,a[e]$ is $a$ with each propositional variable $p$ replaced by $e(p).)$ Pogorzelski/Prucnal\index{Author}{Pogorzelski/Prucnal} \cite{bib:1974}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AY}] Let $F$ be a class of partial functions on $I$ of finite character such that (a) $\{f(\nu):f \in F\}$ is finite for each $\nu\in I$ and (b) for each finite $W \subseteq I$, there exists $f\in F$ with dom$(f)=W$. Then $F$ contains a function with domain $I$. ($F$ is of finite character means $f\in F$ iff for all finite $w\subseteq I, f|w\in F.)$ Cowen\index{Author}{Cowen} \cite{bib:1973}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 AZ}] Let $\Phi=\{\phi_{t}\}_{t\in T}$ be a set of partial valuations on a set $S$ (that is, dom$(\phi_{t})\subseteq S$ and range$(\phi_{t})\subseteq\{0,1\})$ such that for all finite $U\subseteq S$ there is a $t \in T$ for which $U\subseteq$ dom$(\phi_{t})$. Then there is a valuation $\Psi$ with dom$(\Psi)=S$ and such that for every finite $U\subseteq S$, there is a $t\in T$ with $U\subseteq$ dom$(\phi_{t})$ and $\Psi|U=\phi_{t}|U$. Cowen \cite{bib:1973}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BA}] Monteiro's\index{Author}{Monteiro} Theorem\index{Subject}{Monteiro's theorem} for Complete Atomic Boolean Algebras: Let $K$ be a complete atomic Boolean algebra, $A$ a subalgebra of the Boolean algebra $B$ and $f$ a homomorphism from $A$ to $K$. Let $d$ be a semimorphism from $B$ into $K$ (that is, $d:B\rightarrow K,\, d(0)=0,\,d(1)=1$ and for all $x,\,y\in B,\, d(x\vee y)=d(x)\vee d(y)\ )$ with $f(x)\leq d(x)$ for all $x\in A$. Then there is a homomorphism $h$ from $B$ to $K$ such that $h(x)\leq d(x)$ for all $x\in B$ and $h/A=f$. Monteiro \cite{bib:1965} and Bacsich\index{Author}{Bacsich} \cite{bib:1972}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BB}] Fra\"{\i}ss\'{e}'s Theorem:\index{Subject}{Fra\"{i} ss\'{e}'s theorem} Let $\mathcal{E}$ be inductively ordered (that is, for any $E,\,E^{\prime}\in \mathcal{E},\,\exists E^{\prime\prime}\in \mathcal{E}$ such that $E\cup E^{\prime}\subseteq E^{\prime\prime}$.) For any $E\in \mathcal{E}$, assume $\mathcal{R}_{E}$ is a finite set of $m$-ary relations on $E$. If for any $E,\,E^{\prime}\in \mathcal{E}$ with $E\subseteq E^{\prime}$ we have $\forall R\in \mathcal{R}_{E^{\prime}},\,R/E\in \mathcal{R}_{E}$ then there is an $m$-ary relation $S$ on $\bigcup \mathcal{E}$ such that $S|E\in \mathcal{R}_{E}$ for any $E\in \mathcal{E}$. B\'{e}n\'{e}jam\index{Author}{B\'{e}n\'{e}jam} \cite{bib:1970}. See [14 Y].

\noindent[\textbf{14 BC}] If $m_{0}$ is an additive, real valued measure on a subalgebra $\mathcal{B}_{0}$ of a Boolean algebra $\mathcal{B}$ then there exists a measure $m$ on $\mathcal{B}$ such that $m=m_{0}$ on $\mathcal{B}_{0}$ and the range of $m$ is contained in the closure of the range of $m_{0}$. Tarski\index{Author}{Tarski} \cite{bib:1930} and note 147.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BD}] Let $H$ be a hypergraph. If every finite subhypergraph has an independent vertex cover then $H$ has an independent vertex cover. Cowen \cite{bib:1990} and note 117.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BE}] Let $H$ be a hypergraph. If every finite subhypergraph is 2-colorable then $H$ is 2-colorable. Cowen \cite{bib:1990} and note 117.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BF}] Let $H$ be a hypergraph whose edges contain at most three vertices. If every finite subhypergraph of $H$ has an independent vertex cover then $H$ has an independent vertex cover. Cowen \cite{bib:1990} and note 117.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BG}] Let $H$ be a hypergraph whose edges contain at most three vertices. If every finite subhypergraph of $H$ is 2-colorable then $H$ is 2-colorable. Cowen\index{Author}{Cowen} \cite{bib:1990} and note 117.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BH}] The sum of finite frames is a spatial frame. Paseka\index{Author}{Paseka} \cite{bib:1989} and note 29.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BI}] Every compact, conjunctive frame is spatial. Paseka \cite{bib:1989} and note 29.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BJ}] The sum of compact, regular frames is spatial. Paseka \cite{bib:1989} and note 29.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BK}] The sum of 4-element Boolean algebras is spatial. Paseka \cite{bib:1989} and note 29.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BL}] Every compact, 0 dimensional frame is spatial. Paseka \cite{bib:1989} and note 29.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BM}] A system of equations over a finite ring $R$ has a solution in $R$ if and only if every finite sub-system has a solution in $R$. Abian\index{Author}{Abian} \cite{bib:1972} and note 30.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BN}] A system of equations over a finite field $F$ has a solution in $F$ if and only if every finite sub-system has a solution in $F$. Cowen/Emerson\index{Author}{Cowen/Emerson} \cite{bib:1995} and note 30.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BO}] A system of equations over a finite structure $(A, +, \cdot)$ has a solution in $A$, if and only if every finite sub-system has a solution in \emph{A}. note 30.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BP}] Every non-empty bounded distributive lattice has a prime ideal. Morillon\index{Author}{Morillon} \cite{bib:1988}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BQ}] Every proper ideal in a bounded distributive lattice is the intersection of the prime ideals containing it. Morillon \cite{bib:1988} and note 79. (Compare with [14 AE].)

\noindent[\textbf{14 BR}] Every $\vee$-compact non trivial lattice has a principal prime ideal. Morillon \cite{bib:1988}, \cite{bib:1985} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BS}] Every bounded distributive lattice has a prime ideal choice function. Morillon \cite{bib:1988}, \cite{bib:1985} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BT}] If $(A_{i})_{i\in I}$ is a family of bounded, distributive, $\vee$-compact lattices and if $(J_{i})_{i\in I}$ is a family such that for all $i\in I,\,J_{i}$ is a proper ideal in $A_{i}$ then there is a family $(P_{i})_{i\in I}$ such that for all $i\in I,\,P_{i}$ is a prime principal ideal in $A_{i}$ containing $J_{i}$. Morillon \cite{bib:1985}, \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BU}] If $(A_{i})_{i\in I}$ is a family of distributive non trivial bounded lattices, then there is a family $(f_{i})_{i\in I}$ such that each $f_{i}$ is a prime ideal choice function on $A_{i}$. Morillon \cite{bib:1985}, \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BV}] For every set $E$ there is an effectively $E$-adequate ultrafilter. Morillon \cite{bib:1988}, \cite{bib:1985} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BW}] For every set $E$ there is an ultrafilter choice function on $E$. Morillon \cite{bib:1985}, \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BX}] If $(E_{i})_{i\in I}$ is a family of sets and $(F_{i})_{i\in I}$ is a family such that for each $i,\,F_{i}$ is a filter in $\mathcal{P}(E_{i})$, then there is a family $(U_{i})_{i\in I}$ such that for each $i\in I,\,U_{i}$ is an ultrafilter in $\mathcal{P}(E_{i})$ containing $F_{i}$. Morillon \cite{bib:1985}, \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BY}] For every topological space $X$, every proper ideal in the normed $\mathbb{R}$-algebra of continuous bounded functions from $X$ into $\mathbb{R}$ is contained in a maximal ideal. Morillon\index{Author}{Morillon} \cite{bib:1988}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 BZ}] Every proper ideal in a non-trivial normed $\mathbb{R}$-algebra or $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with identity is contained in a maximal ideal. Morillon \cite{bib:1988}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 CA}] If $(A_{i})_{i\in I}$ is a family of non trivial commutative normed algebras with identity then there is a family $(J_{i})_{i\in I}$ such that for each $i\in I,\,J_{i}$ is a maximal ideal in $A_{i}$. Morillon \cite{bib:1988}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 CB}] If $X$ is a topological space and $I$ is a proper ideal in the algebra of all bounded continuous functions from $X$ to $\mathbb{R}$ such that every function in $I$ vanishes at at least one point of $X$ then $I$ is contained in a maximal ideal. Morillon \cite{bib:1988}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 CC}] A projective limit of compact topological spaces is compact. Morillon \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{14 CD}] A projective limit of a directed projective system of compact topological spaces is compact. Morillon \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{14 CE}] A projective limit of a directed projective system of compact nonempty topological spaces is non-empty. Morillon \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{14 CF}] A projective limit of a directed projective system of non-empty sets is non-empty. Morillon \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{14 CG}] A projective limit of a directed projective system of finite sets is compact. Morillon \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{14 CH}] For every bounded, distributive lattice $(A, \wedge, \vee)$ in which $0$ is $\wedge$-compact, for all $a\in A,\,a\neq 0$ and for all sequences $(X_{n})_{n\in\omega}$ of subsets of $A$, there is a prime filter in $A$ which contains $a$ and respects each $X_{n}$. Morillon \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{14 CI}] 3-Sat: Restricted Compactness Theorem for Propositional Logic II: If $\Sigma$ is a set of formulas in a propositional language such that every finite subset of $\Sigma$ is satisfiable and if every formula in $\Sigma$ is a disjunction of at most three literals, then $\Sigma$ is satisfiable. (A \emph{literal} is a propositional variable or its negation.) Cowen\index{Author}{Cowen} \cite{bib:1990}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 CJ}] The Completeness Theorem for Propositional Logic: Every consistent set of formulas is satisfiable. Henkin\index{Author}{Henkin} \cite{bib:1954a} and \cite{bib:1954b}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 CK}] The Completeness Theorem for First Order Logic: Every consistent set of formulas is satisfiable. Henkin \cite{bib:1954a} and \cite{bib:1954b}.

\noindent[\textbf{14 CL}] Gelfand Extreme Point Theorem:\index{Subject}{Gelfand extreme point theorem} If $A$ is a non-trivial Gelfand algebra then the closed unit ball in the dual of $A$ has an extreme point $e$ with $e\neq 0$. Morillon \cite{bib:1986}, notes 23 and 29.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 15.} $KW(\infty, \infty)$ (KW),\index{Subject}{Banach-Tarski paradox} The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle: For every set $M$ there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in M$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$. (See form $81(n)$). Kinna/Wagner\index{Author}{Kinna/Wagner} \cite{bib:1955}.

[\textbf{15 A}] $K(1)$: $(\forall M)(\exists\alpha$ an ordinal) $(|M|=|A|$ for some $A\subseteq \mathcal{P}(\alpha))$. (See form $81(n).)$ Jech \cite{bib:1973b}
p 53 prob 4.12 and Kinna/Wagner \cite{bib:1955}.

\noindent[\textbf{15 B}] SDO: For any family $X$ of infinite sets, there is a function $f$ with domain $X$ such that $\forall y\in X,\,f(y)$ is a dense linear ordering of $y$. Pincus\index{Author}{Pincus} \cite{bib:1997}.

\noindent[\textbf{15 C}] SUO: For any family $X$ of infinite sets, there is a function $f$ with domain $X$ such that $\forall y\in X,\,f(y)$ is an unbounded linear ordering of $y$. (An ordering is unbounded if there is neither a least element nor a greatest element.) Pincus\index{Author}{Pincus} \cite{bib:1997}.

\noindent[\textbf{15 D}]\index{Author}{Sierpi\'{n}ski} SDUO: For any family $X$ of infinite sets, there is a function $f$ with domain $X$ such that $\forall y\in X,\,f(y)$ is a dense unbounded linear ordering of $y$. Pincus \cite{bib:1997}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 16.} $C(\aleph_{0}, \leq 2^{\aleph_{0}})$: Every denumerable collection of non-empty sets each with power $\leq 2^{\aleph_{0}}$ has a choice function. Sierpi\'{n}ski \cite{bib:1918}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 17.} Ramsey's Theorem\index{Subject}{Ramsey's theorem} I: If $A$ is an infinite set and the family of all 2 element subsets of $A$ is partitioned into 2 sets $X$ and $Y$, then there is an infinite subset $B\subseteq A$ such that all 2 element subsets of $B$ belong to $X$ or all 2 element subsets of $B$ belong to $Y$. (Also, see form 325.) Jech\index{Author}{Jech} \cite{bib:1973b} p 164 prob 11.20 and Ramsey\index{Author}{Ramsey} \cite{bib:1929}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 18.} $PUT(\aleph_{0},2, \aleph_{0})$: The union of a denumerable family of pairwise disjoint pairs has a denumerable subset. Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1984f}.

[\textbf{18 A}] $PC(\aleph_{0},2, \infty)$: Every denumerable set of pairs has an infinite subset with a choice function.

\noindent[\textbf{18 B}] The union of a denumerable family of pairs has a denumerable subset. Note 135.

\noindent[\textbf{18 C}] $PC(WO, 2, \infty)$: Every infinite well ordered set of pairs has an infinite subset with a choice function.

\noindent[\textbf{18 D}] $PUT(WO, 2, WO)$: The union of an infinite well ordered family of pairwise disjoint pairs has an infinite well ordered subset. ([18D $\leftrightarrow$ 18)

\noindent\textbf{FORM 19.} A real function is analytically representable if and only if it is in Baire's classification.\index{Subject}{Baire's classification} G. Moore\index{Author}{G. Moore} \cite{bib:1982} (2.3.1).

\noindent\textbf{FORM 20.} If $\{A_{x}:x\in S\}$ and $\{B_{x}:x\in S\}$ are families of pairwise disjoint sets and $|A_{x}|=|B_{x}|$ for all $x\in S$, then $I\bigcup_{x\in S}A_{x}|=|\bigcup_{x\in S}B_{x}|$. G. Moore \cite{bib:1982} (1.4.12 and 1.7.8).

\noindent\textbf{FORM 21.} If $S$ is well ordered, $\{A_{x}:x\in S\}$ and $\{B_{x}:x\in S\}$ are families of pairwise disjoint sets, and $|A_{x}|=|B_{x}|$ for all $x\in S$, then $|\bigcup_{x\in S}A_{x}|=|\bigcup_{x\in S}B_{x}|$.
G. Moore \cite{bib:1982}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 22.} $UT(2^{\aleph_{0}},2^{\aleph_{0}},2^{\aleph_{0}})$: If every member of an infinite set of cardinality $2^{\aleph_{0}}$ has power $2^{\aleph_{0}}$, then the union has power $2^{\aleph_{0}}$. Borel\index{Author}{Borel} \cite{bib:1898} and G. Moore \cite{bib:1982}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 23.} $(\forall\alpha)(UT(\aleph_{\alpha}, \aleph_{\alpha}, \aleph_{\alpha}))$: For every ordinal $\alpha$, if $A$ and every member of $A$ has cardinality $\aleph_{\alpha}$, then $|\bigcup A|=\aleph_{\alpha}$. G. Moore \cite{bib:1982}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 24.} $C(\aleph_{0},2^{(2^{\aleph_{0}})})$: Every denumerable collection of non-empty sets each with power $2^{(2^{\aleph_{0}})}$ has a choice function. G. Moore \cite{bib:1982}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 25.} $\aleph_{\beta+1}$ is regular for all ordinals $\beta$. Feferman/Levy\index{Author}{Feferman/Levy} \cite{bib:1963} and Gitik\index{Author}{Gitik} \cite{bib:1980}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 26.} $UT(\aleph_{0},2^{\aleph_{0}},2^{\aleph_{0}})$: The union of denumerably many sets each of power $2^{\aleph_{0}}$ has power $2^{\aleph_{0}}$. Borel \cite{bib:1898}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 27.} $(\forall\alpha)(UT(\aleph_{0}, \aleph_{\alpha}, \aleph_{\alpha}))$: The union of denumerably many sets each of power $\aleph_{\alpha}$ has power $\aleph_{\alpha}$. G. Moore\index{Author}{G. Moore} \cite{bib:1982} p 36.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 28.}\index{Author}{Sierpi\'{n}ski} $C(\aleph_{0},2^{\aleph_{0}})$: Every denumerable collection of non-empty sets each with power $2^{\aleph_{0}}$ has a choice function. Sierpi\'{n}ski \cite{bib:1918}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 29.} If $|S|=\aleph_{0}$ and $\{A_{x}:x\in S\}$ and $\{B_{x}:x\in S\}$ are families of pairwise disjoint sets and $|A_{x}|=|B_{x}|$ for all $x\in S$, then $|\bigcup_{x\in S}A_{x}|=|\bigcup_{x\in S}B_{x}|$. G. Moore \cite{bib:1982} p 324.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 30.} Ordering Principle:\index{Subject}{ordering principle} Every set can be linearly ordered. Schr\"{o}der\index{Author}{Schr\"{o}der} \cite{bib:1988}.

[\textbf{30 A}] If $R$ is a partial ordering in which the set of predecessors of each element is linearly ordered, then there is a linear ordering extending $R$. Felgner\index{Author}{Felgner} \cite{bib:1969}.

\noindent[\textbf{30 B}] ADO: Every infinite set differs finitely from a set with a dense linear ordering: for all infinite $x$, there is a $y\subseteq x$ such that $y$ has a dense linear ordering and $x-y$ is finite. Pincus\index{Author}{Pincus} \cite{bib:1997}.

\noindent[\textbf{30 C}] SADO: For every set $F$ there is a function $f$ with domain $F$ such that for all $x\in F,\, f(x)\subseteq x,\,f(x)$ has a dense linear ordering, and $x-f(x)$ is finite. Pincus \cite{bib:1997}.

\noindent[\textbf{30 D}] UO: There exists an unbounded linear ordering on every infinite set. (An ordering is unbounded if there is neither a least element nor a greatest element.) Pincus \cite{bib:1997}.

\noindent[\textbf{30 E}] ADUO: For all infinite $x$, there exists $y\subseteq x$ such that $y$ has a dense unbounded linear ordering and $x-y$ is finite. Pincus \cite{bib:1997}.

\noindent[\textbf{30 F}] SADUO: For every set $F$ there is a function $f$ with domain $F$ such that for all $x\in F,\, f(x)\subseteq x,\,f(x)$ has a dense unbounded linear ordering, and $x-f(x)$ is finite. Pincus \cite{bib:1997}.

\noindent[\textbf{30 G}] Weak Hausdorff Lemma:\index{Subject}{Hausdorff lemma} For every set $X$, every $\subseteq$-chain in $\mathcal{P}(X)$ is contained in a maximal $\subseteq$-chain. Note 130.

\noindent \textbf{FORM 31.} $UT(\aleph_{0}, \aleph_{0}, \aleph_{0})$: The countable union theorem: The union of a denumerable set of denumerable sets is denumerable. Cantor\index{Author}{Cantor} \cite{bib:1878}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 32.} $C(\aleph_{0}, \leq\aleph_{0})$: Every denumerable set of non-empty countable sets has a choice function. Sierpi\'{n}ski \cite{bib:1918}.

[\textbf{32 A}] $C(\aleph_{0}, \aleph_{0})$. Every denumerable set of denumerable sets has a choice function.

\noindent[\textbf{32 B}] $PC(\aleph_{0}, \aleph_{0}, \infty)$: Every denumerable set of denumerable sets has an infinite subset with a choice function.

\noindent[\textbf{32 C}] $PC(WO, \aleph_{0}, \infty)$: Every infinite well ordered set of denumerable sets has an infinite subset with a choice function.

\noindent\textbf{\textbf{FORM 33($n$).}} If $n\in \omega-\{0,1\},\,C(LO, n)$: Every linearly ordered set of $n$ element sets has a choice function. Truss\index{Author}{Truss} \cite{bib:1973a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 34.} $\aleph_{1}$ is regular. Russell\index{Author}{Russell} \cite{bib:1906} and note 3.

[\textbf{34 A}] $\exists\alpha< \omega_{2}$ such that there are no hereditarily countable sets of rank $\alpha$. Jech\index{Author}{Jech} \cite{bib:1982} and note 48.

\noindent[\textbf{34 B}] $\omega_{1}$ with the order topology is not paracompact. Good/Tree\index{Author}{Good/Tree} \cite{bib:1995} and note 107.

\noindent[\textbf{34 C}]\index{Author}{Sierpi\'{n}ski} $\omega_{1}$ with the order topology has the property that every infinite subset has a limit point in $\omega_{1}$. Good/Tree \cite{bib:1995} and note 107.

\noindent[\textbf{34 D}] $\omega_{1}$ with the order topology does not contain a countable discrete family of open subsets. Good/Tree \cite{bib:1995} and note 107.

\noindent[\textbf{34 E}] $\omega_{1}$ with the order topology is not Lindel\"{o}f. Good/Tree \cite{bib:1995} and note 107.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 35.} The union of countably many meager subsets of $\mathbb{R}$ is meager. (Meager sets are the same as sets of the first category.) Feferman/Levy\index{Author}{Feferman/Levy}\index{Author}{Levy} \cite{bib:1963}, Jech\index{Author}{Jech} \cite{bib:1973b} p 7 prob 1.7, and note 28.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 36.} If $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^{n}$ and $A \bigcap B$ is countable for every bounded $B$ then $A$ is countable. G. Moore\index{Author}{G. Moore} \cite{bib:1982} p 36.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 37.} Lebesgue measure is countably additive. Sierpi\'{n}ski \cite{bib:1916}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 38.} $\mathbb{R}$ is not the union of a countable family of countable sets. Feferman/Levy \cite{bib:1963} and note 3.

[\textbf{38 A}] $UT(\aleph_{0}, \aleph_{0}, \neq 2^{\aleph_{0}})$: A denumerable union of denumerable sets does not have cardinality $2^{\aleph_{0}}$.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 39.} $C(\aleph_{1}, \infty)$: Every set $A$ of non-empty sets such that $|A|=\aleph_{1}$ has a choice function. Sierpi\'{n}ski \cite{bib:1918}, G. Moore \cite{bib:1982} p. 202.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 40.} $C(WO, \infty)$: Every well orderable set of non-empty sets has a choice function. G. Moore \cite{bib:1982} p 325.

[\textbf{40 A}] $A(L2, L1)$: For every $T_{2}$ topological space $(X, T)$, if each open cover of $X$ has a well ordered subcover, then each open cover has a well ordered refinement. Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1983d} and note 26.

\noindent[\textbf{40 B}] For all ordinals $\alpha$, the $\aleph_{\alpha}$ partition principle holds: For every ordinal $\alpha$ and every cardinal $\kappa$, if $\aleph_{\alpha}\leq^{\ast}\kappa$, then $\aleph_{\alpha}\leq \kappa$. Pelc\index{Author}{Pelc} \cite{bib:1978}, Banaschewski/Moore\index{Author}{Banaschewski/Moore} \cite{bib:1990}, and note 69.

\noindent[\textbf{40 C}] For each idemmultiple set $x\ (2\times x\approx x)$, if there exists a surjection $f$ mapping $x$ onto an ordinal $\lambda$ such that for each $\psi<\lambda,\,f^{-1}[\{\psi\}]$ is Dedekind infinite, then $\lambda\precsim x$. Higasikawa\index{Author}{Higasikawa} \cite{bib:1995} and note 94.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 41}. $W_{\aleph_{1}}$: For every cardinal $m,\,m\leq\aleph_{1}$ or $\aleph_{1}\leq m$. Jech \cite{bib:1973b}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 42.} L\"{o}wenheim-Skolem Theorem:\index{Subject}{L\"{o}wenheim-Skolem theorem} If a countable family of first order sentences is satisfiable in a set $M$ then it is satisfiable in a countable subset of $M$. G. Moore \cite{bib:1982} p 251.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 43.} $DC(\omega)$ (DC), Principle of Dependent Choices: If $S$ is a relation on a non-empty set $A$ and $(\forall x\in A)(\exists y\in A)(xSy)$ then there is a sequence $a(0),a(1),a(2),\ldots$ of elements of $A$ such that $(\forall n\in \omega) (a(n)\,S\,a(n+1))$. Tarski\index{Author}{Tarski} \cite{bib:1948} p 96 , Levy \cite{bib:1964} p 136 and note 54.

[\textbf{43 A}] Tarski's Lemma: Let $\{x(n) : n\in \omega\}$ be a denumerable collection of subsets of a Boolean algebra $B$ each of which has a meet in B. Then for any $a\neq 0$ in $B$ there is a proper filter $F$ of $B$ that decides $\bigwedge x(n)$ for all $n$ and has $a\in F$. ($F$ \emph{decides} $\bigwedge x(n)$ if either $\bigwedge x(n)\in F$ or $t\not\in F$ for some $t\in x(n).)$ Goldblatt\index{Author}{Goldblatt} \cite{bib:1985}.

\noindent[\textbf{43 B}]\index{Subject}{Tarski's lemma} Countable Henkin Principle:\index{Subject}{Henkin principle} Let $\Phi$ be the class of formulas in a language that includes the language of the sentential calculus. Let $I$ be a countable set of inferences, and $\Gamma$ a consistent subset of $\Phi$ such that $\Gamma \cup\{\psi\}$ respects $I$ for each $\psi\in\Phi$. Then for any $\phi \in\Phi$, if $\phi$ is consistent with $\Gamma$ then $\Gamma$ has a finitely consistent extension that contains $\phi$ and decides $I$. Goldblatt \cite{bib:1985} and note.

\noindent[\textbf{43 C}] Existence of a generic set: If $\mathcal{D}$ is a denumerable collection of dense sets in a partial order $(P, \leq)$ then for all $p\in P$ there is a $\mathcal{D}$ generic $G$ with $p\in G$. Goldblatt \cite{bib:1985} and note 47.

\noindent[\textbf{43 D}] If $\mathcal{D}$ is a denumerable collection of dense subsets of a partial order $(P, \leq)$ then for all $p\in P$ there is a sequence $f:\omega \rightarrow P$ with $f(0)=p$ and ($\forall n\in\omega)(f(n)\geq f(n+1))$ and range $(f) \cap D\neq\emptyset$ for all $D\in \mathcal{D}$. Goldblatt \cite{bib:1985}.

\noindent[\textbf{43 E}] The Baire Category Theorem for \v{C}ech Complete-I Spaces: Every \v{C}ech complete space is Baire. Goldblatt \cite{bib:1985} and note 28.

\noindent[\textbf{43 F}] Baire Category Theorem for Sequentially Complete Metric Spaces: Every sequentially complete metric space is Baire. Blair\index{Author}{Blair} \cite{bib:1977}, Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1983c}, Goldblatt \cite{bib:1985}, and note 28.

\noindent[\textbf{43 G}] Form 106 + form 154. Brunner \cite{bib:1983c} \cite{bib:1984b}.

\noindent[\textbf{43 H}] Every tree in which every element has at least one successor has a branch. Blass\index{Author}{Blass} \cite{bib:1979} and note note 21.

\noindent[\textbf{43 I}] Form [106 A] + form 10. Blass \cite{bib:1979}.

\noindent[\textbf{43 J}] Baire Category Theorem for Cantor Complete Metric Spaces: Every Cantor complete metric space is Baire. Brunner \cite{bib:1983c} and note 28.

\noindent[\textbf{43 K}] Let $M$ be a non-empty set partially ordered by $<$ without $<$-minimal elements. Then there is a subset $C$ of $M$ which is linearly ordered by $<$ such that $C$ has no $<$-minimal element. Note 146.

\noindent[\textbf{43 L}] $Z_{\omega}$: If every chain in a partially ordered set $P$ is finite, then $P$ contains a maximal element. Tarski\index{Author}{Tarski} \cite{bib:1948}, Wolk\index{Author}{Wolk} \cite{bib:1983}, and note 54.

\noindent[\textbf{43 M}] If $(X, \rho)$ is a complete metric space and $\phi:X\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is bounded above and upper semi-continuous then in the Br{\o}ndsted ordering, $(x\leq y$ iff $\rho(x, y)\leq \phi(y)-\phi(x))$, there is a maximal element. Brunner \cite{bib:1987a} and note 38.

\noindent[\textbf{43 N}] $RM1,\,\aleph_{0}$: The representation theorem for multi-algebras with $\aleph_{0}$ unary operations: Assume $(A, F)$ is a multi-algebra with $\aleph_{0}$ unary operations (and no other operations), then there is an algebra $(B, G)$ with $\aleph_{0}$ unary operations and an equivalence relation $E$ on $B$ such that $(B/E, G/E)$ and $(A, F)$ are isomorphic multi-algebras. Note 50 and H\"{o}ft/Howard\index{Author}{H\"{o}ft/Howard} \cite{bib:1981}.

\noindent[\textbf{43 O}] (Depends on $n\in\omega,\ n\geq 1)\ RM1,\,n$: The representation theorem for multi-algebras with $n$ unary operations: Assume $(A, F)$ is a multi-algebra with $n$ unary operations (and no other operations), then there is an algebra $(B, G)$ with $n$ unary operations and an equivalence relation $E$ on $B$ such that $(B/E, G/E)$ and $(A, F)$ are isomorphic multi-algebras. H\"{o}ft/Howard \cite{bib:1981} and note 50.

\noindent[\textbf{43 P}] The ultraproduct of a well founded structure by a countably complete ultrafilter is well founded. Spector\index{Author}{Spector} \cite{bib:1980} and note 54.

\noindent[\textbf{43 Q}] Matrix$(\omega)$: For every atomless poset $(P, \leq)$ and every family $D=\{D_{i}:i\in \omega\}$ of dense open subsets of $P$, there exists a matrix $C=\{C_{i}:i\in \omega\},\, |\bigcup C|=\omega$ of $P$ for $D$. Keremedis\index{Author}{Keremedis} \cite{bib:1996d} and note 132.

\noindent[\textbf{43 R}] Any partial order $(A, \leq)$ with no infinite descending chains is well founded, (that is, for all $X$ such that $\emptyset \neq X\subseteq A, X$ has a minimal element.) Spector\index{Author}{Spector} \cite{bib:1980} and note 54.

\noindent[\textbf{43 S}] If $S$ is a relation on $A$ such that $(\forall x\in A)(\exists y\in A)(x\,S\, y)$ and $x_{0}$ is any element of A, then there is a sequence $a(1),a(2),\ldots$ of elements of $A$ such that $a(n)\,S\,a(n+1)$ for all $n\in \omega$ and such that $a(0)=x_{0}$. Notes 101 and 54.

\noindent[\textbf{43 T}] A sequentially complete metric space is not meager. Note 28.

\noindent[\textbf{43 U}] Baire Category Theorem for Filter Complete Metric Spaces: Every filter complete metric space is Baire, Morillon\index{Author}{Morillon} \cite{bib:1988} and note 28.

\noindent[\textbf{43 V}] Every convex-compact set in a Hausdorff topological vector space with a basis of convex open sets is Baire. Fossy/Morillon\index{Author}{Fossy/Morillon} \cite{bib:1995} and note 23.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 44.} $DC(\aleph_{1})$: Given a relation $R$ such that for every subset $Y$ of a set $X$ with $|Y|<\aleph_{1}$ there is an $x\in X$ with $Y\ R\,x$, then there is a function $f:\aleph_{1}\rightarrow X$ such that $(\forall\beta<\aleph_{1})(\{f(\gamma):\gamma<b\}\,R\,f(\beta))$. Levy\index{Author}{Levy} \cite{bib:1964}.

\noindent \textbf{FORM 45($n$).} If $n\in \omega-\{0,1\},\,C(\infty, n)$: Every set of $n$-element sets has a choice function. Mostowski\index{Author}{Mostowski} \cite{bib:1945}, Truss\index{Author}{Truss} \cite{bib:1973a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 46($K$).} If $K$ is a finite subset of $\omega-\{0,1\},\,C(\infty, K)$: For every $n\in K$, every set of $n$-element sets has a choice function. Mostowski \cite{bib:1945}, Truss \cite{bib:1973a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 47($n$).} If $n\in \omega-\{0, 1\},\,C(WO, n)$: Every well ordered collection of $n$-element sets has a choice function. Mostowski \cite{bib:1945}, Truss \cite{bib:1973a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 48($K$).} If $K$ is a finite subset of $\omega-\{0, 1\},\,C(WO, K)$: For every $n\in K,\,C(WO, n)$. Mostowski \cite{bib:1945}, Truss \cite{bib:1973a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 49.} Order Extension Principle:\index{Subject}{order extension principle} Every partial ordering can be extended to a linear ordering. Tarski\index{Author}{Tarski} \cite{bib:1924} p 78.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 50.} Sikorski's\index{Author}{Sikorski} Extension Theorem:\index{Subject}{Sikorski's extension theorem} Every homomorphism of a subalgebra $B$ of a Boolean algebra $A$ into a complete Boolean algebra $B^{\prime}$ can be extended to a homomorphism of $A$ into $B^{\prime}$. Sikorski \cite{bib:1964}, p 141.

[\textbf{50 A}] Every complete Boolean algebra is injective. Banaschewski\index{Author}{Banaschewski} \cite{bib:1988}.

\noindent[\textbf{50 B}] Monteiro's\index{Author}{Monteiro} Theorem:\index{Subject}{Monteiro's theorem} Let $K$ be a complete Boolean algebra, $A$ a subalgebra of the Boolean algebra $B$ and $f$ a homomorphism from $A$ to $K$. Let $d$ be a semimorphism from $B$ into $K$ (that is, $d:B\rightarrow K, d(0)=0,\,d(1)=1$ and for all $x$ and $y$ in $B,\,d(x\vee y)=d(x)\vee d(y))$ with $f(x)\leq d(x)$ for all $x\in A$. Then there is a homomorphism $h$ from $B$ to $K$ such that $h(x)\leq d(x)$ for all $x\in B$ and $h/A=f$. Monteiro \cite{bib:1965} and Bacsich\index{Author}{Bacsich} \cite{bib:1972}.

\noindent[\textbf{50 C}] Every DeMorgan compact regular frame is injective in the category of all such frames. Banaschewski \cite{bib:1988}, notes 29 and 60.

\noindent[\textbf{50 D}] For any extension $M\supseteq L$ of a compact regular frame $L$, there is an $s\in M$ maximal with respect to the property that $x\vee s=1\rightarrow x=1$ for all $x\in L$. Banaschewski \cite{bib:1988}, notes 29 and 60.

\noindent[\textbf{50 E}] Form 14 + form 297. Banaschewski \cite{bib:1988} and Bell\index{Author}{Bell} \cite{bib:1988}.

\noindent[\textbf{50 F}] For any complete Boolean algebra $B$ and any subalgebra $A$ of $B$, there is a $U\in V^{(B)}$ such that $V^{(B)}\models ``U$ is an ultrafilter on $A$ and $U^{B}\subseteq U\mbox{''}$. $(V^{(B)}$ is the Boolean valued universe constructed from $B,\,U^{B}=\{(\hat{x}, x):x\in B\}$ is the canonical ultrafilter on $B$ and $x\mapsto\hat{x}$ is the canonical embedding of $V$ into $V^{(B)}.)$ Bell\index{Author}{Bell} \cite{bib:1977} and \cite{bib:1983}.

\noindent[\textbf{50 G}]\index{Author}{Sierpi\'{n}ski} For any complete Boolean algebra $B$ and any $C\in V^{(B)}$ such that $V^{(B)}\models ``C$ is a Boolean algebra.'' there is a $U\in V^{(B)}$ such that $V^{(B)}\models ``U$ is an ultrafilter in \emph{C}.'' See [50 F] for definitions. Bell \cite{bib:1983}.

\noindent[\textbf{50 H}] If $m:A\rightarrow B$ is a monomorphism between Boolean algebras, then there is an $m$-minimal epimorphism $p:B\rightarrow C$ to some Boolean algebra \emph{C}. $(p$ is $m$-minimal if (1) $p\circ m$ is monic and (2) if $q:C\rightarrow D$ is any epimorphism to a Boolean algebra $D$ such that $q\circ p\circ m$ is monic, then $q$ is an isomorphism.) Bell \cite{bib:1988}.

\noindent[\textbf{50 I}] If $A$ is a subalgebra of a Boolean algebra $B$, then there is a $\subseteq$-maximal proper filter $F$ in $B$ such that $F\cap A=\{1\}$. Bell \cite{bib:1988}

\noindent[\textbf{50 J}] Form 299 + form 14. Bell \cite{bib:1988}.

\noindent[\textbf{50 K}] Form 300 + form 14. Bell \cite{bib:1988}.

\noindent[\textbf{50 L}] Form 301 + form 14. Bell \cite{bib:1988}.

\noindent[\textbf{50 M}] Form 302 + form 14. Bell \cite{bib:1988}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 51.} Cofinality Principle:\index{Subject}{cofinality principle} Every linear ordering has a cofinal sub well ordering. Sierpi\'{n}ski \cite{bib:1918} p 117.

[\textbf{51 A}] For all linear orders $(X, \leq)$, there is a $\displaystyle \sup$ function on the bounded, well ordered subsets of $X$. Manka\index{Author}{Manka} \cite{bib:1988a} and note 38.

\noindent[\textbf{51 B}] $Z(L, W)$: Every non-empty linearly ordered set in which every well ordered subset has an upper bound has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin \cite{bib:1976}, Manka \cite{bib:1988a}, H. Rubin/J. Rubin\index{Author}{Harper/Rubin}\index{Author}{H. Rubin/J. Rubin} \cite{bib:1985} p 37 $M1(L, W)$, and note 39.

\noindent[\textbf{51 C}] For every linearly ordered set $(X, \leq)$, if every well ordered subset of $X$ is bounded above then there is a sup function on the well ordered subsets of \emph{X}. Manka \cite{bib:1988a} and note 38.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 52.} Hahn-Banach Theorem:\index{Subject}{Hahn-Banach theorem} If $V$ is a real vector space and $p:V\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ satisfies $p(x+y)\leq p(x)+p(y)$ and $(\forall t>0)(p(tx)=tp(x))$ and $S$ is a subspace of $V$ and $f:S\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is linear and satisfies $(\forall x\in S)(f(x)\leq p(x))$ then $f$ can be extended to $f^{\ast}:V\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that $f^{\ast}$ is linear and $(\forall x\in V)(f^{\ast}(x)\leq p(x))$.
L\'{o}s/Ryll-Nardzewski\index{Author}{{\L}o\'{s}/Ryll-Nardzewski}
 \cite{bib:1951}.

[\textbf{52 A}] On every Boolean algebra there is an additive real valued measure. Luxemburg\index{Author}{Luxemburg} \cite{bib:1969} and note 147.

\noindent[\textbf{52 B}] For every proper filter $\mathcal{F}$ of elements of a Boolean algebra $\mathcal{B}$, there exists an additive, real valued measure $m$ on $\mathcal{B}$ such that $m(x)=1$ for all $x\in \mathcal{F}$. Luxemburg \cite{bib:1969} and note 147.

\noindent[\textbf{52 C}] For every non-empty set X and every proper ideal $\mathcal{I}$ of in $\mathcal{P}(X)$ there is a measure $m$ on $\mathcal{P}(X)$ such that $m(x)=0$ for all $x\in \mathcal{I}$. Luxemburg \cite{bib:1969} and note 147.

\noindent[\textbf{52 D}] Let $\mathcal{B}_{0}$ be a subalgebra of a Boolean algebra $\mathcal{B}$ and $m_{0}$ an additive, real valued measure on $\mathcal{B}_{0}$. Then there is a real valued, additive measure $m$ on $\mathcal{B}$ such that $m=m_{0}$ on $\mathcal{B}_{0}$ and the range of $m$ is contained in the closed convex hull of the range of $m_{0}$. Luxemburg\index{Author}{Luxemburg} \cite{bib:1969} and note 147.

\noindent[\textbf{52 E}] The unit ball is convex-compact in the weak$^\ast$ topology in the dual of a Banach space. (See [14 Q].) Luxemburg \cite{bib:1969}, H. Rubin/J. Rubin \cite{bib:1985} p 178, and note 23.

\noindent[\textbf{52 F}] If $X$ is a topological vector space then for every continuous sublinear functional $p$ on $E$ there is a linear functional $f$ on $E$ such that $f\leq p$. Fossy/Morillon\index{Author}{Fossy/Morillon} \cite{bib:1995}.

\noindent[\textbf{52 G}] If $X$ is a normed vector space then for every continuous sublinear functional $p$ on $E$ there is a linear functional $f$ on $E$ such that $f\leq p$. Fossy/Morillon \cite{bib:1995}.

\noindent[\textbf{52 H}] Existence of Real Valued Banach Limits: For any directed set $(\Delta, \sqsubseteq)$ there exists a (real valued) Banach limit. Schechter\index{Author}{Schechter} \cite{bib:1996b} and note 31.

\noindent[\textbf{52 I}] Real Valued Convex Domination Theorem: For every real vector space $X$, every subspace $X_{0}\subseteq X$, every linear $\lambda_{0}:X_{0}\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ and every convex $p:X\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$, if $\lambda_{0}\leq p$ on $X_{0}$ then $\lambda_{0}$ can be extended to a linear map $\lambda:X\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that $\lambda\leq p$ on $X$. Schechter \cite{bib:1996b} and note 31.

\noindent[\textbf{52 J}] Support Theorem for Real Valued Convex Functions: For every real vector space $X$, every convex function $p:X\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is a pointwise maximum of affine functions. Schechter \cite{bib:1996b} and note 31.

\noindent[\textbf{52 K}] Sandwich Theorem for Real Valued Functions: For every real vector space $X$, if $e:X\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is a concave function, $g:X\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is a convex function, and $e\leq g$ everywhere on $X$, then there exists an affine function $f: X\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ satisfying $e\leq f\leq g$ everywhere on $X$. Schechter \cite{bib:1996b} and note 31.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 53.} For all infinite cardinals $m,\,m^{2}\leq 2^{m}$. Mathias\index{Author}{Mathias} \cite{bib:1979} prob 1336.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 54.} For all infinite cardinals $m,\,m\ \mathrm{adj}\ 2^{m}$ implies $m$ is an aleph. ($m\ \mathit{adj}\ n$ iff $m<n$ and $(\neg\exists p)(m<p<n).)$ Mathias \cite{bib:1979} prob 1337, thm 1338 and prob 1339.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 55.} For all infinite cardinals $m$ and $n$, if $m\cdot n=m+n$ then, $m\leq n$ or $n\leq m$. Mathias \cite{bib:1979} p 125.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 56.} $\aleph(2^{\aleph_{0}})\neq\aleph_{\omega}$. ($\aleph(2^{\aleph_{0}})$ is Hartogs' aleph, the least $\aleph$ not $\leq 2^{\aleph_{0}}$.) Mathias \cite{bib:1979} p 125.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 57.} If $x$ and $y$ are Dedekind finite sets then either $|x|\leq|y|$ or $|y|\leq|x|$. Mathias \cite{bib:1979} p 125 and note 94.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 58.} There is an ordinal $\alpha$ such that $\aleph(2^{\aleph_{\alpha}})\neq\aleph_{\alpha+1}.\
 (\aleph(2^{\aleph_{\alpha}})$ is Hartogs' aleph, the least $\aleph$ not $\leq 2^{\aleph_{\alpha}}$.) Mathias \cite{bib:1979} p 126.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 59($\leq$).} If $(A, \leq)$ is a partial ordering that is not a well ordering, then there is no set $B$ such that $(B, \leq)$ (the usual injective cardinal ordering on $B$) is isomorphic to $(A, \leq)$. Mathias \cite{bib:1979} p 120.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 60.} $C(\infty, WO)$: Every set of non-empty, well orderable sets has a choice function. Jech\index{Author}{Jech} \cite{bib:1973b}, G. Moore\index{Author}{G. Moore} \cite{bib:1982} p 125.

[\textbf{60 A}] $(\forall\alpha)C(\infty, \aleph_{\alpha})$: For every ordinal $\alpha$, every family of sets each with power $\aleph_{\alpha}$ has a choice function.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 61.} $(\forall n\in\omega, n\geq 2)(C(\infty, n))$: For each $n\in\omega, n\geq 2$, every set of $n$ element sets has a choice function. Levy\index{Author}{Levy} \cite{bib:1962}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 62.}\index{Author}{Royden} $C(\infty, <\aleph_{0})$: Every set of non-empty finite sets has a choice function.

[\textbf{62 A}] (Depends on the two primes $p_{1}\neq p_{2}$) Form $308(p_{1})\
+$ form $308(p_{2})$. Howard/Yorke\index{Author}{Howard/Yorke} \cite{bib:1987}.

\noindent[\textbf{62 B}] (Depends on the prime $p_{1}$) Form $45(p_{1})\
+$ form $308(p_{1})$. Howard/Yorke \cite{bib:1987}.

\noindent[\textbf{62 C}] For every prime $p$, if $\{G_{y}:y\in Y\}$ is a set of finite groups, then the weak direct product $\prod_{y\in Y}G_{y}$ has a maximal $p$-subgroup. Howard/Yorke \cite{bib:1987} and note 24.

\noindent[\textbf{62 D}] For every prime $p$, if $Y$ is a set of non-empty, finite sets, then the weak direct product $\prod_{y\in Y}S_{y}$ has a maximal $p$-subgroup. $(S_{y}$ is the symmetric group on $y.)$ Howard/Yorke \cite{bib:1987} and note 24.

\noindent [\textbf{62 E}] $KW(\infty, <\aleph_{0})$, The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for families of finite sets: For every set $M$ of finite sets there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in M$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$. Note 70.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 63.} $SPI$: Weak ultrafilter principle: Every infinite set has a non-trivial ultrafilter. Jech\index{Author}{Jech} \cite{bib:1973b} p 172 prob 8.5.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 64.} $E(I, Ia)$ (Howard/Yorke \cite{bib:1989}): There are no amorphous sets. Note 94 and Levy \cite{bib:1958}, notes 57 and 94.

[\textbf{64 A}] An amorphous power of a compact $T_{2}$ space is compact. Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1984b}.

\noindent[\textbf{64 B}] Finite products of metric $C$ spaces are $C$. (A space is $C$ if each open covering has an amorphous refinement.) Brunner \cite{bib:1984b}.

\noindent[\textbf{64 C}] $C$ spaces are compact. (A space is $a\ C$ \emph{space}
if each open covering has an amorphous refinement.) Brunner \cite{bib:1984b}.

\noindent[\textbf{64 D}] Metric $C$ spaces are limited amorphous. (A space is $C$ if every open covering has an amorphous refinement. A space is \emph{limited amorphous} if each amorphous subset is relatively compact.) Brunner \cite{bib:1984b}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 65.} The Krein-Milman Theorem:\index{Subject}{Krein-Milman theorem} Let $K$ be a compact convex set in a locally convex topological vector space $X$. Then $K$ has an extreme point. (An extreme point is a point which is not an interior point of any line segment which lies in $K$.) Royden \cite{bib:1963} and H. Rubin/J. Rubin\index{Author}{H. Rubin/J. Rubin} \cite{bib:1985}, p. 177.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 66.} Every vector space over a field has a basis. Hamel\index{Author}{Hamel} \cite{bib:1905}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 67.} $MC(\infty, \infty)$ (MC), The Axiom of Multiple Choice: For every set $M$ of non-empty sets there is a function $f$ such that $(\forall x\in M)(\emptyset\neq f(x)\subseteq x$ and $f(x)$ is finite).

[\textbf{67 A}] $A(A2, H2)$: For every $T_{2}$ topological space $(X, T)$ if $(X, T)$ is A2, then $(X, T)$ is hereditarily $A2$. $((X, T)$ is A2 means if $U\subseteq T$ covers $X$ then $\exists f:X\rightarrow T$ such that for all $x\in X,\,x\in f(x)$ and $f$'' $X$ refines $U$.) Brunner \cite{bib:1983d} and note 26.

\noindent[\textbf{67 B}] $MW$: Each set can be covered by a well ordered family of finite sets. Levy \cite{bib:1962}.

\noindent[\textbf{67 C}] $A(P)$: (Depends on $P\in\{D1, B2, B3, H2, A2\}.)$ Every $T_{2}$ topological space has property $P$. Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1983d} and note 26.

\noindent[\textbf{67 D}] For every Abelian group $A$, every torsion free divisible subgroup of $A$ is a direct summand of $A$. Armbrust\index{Author}{Armbrust} \cite{bib:1972} and note 24.

\noindent[\textbf{67 E}] For any algebra \textbf{A} with finitary operations (that is, \textbf{A} is of type $\tau$ where $\tau =(K_{i})_{i\in I}$ with $K_{i}$ finite for each $i\in I$) and for any generating subset $Z$ of \textbf{A}, there is a function $h:A\rightarrow \mathcal{P}_{\omega}(Z)$ ($A$ is the domain of \textbf{A} and $\mathcal{P}_{\omega}(Z)$ is the set of all finite subsets of $Z$.) such that $\forall a\in A,\ a$ is in the subalgebra of \textbf{A} generated by $h(a)$. Diener\index{Author}{Diener} \cite{bib:1989} and note 115.

\noindent[\textbf{67 F}] For any algebra \textbf{A} with one unary operation $f$ and any generating set $Z$ of \textbf{A}, there is a function $h:A\rightarrow \mathcal{P}_{\omega}(Z)$ ($A$ is the domain of \textbf{A} and $\mathcal{P}_{\omega}(Z)$ is the set of all finite subsets of $Z$.) such that $\forall a\in A,\,a$ is in the subalgebra of \textbf{A} generated by $h(a)$. Diener \cite{bib:1989} and note 115.

\noindent[\textbf{67 G}] For every $T_{1}$ topological space $(X, T)$ and every cellular family $\mathcal{O}= \{O_{i}:i\in k\}\subseteq T-\{\emptyset\}$, there is a closed discrete set $\mathcal{I}$ such that for every $i\in k,\, \mathcal{I}\cap O_{i}\neq\emptyset$. Keremedis\index{Author}{Keremedis} \cite{bib:1996b} and note 77.

\noindent[\textbf{67 H}] Let $(X, T)$ be a $T_{4}$ topological space and let $\{G_{i}:i\in K\}$ be a locally finite family of pairwise disjoint, non-empty, open subsets of $X$. Then there exists a continuous real valued function $f:X\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that for each $i\in K,\,f$ vanishes on the boundary of $G_{i}$ and $f(x_{i})=1$ for some $x_{i}\in G_{i}$. Keremedis
\cite{bib:1995} and note 43.

\noindent[\textbf{67 I}] If $(X, T)$ is a $T_{4}$ topological space and $U=\{U_{i}:i\in K\}$ is a family of non-empty open sets, then there is a family $F=\{f_{i}:i\in K\}$ of non-negative, non-constant, continuous real valued functions on $X$ such that each $f_{i}$ vanishes on $X-U_{i}$. Keremedis \cite{bib:1995}.

\noindent[\textbf{67 J}] If $(X, T)$ is a $T_{4}$ topological space and $U=\{U_{i}:i\in K\}$ is a family of non-empty open sets, then there is a family $V=\{V_{i}:i\in K\}$ of non-empty closed (compact) sets such that $U_{i}\supseteq V_{i}$ for each $i\in K$. Keremedis \cite{bib:1995}.

\noindent[\textbf{67 K}] DUN: The disjoint union of normal topological spaces is normal. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin\index{Author}{Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin} \cite{bib:1997a} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{67 L}] DUU: If $C$ is a collection of pairwise disjoint topological spaces each of which satisfies Urysohn's lemma, then the disjoint union of the spaces in $C$ satisfies Urysohn's lemma. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin \cite{bib:1997a} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{67 M}] DUT: If $C$ is a collection of pairwise disjoint topological spaces each of which satisfies the Tietze-Urysohn extension theorem, then the disjoint union of the spaces in $C$ satisfies the Tietze-Urysohn extension theorem.
Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin \cite{bib:1997a} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{67 N}] DUP: The disjoint union of paracompact spaces is paracompact. Howard/ Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin \cite{bib:1997b} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{67 O}] DUMET: The disjoint union of metacompact spaces is metacompact. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin \cite{bib:1997b} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{67 P}] DUPFCS: The disjoint union of PFCS spaces is PFCS. ($X$ is a \emph{PFCS space} iff every point finite open cover of $X$ is shrinkable.) Howard/Keremedis/ Rubin/Rubin \cite{bib:1997b} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{67 Q}] DUPN: The disjoint union of paracompact spaces is normal. Howard/ Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin\index{Author}{Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin} \cite{bib:1997b} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{67 R}] DUcw$H$: The disjoint union of cwH spaces is cwH. Howard/Keremedis/ Rubin/Rubin \cite{bib:1997b} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{67 S}] DUcwN: The disjoint union of cwN spaces is cwN. Howard/Keremedis/ Rubin/Rubin \cite{bib:1997b} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{67 T}] DUcwNN: The disjoint union of cwN spaces is normal. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin \cite{bib:1997b} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{67 U}] Every open cover $\mathcal{U}$ of a metric space ($X,\,d$) can be written as a well ordered union $\bigcup\{U_{\alpha}:\alpha\in\gamma\}$ where $\gamma$ is an ordinal and each $U_{\alpha}$ is locally finite. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley\index{Author}{Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley} \cite{bib:1997} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{67 V}] Every open cover $\mathcal{U}$ of a metric space ($X,\,d$) can be written as a well ordered union $\bigcup\{U_{\alpha}:\alpha\in\gamma\}$ where $\gamma$ is an ordinal and each $U_{\alpha}$ is point finite. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley \cite{bib:1997} and note 141.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 68.} Nielsen-Schreier Theorem:\index{Subject}{Nielsen-Schreier theorem} Every subgroup of a free group is free. Jech\index{Author}{Jech} \cite{bib:1973b} p 12.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 69.} Every field has an algebraic closure. Jech \cite{bib:1973b}
p 13.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 70.} There is a non-trivial ultrafilter on $\omega$. Jech \cite{bib:1973b} prob 5.24.

[\textbf{70 A}] Every Dedekind infinite set has a non-principal ultrafilter.

\noindent[\textbf{70 B}] Weak Universal Net Theorem: There is a universal net in $\omega$ which is not eventually constant. Schechter\index{Author}{Schechter} \cite{bib:1996a} and note 31.

\noindent[\textbf{70 C}] There is a 2-valued measure on $\mathcal{P}(\omega)$. Pincus\index{Author}{Pincus} \cite{bib:1972c} and note 147.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 71($\alpha$).} $W_{\aleph_{\alpha}}:(\forall x)(|x|\leq\aleph_{\alpha}$ or $|x|\geq\aleph_{\alpha})$. Pelc\index{Author}{Pelc} \cite{bib:1978}, Jech \cite{bib:1973b}, page 119 and Levy\index{Author}{Levy} \cite{bib:1964}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 72.} Artin-Schreier Theorem:\index{Subject}{Artin-Schreier theorem} Every field in which $-1$ is not the sum of squares can be ordered. (The ordering, $\leq$, must satisfy (a) $a\leq b\rightarrow a+c\leq b+c$ for all $c$ and (b) $c\geq 0$ and $a\leq b\rightarrow a\cdot c\leq b\cdot c.\rangle$ Tarski\index{Author}{Tarski} \cite{bib:1954b}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 73.} For every $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ and $x\in \mathbb{R}$ the following definitions are equivalent:

(1) $x$ is in the closure of $A$ iff every neighborhood of $x$ intersects $A$.

\noindent(2) $x$ is in the closure of $A$ iff there is a sequence $\{x_{n}\}\subseteq A$ such that $\displaystyle \lim x_{n}=x$. Jech \cite{bib:1973b} p 21.

\noindent[\textbf{73 A}] For all $A\subseteq \mathbb{R},\,x\in A$ and $f: A\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ the following are equivalent:

\noindent(1) $(\forall\epsilon>0)(\exists\delta>0)(\forall y\in A)(|y-x|<\delta$ implies $|f(y)-f(x)|<\epsilon)$

\noindent(2) Whenever $\{x_{n}\}\subseteq A$ and $\lim x_{n}=x$ then $\lim f(x_{n})=f(x)$. Notes 4, 5 and 6.

\noindent[\textbf{73 B}] $(\forall f:\mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R})(\forall x\in \mathbb{R})$ the following are equivalent:

\noindent(1) $(\forall\epsilon>0)(\exists\delta>0)((\forall y\in \mathbb{R})(|y-x|<\delta\rightarrow|f(y)-f(x)|<\epsilon)$

\noindent(2) Whenever $\displaystyle \lim x_{n}=x$, then $\lim f(x_{n})=f(x)$.
Note 10.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 74.} For every $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ the following are equivalent:

(1) A is closed and bounded.

\noindent(2) Every sequence $\{x_{n}\}\subseteq A$ has a convergent subsequence with limit in A. Jech \cite{bib:1973b} p 21.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 75.} Every subspace of a separable metric space is separable. Jech\index{Author}{Jech} \cite{bib:1973b} p 21.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 76.}\index{Author}{Sierpi\'{n}ski} $MC_{\omega}(\infty, \infty) (\omega\text{-}\mathrm{MC}$): For every family $X$ of pairwise disjoint nonempty sets, there is a function $f$ such that for each $x\in X,\, \mathrm{f(x)}$ is a non-empty countable subset of $x$. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin\index{Author}{Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin} \cite{bib:1997b}.

[\textbf{76 A}] Every open cover $\mathcal{U}$ of a metric space can be written as a well ordered union $\bigcup\{U_{\alpha}:\alpha\in\gamma\}$ where $\gamma$ is an ordinal and each $U_{\alpha}$ is locally countable. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley\index{Author}{Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley} \cite{bib:1997} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{76 B}] Every open cover $\mathcal{U}$ of a metric space can be written as a well ordered union $\bigcup\{U_{\alpha}:\alpha\in\gamma\}$ where $\gamma$ is an ordinal and each $U_{\alpha}$ is point countable. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley \cite{bib:1997} and note 141.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 77.} A linear ordering of a set $P$ is a well ordering if and only if $P$ has no infinite descending sequences. Jech \cite{bib:1973b} p 23.

[\textbf{77 A}] If a linearly ordered set $(X, \leq)$ has no greatest element then it has a subset of order type $\omega$. Sierpi\'{n}ski \cite{bib:1918}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 78.} Urysohn's Lemma:\index{Subject}{Urysohn's lemma} If $A$ and $B$ are disjoint closed sets in a normal space $S$, then there is a continuous $f:S\rightarrow[0, 1]$ which is 1 everywhere in $A$ and $0$ everywhere in $B$. Urysohn\index{Author}{Urysohn} \cite{bib:1925} pp 290-292.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 79.} $\mathbb{R}$ can be well ordered. Hilbert\index{Author}{Hilbert} \cite{bib:1900} p 263.

[\textbf{79 A}] $C(\infty, \infty, \mathbb{R})$: Every set whose elements are non-empty subsets of $\mathbb{R}$ has a choice function. Schechter\index{Author}{Schechter} \cite{bib:1996a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 80.} $C(\aleph_{0},2)$: Every denumerable set of pairs has a choice function. Mostowski\index{Author}{Mostowski} \cite{bib:1948}.

[\textbf{80 A}] $UT(\aleph_{0},2, \aleph_{0})$: The union of denumerably many pairs is denumerable.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 81($n$).} (For $n\in \omega\ K(n)$: For every set $S$ there is an ordinal $\alpha$ and a one to one function $f:S\rightarrow \mathcal{P}^{n}(\alpha)$. $(\mathcal{P}^{0}(X)=X$ and $\mathcal{P}^{n+1}(X)=\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{P}^{n}(X))$. $(K(0)$ is equivalent to form 1 (AC) and $K(1)$ is equivalent to the selection principle (form 15)). Monro\index{Author}{Monro} \cite{bib:1972}, \cite{bib:1973b} and note 90.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 82.} $E(I, III)$ (Howard/Yorke\index{Author}{Howard/Yorke} \cite{bib:1989}): If $X$ is infinite then $\mathcal{P}(X)$ is Dedekind infinite. ($X$ is finite $\Leftrightarrow \mathcal{P}(X)$ is Dedekind finite.) Levy\index{Author}{Levy} \cite{bib:1958} and note 94.

[\textbf{82 A}]. Every infinite set can be mapped onto $\omega$. Howard/Yorke \cite{bib:1989}, Monro \cite{bib:1972}.

\noindent[\textbf{82 B}] $E(Ia, III)$: For every set $X$, if $\mathcal{P}(X)$ is Dedekind finite then $X$ is amorphous. Howard/Yorke \cite{bib:1989}, notes 57 and 94.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 83.} $E(I, II)$ (Howard/Yorke \cite{bib:1989}): $T$-finite is equivalent to finite. Tarski\index{Author}{Tarski} \cite{bib:1924} and note 94.

[\textbf{83 A}] $E(Ia, II)$: Every $T$-finite set is amorphous. Howard/Yorke \cite{bib:1989}, notes 57 and 94.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 84.} $E(II, III)$ (Howard/Yorke \cite{bib:1989}): $(\forall x)(x$ is $T$-finite if and only if $\mathcal{P}(x)$ is Dedekind finite). Howard/Yorke \cite{bib:1989} and note 94.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 85.} $C(\infty, \aleph_{0})$: Every family of denumerable sets has a choice function. Jech \cite{bib:1973b} p 115 prob 7.13.

[\textbf{85 A}] $C(\infty, \leq\aleph_{0})$: Every family of non-empty countable sets has a choice function.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 86($\alpha$).} $C(\aleph_{\alpha}, \infty)$: If $X$ is a set of non-empty sets such that $|X|=\aleph_{\alpha}$, then $X$ has a choice function. Levy\index{Author}{Levy} \cite{bib:1964}.

[\textbf{86 A($\alpha$)}] If $(P, \leq)$ is a tree of height $\lambda\leq\aleph_{\alpha}$ which has fewer than $\lambda$ branches of height $<\lambda$ then one of the following holds for the upside down tree $(P, \geq)$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] There is a cardinal $\mu<\lambda$ such that $(P, \geq)$ does not contain a strong antichain of cardinality $\mu$.
\item[(b)] $(P, \geq)$ contains a strong antichain of cardinality $\lambda$.
\item[(c)] $(P, \geq)$ contains a chain of cardinality $\lambda$.
\end{enumerate}
Shannon\index{Author}{Shannon} \cite{bib:1992} and note 119.

[\textbf{86 B($\alpha$)}] The frame envelope of any $\aleph_{\alpha}$ frame is $\aleph_{\alpha}$-Lindel\"{o}f. Banaschewski\index{Author}{Banaschewski} \cite{bib:1997} and note 29.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 87($\alpha$).} $DC(\aleph_{\alpha})$: Given a relation $R$ such that for every subset $Y$ of a set $X$ with $|Y|<\aleph_{\alpha}$, there is an $x\in X$ with $Y\,R\,x$ then there is a function $f:\aleph_{\alpha}\rightarrow X$ such that $(\forall\beta<\aleph_{\alpha})\ \{f(\gamma):\gamma<\beta\}\,R\,f(\beta)$. Levy \cite{bib:1964}.

[\textbf{87 A($\alpha$)}] $Z_{\aleph_{\alpha}}$: Let $P$ be a partially ordered set in which every well ordered chain has type $<\aleph_{\alpha}$. If every well ordered chain in $P$ has an upper bound in $P$, then $P$ contains a maximal element. Wolk\index{Author}{Wolk} \cite{bib:1983}.

\noindent[\textbf{87 B($\alpha$)}] $Z_{\aleph_{\alpha}}^{\ast}$: Let $P$ be a well-founded partially ordered set (that is, every chain in $P$ is well ordered.) in which every chain has type $<\aleph_{\alpha}$. If every chain in $P$ has an upper bound in $P$, then $P$ contains a maximal element. Wolk \cite{bib:1983}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 88.} $C(\infty, 2)$: Every family of pairs has a choice function.

[\textbf{88 A}] $P(2,2)$: If $X$ is a set and $P$ is a property of subsets of $X$ of 2 character (that is, $\forall y\subseteq X(P(y)$ iff $\forall z\subseteq y(|z|\leq 2\rightarrow P(z))$)) then if every finite subset of $X$ can be partitioned into two or fewer $P$-sets (that is, sets $z$ such that $P(z)$) then $X$ can be partitioned into two or fewer $P$-sets. Cowen\index{Author}{Cowen} \cite{bib:1982}.

\noindent[\textbf{88 B}] $G_{2}$: A graph is 2-colorable if every finite subgraph is 2-colorable. Mycielski\index{Author}{Mycielski} \cite{bib:1961} and note 117.

\noindent[\textbf{88 C}] If $m$ is a cardinal number and $\mathcal{L}$ is a lattice isomorphic to the lattice of subalgebras of some unary universal algebra (a unary universal algebra is one with only unary or nullary operations) and $\alpha$ is an automorphism of $\mathcal{L}$ of order 2 (that is, $\alpha^{2}$ is the identity) then there is a unary algebra $\mathfrak{A}$ with $|$ domain $\mathfrak{A}|\geq m$ and an isomorphism $\rho$ from $\mathcal{L}$ onto the lattice of subalgebras of $\mathfrak{A}^{2}$ with $\rho(\alpha(x))=(\rho(x))^{-1}(=\{(s, t):(t, s)\in\rho(x)\})$ for all $x\in \mathcal{L}$. Lampe \cite{bib:1974}.

\noindent[\textbf{88 D}] For any cardinal $m$, there is a unary algebra $\mathfrak{A}=\langle A,\, F\rangle$ (only unary and nullary operations) and a proper subalgebra $\mathfrak{D}$ of $\mathfrak{A}^{2}$ such that $\mathfrak{A}^{2}$ has exactly four subalgebras, $\mathfrak{A},\,\emptyset,\,\mathfrak{D}$ and $\mathfrak{D}^{\ast}=\{(s, t):(t, s)\in \mathfrak{D}\}$. Lampe\index{Author}{Lampe} \cite{bib:1974}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 89.} Antichain Principle:\index{Subject}{antichain principle} Every partially ordered set has a maximal antichain. Jech\index{Author}{Jech} \cite{bib:1973b} p 133 and Kurepa\index{Author}{Kurepa} \cite{bib:1953}.

[\textbf{89 A}] If $\forall y\in X,\,y=\langle u,\, R\rangle$ where $R$ is a partial order on $u$ then there is a function $f$ on $X$ such that $\forall\langle u,\,R\rangle\in X,\,f(\langle u, R\rangle)$ is a maximal antichain in $u$. Felgner\index{Author}{Felgner} \cite{bib:1969} and Harper/Rubin\index{Author}{Harper/Rubin} \cite{bib:1976}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 90.} $LW$: Every linearly ordered set can be well ordered. Jech\index{Author}{Jech} \cite{bib:1973b} p 133 and Felgner/Jech\index{Author}{Felgner/Jech} \cite{bib:1973}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 91.}\index{Author}{Sierpi\'{n}ski} $PW$:\index{Subject}{antichain principle} The power set of a well ordered set can be well ordered. Jech \cite{bib:1973b} p 133 and H. Rubin/J. Rubin\index{Author}{H. Rubin/J. Rubin} \cite{bib:1985}.

[\textbf{91 A}] $A(S, W1)$: For every $T_{2}$ topological space ($X,\, T)$ if $X$ has a dense well ordered subset, then $T$ is well ordered. (Clear) Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1983d} and note 26.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 92.} Every subset of $\mathbb{R}$ is separable. Jech \cite{bib:1973b} p 142.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 93.} There is a non-measurable subset of $\mathbb{R}$. Sierpi\'{n}ski \cite{bib:1918}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 94.} $C(\aleph_{0}, \infty, \mathbb{R})$: Every denumerable family of non-empty sets of reals has a choice function. Jech \cite{bib:1973b} p 148 prob 10.1.

[\textbf{94 A}] The discrete topology on $\omega$ is Lindel\"{o}f. Brunner \cite{bib:1982d} and note 40.

\noindent[\textbf{94B}] There is a Lindel\"{o}f space with a closed, discrete infinite subset. Brunner \cite{bib:1982d} and note 40.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 95 ($F$).} Existence of Complementary Subspaces over a Field $F$: If $F$ is a field, then every vector space $V$ over $F$ has the property that if $S\subseteq V$ is a subspace of $V$, then there is a subspace $S^{\prime}\subseteq V$ such that $S\cap S^{\prime}=\{0\}$ and $S\cup S^{\prime}$ generates $V$. Bleicher\index{Author}{Bleicher} \cite{bib:1964}, \cite{bib:1965}, H. Rubin/J. Rubin \cite{bib:1985}, pp 119ff, and Jech \cite{bib:1973b}, p 148 prob 10.4.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 96.} L\"{o}wig's\index{Author}{L\"{o}wig} Theorem.\index{Subject}{L\"{o}wig's theorem} If $B_{1}$ and $B_{2}$ are both bases for the vector space $V$ then $|B_{1}|=|B_{2}|$. L\"{o}wig \cite{bib:1934}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 97.} Cardinal Representatives:\index{Subject}{cardinal representatives} For every set $A$ there is a function $c$ with domain $\mathcal{P}(A)$ such that for all $x,\,y\in \mathcal{P}(A)$, (i) $c(x)=c(y\rangle\leftrightarrow x\approx y$ and (ii) $c(x)\approx x$. Jech \cite{bib:1973b} p 154.

[\textbf{97 A}] For every set $\{X_{i}:i\in I\}$ of local cardinal numbers, there is a set $\{x_{i}:i\in I\}$ of sets such that for each $i\in I$ there exists a $y_{i}\in X_{i}$ such that $x_{i}\approx y_{i}$. ($X$ is a \emph{local cardinal number} if for all $x, y\in X, x\approx y$.) Higasikawa\index{Author}{Higasikawa} \cite{bib:1995}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 98.} The set of all finite subsets of a Dedekind finite set is Dedekind finite. Jech \cite{bib:1973b} p 161 prob 11.5 and note 94.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 99.} Rado's\index{Author}{Rado} Selection Lemma:\index{Subject}{Rado's selection lemma} Let $\{K(\lambda):\lambda\in\Lambda\}$ be a family of finite subsets (of $X$) and suppose for each finite $S\subseteq\Lambda$ there is a function $\gamma(S):S\rightarrow X$ such that $(\forall\lambda\in S)(\gamma(S)(\lambda)\in K(\lambda))$. Then there is an $f:\Lambda\rightarrow X$ such that for every finite $S\subseteq\Lambda$ there is a finite $T$ such that $S\subseteq T\subseteq\Lambda$ and such that $f$ and $\gamma(T)$ agree on S. Rado \cite{bib:1949}.

[\textbf{99 A}] Weak Rado Lemma: Let $\Lambda$ be a set. Suppose that $\gamma$ is a function with domain all finite subsets of $\Lambda$ such that for each finite $S\subseteq\Lambda,\,\gamma(S):S\rightarrow\{0,1\}$. Then there is a $\phi$ defined on $\Lambda$ with the property that for every finite $S\subseteq\Lambda$ there is a finite $T\subseteq\Lambda$ such that $S\subseteq T$ and $\gamma(T)$ and $\phi$ agree on $S$. Schechter\index{Author}{Schechter}
\cite{bib:1996a} and Howard\index{Author}{Howard} \cite{bib:1993}.

\noindent[\textbf{99 B}] Rado's Lemma restricted to families of two element sets: Let $\{k(\lambda):\lambda\in \Lambda\}$ be a family of 2 element subsets of a set $X$ and suppose that for each finite $S\subseteq\Lambda$, there is a function $\gamma(S)$ from $S$ into $X$ such that $(\forall\lambda\in S)(\gamma(S)(\lambda)\in k(\lambda))$. Then there is a function from $\Lambda$ into $X$ such that for every finite $S\subseteq\Lambda$, there is a finite $T$ with $S\subseteq T\subseteq\Lambda$ such that $f$ and $\gamma(T)$ agree on $S$. Rav\index{Author}{Rav} \cite{bib:1977} and Howard\index{Author}{Howard} \cite{bib:1993}.

\noindent[\textbf{99 C}]\index{Subject}{Rado's selection lemma}\index{Author}{Sierpi\'{n}ski} Strong Rado Lemma 2: Let $T$ be a family of finite sets and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a collection of finite subsets of $T$ satisfying

\noindent(1) $(\forall K\in T)(\exists S\in \mathcal{F})(K\in S)$

\noindent(2) $(\forall S_{1}, S_{2}\in \mathcal{F})(S_{1}\cup S_{2}\in \mathcal{F})$

\noindent Assume there is a function $\phi$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ such that for each $S\in \mathcal{F},\,\phi(S)= \phi_{S}$ is a function with domain $S$ and satisfies $(\forall K\in S)(\phi_{S}(K)\in K)$. Then there is a function $f$ with domain $T$ and with the following property: For all $S\in \mathcal{F}$ there is an $S^{\prime}\in \mathcal{F}$ such that $S\subseteq S^{\prime}$ and $f$ and $\phi_{S^{\prime}}$ agree on $S$. Howard \cite{bib:1993}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 100.} Weak Partition Principle:\index{Subject}{partition principle} For all sets $x$ and $y$, if $x\precsim^{\ast}y$, then it is not the case that $y\prec x$. Lindenbaum/Tarski\index{Author}{Lindenbaum/Tarski} \cite{bib:1926} and note 69.

[\textbf{100 A}] For every set $A$ and function $f$ it is false that $A\prec f^{\prime\prime}A$. G. Moore\index{Author}{G. Moore} \cite{bib:1982}, p. 327.

\noindent[\textbf{100 B}] For all sets $x$ and $y$, if $x\precsim^{\ast}y$ and $y\precsim x$, then $x\approx y$. Higasikawa\index{Author}{Higasikawa} \cite{bib:1995} and note 69.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 101.} Partition Principle: If $S$ is a partition of $M$, then $S\precsim M$. Sierpi\'{n}ski \cite{bib:1947}.

[\textbf{101 A}] For all sets $x$ and $y,\,x\precsim^{\ast}y$ implies $x\precsim y$. Lindenbaum/Tarski \cite{bib:1926} and note 69.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 102.} For all Dedekind finite cardinals $p$ and $q$, if $p^{2}=q^{2}$ then $p=q$. Jech\index{Author}{Jech} \cite{bib:1973b} p 162 prob 11.12 and note 94.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 103.} If $(P, <)$ is a linear ordering and $|P|>\aleph_{1}$ then some initial segment of $P$ is uncountable. Jech \cite{bib:1973b} p 164 prob 11.21.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 104.} There is a regular uncountable aleph. Jech \cite{bib:1966b} p 165 prob 11.26.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 105.} There is a partially ordered set $(A, \leq)$ such that for no set $B$ is $(B, \leq)$ (the ordering on $B$ is the usual injective cardinal ordering) isomorphic to $(A, \leq)$. Forti/Honsell\index{Author}{Forti/Honsell} \cite{bib:1985} and Jech \cite{bib:1966c}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 106.} Baire Category Theorem for Compact Hausdorff Spaces: Every compact Hausdorff space is Baire. Goldblatt\index{Author}{Goldblatt} \cite{bib:1985}, G. Moore \cite{bib:1982}, and note 28.

[\textbf{106 A}] $DMC$: Dependent Multiple Choice: Every tree in which every element has at least one immediate successor has a subtree whose levels are finite and in which every element has at least one immediate successor. Blass\index{Author}{Blass} \cite{bib:1979}, Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1983c}, Fossy/Morillon\index{Author}{Fossy/Morillon} \cite{bib:1995} and note 21.

\noindent[\textbf{106 B}] Weak DC: If $R$ is a binary relation on a non-empty set $E$ such that $(\forall x\in E)(\exists y\in E)(x\,R\,y)$, then there is a sequence $\langle F_{n}\rangle_{n\in\omega}$ of non-empty finite subsets of $E$ such that $(\forall n\in \omega)(\forall x\in F_{n})(\exists y\in F_{n+1})(x\,R\,y)$. (This statement remains equivalent to form 106 if we replace ``binary relation'' by ``transitive binary relation''.) Fossy/Morillon \cite{bib:1995}.

\noindent[\textbf{106 C}] Every scattered compact space is a Baire space. Fossy/Morillon \cite{bib:1995} and note 28.

\noindent[\textbf{106 D}] For every compact $\mathrm{T}_{2}$ space $(X, T)$ and every family $D=\{D_{i}:i\in \omega\}$ of dense open sets of $X$ there is a regular filter base $\mathcal{F}\subseteq T$ (that is, if $F,\,G\in \mathcal{F}$, then there exists $Q\in \mathcal{F}$ such that $\overline{Q}\subseteq F\cap G$) such that for all $i\in\omega$, for all but finitely many $F\in \mathcal{F},\,\overline{F}\subset D_{i}$. Fossy/Morillon\index{Author}{Fossy/Morillon} \cite{bib:1995}

\noindent\textbf{FORM 107.} M. Hall's\index{Author}{Hall} Theorem:\index{Subject}{Hall's theorem} Let $\{S(\alpha):\alpha\in A\}$ be a collection of finite subsets (of a set $X$) then if
\begin{equation*}
\tag{$\ast$} \text{for each finite}\ F\subseteq A\ \text{there is an injective choice function on}\ F
\end{equation*}

\noindent then there is an injective choice function on $A$. (That is, a 1-1 function $f$ such that $(\forall\alpha\in A)(f(\alpha)\in S(\alpha)).)$ (According to a theorem of P. Hall $(\ast)$ is equivalent to $|\bigcup_{\alpha\in F}S(\alpha)|\geq|F|$. P. Hall's theorem does not require the axiom of choice.) M. Hall \cite{bib:1948}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 108.} There is an ordinal $\alpha$ such that $2^{\aleph_{\alpha}}$ is not the union of a denumerable set of denumerable sets. Gitik\index{Author}{Gitik} \cite{bib:1985}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 109.} Every field $F$ and every vector space $V$ over $F$ has the property that each linearly independent set $A\subseteq V$ can be extended to a basis. Bleicher\index{Author}{Bleicher} \cite{bib:1964}, \cite{bib:1965}, Blass\index{Author}{Blass} \cite{bib:1984a}, H. Rubin/J. Rubin\index{Author}{H. Rubin/J. Rubin} \cite{bib:1985}, pp 119 ff.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 110.} Every vector space over $\mathbb{Q}$ has a basis. Blass \cite{bib:1984a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 111.} $UT(WO, 2, WO)$: The union of an infinite well ordered set of 2-element sets is an infinite well ordered set.

[\textbf{111 A}] $C(WO, 2)$: Every well ordered family of 2-element sets has a choice function.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 112.} $MC(\infty, LO)$: For every family $X$ of non-empty sets each of which can be linearly ordered there is a function $f$ such that for all $y\in X,\,f(y)$ is a non-empty finite subset of $y$. Howard/Rubin\index{Author}{Howard/Rubin} \cite{bib:1977}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 113.} Tychonoff's\index{Subject}{Tychonoff's theorem} Compactness Theorem for Countably Many Spaces: The product of a countable set of compact spaces is compact. Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1985a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 114.} Every A-bounded $T_{2}$ topological space is weakly Loeb. ($A$-\emph{bounded} means amorphous subsets are relatively compact. \emph{Weakly Loeb} means the set of non-empty closed subsets has a multiple choice function.) Brunner \cite{bib:1985a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 115.} The product of weakly Loeb $T_{2}$ spaces is weakly Loeb. (See form 114 for the definition of weakly Loeb.) Brunner \cite{bib:1985a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 116.} Every compact $T_{2}$ space is weakly Loeb. (See form 114 for the definition of weakly Loeb.) Brunner \cite{bib:1985a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 117.} If $\kappa$ is a measurable cardinal, then $\kappa$ is the $\kappa$th inaccessible cardinal. Keisler/Tarski\index{Author}{Keisler/Tarski} \cite{bib:1964} and note 20.

\noindent \textbf{FORM 118.} Every linearly orderable topological space is normal. Birkhoff\index{Author}{Birkhoff} \cite{bib:1967} p 241.
