[\textbf{118 A}] For each complete linear order, the set of non-empty convex subsets has a choice function. van Douwen\index{Author}{Douwen} \cite{bib:1985}.

\noindent[\textbf{118 B}] For each complete linear order, each pairwise disjoint collection of non-empty, convex, open subsets has a choice function. van Douwen \cite{bib:1985}.

\noindent[\textbf{118 C}] Every linearly orderable space is collectionwise normal. van Douwen\index{Author}{Douwen} \cite{bib:1985} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{118 D}] Every linearly orderable space is collectionwise Hausdorff. van Douwen \cite{bib:1985} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{118 E}] Every linearly orderable space satisfies Urysohn's lemma, van Douwen \cite{bib:1985} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{118 F}] Every linearly orderable space satisfies the Tietze-Urysohn extension theorem, van Douwen \cite{bib:1985} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{118 G}] Each complete linear order admits an extreme choice, that is, if $(X, \leq)$ is a linear order then there is a choice function $f$ on the set of non-empty open interval of $X$ with the property that for all $(a, b, c)\in X^{3}$ with $a<b<c,\,f((a, c))\in\{f((a, b)), b, f((b, c))\}$. Morillon\index{Author}{Morillon} \cite{bib:1991a}.

\noindent[\textbf{118 H}] For each linear order $(X, \leq)$, there is an ordinal $\alpha$ and a strictly increasing injective map $j$ from $(X, \leq)$ to $\{0,1\}^{\alpha}$ with the lexicographic order. Morillon \cite{bib:1987}.

\noindent[\textbf{118 I}] Every linearly ordered set of linear orders, each of which is non-empty and conditionally complete, has a choice function. Morillon \cite{bib:1988}, van Douwen \cite{bib:1985}, and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{118 J}] If $(X, \leq)$ is a linear, complete order, then the order topology on $X$ is hereditarily normal. Morillon \cite{bib:1988}, van Douwen \cite{bib:1985}, and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{118 K}] If $(X, \leq)$ is a linear order, then the order topology on $X$ is highly separated. Morillon \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{118 L}] If $X$ is a linear, complete order, then the order topology on $X$ is highly separated. Morillon \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{118 M}] If $(X, \leq)$ is a linear order, then the family $\{A(a, b):a, b\in X\wedge a<b\}$ has a choice function. $(A(a, b)$ denotes the set of continuous, order preserving functions from $X$ into $[0,1]$ such that $f(a)=0$ and $f(b)=1.)$ Morillon \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{118 N}] If $(X, \leq)$ is a linear order then the family $\{A^{\prime}(a, b):a, b\in X\wedge a<b\}$ has a choice function. $(A^{\prime}(a, b)$ denotes the set of continuous functions from $X$ into $[0,1]$ such that $f(a)=0$ and $f(b)=1.)$ Morillon \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{118 O}] If $(X, \leq)$ is a linear order, then the order topology on $X$ is effectively normal. Morillon \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{118 P}] If $(X, \leq)$ is a complete linear order, then the order topology on $X$ is effectively normal. Morillon \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{118 Q}] If $(X, \leq)$ is a linear order, then the order topology on $X$ is hereditarily normal. Morillon \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{118 R}] If $(X, \leq)$ is a linear order, then the order topology on $X$ is monotonely normal. Morillon \cite{bib:1987} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{118 S}] If $(X, \leq)$ is a complete linear order then there is a choice function $\ast$ for the family of non-empty open intervals of $X$ such that if $a,\,b,\,c\in X$ and either $(a, b)\neq\emptyset$ or $(b, c)\neq\emptyset$ then $\ast((a, c))\in\{\ast((a, b)), \ast((b, c)), b, b^{+}\}$ (where $b^{+}$ is the successor of $b$ if it exists and $b$ otherwise). Morillon \cite{bib:1987} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{118 T}] Every complete linear order has an increasing choice function. Morillon \cite{bib:1987} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{118 U}] Every linearly ordered space is monotonically normal. (A space $(X, <)$ is \emph{monotonically normal} if there is an operator $V$ which assigns to each $x\in X$ and basic open neighborhood $U$ of $x$ a basic open neighborhood $V(x, U)$ of $x$ such that $V(x, U)\cap V(x^{\prime}, U^{\prime})\neq\emptyset$ implies $x\in U^{\prime}$ or $x^{\prime}\in U$.) Good/Tree\index{Author}{Good/Tree} \cite{bib:1995}.

\noindent [\textbf{118 V}]\index{Subject}{van Douwen's choice principle} If $(L, \leq)$ is a linear order and $G=\{[l_{i}, r_{i}]:i\in K\}$ is a locally finite family of closed intervals of $L$ whose interiors are non-empty and pairwise disjoint, then there exists a continuous real valued function $f:L\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that $|f^{-1}(0) \cap [l_{i}, r_{i}]|\geq 2$ and $|f^{-1}(1) \cap [l_{i}, r_{i}]|\geq 1$ for all $i\in K$. Keremedis\index{Author}{Keremedis} \cite{bib:1995} and note 43.

\noindent[\textbf{118 W}] If $(L, \leq)$ is a linear order and $G=\{[l_{i}, r_{i}]:i\in K\}$ is a locally finite family of closed intervals of $L$ whose interiors are non-empty and pairwise disjoint, then there exists a continuous real valued function $f:L\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that for each $i\in K,\,f(l_{i})=f(r_{i})=0$ and $f(x)>0$ for all $x\in(l_{i}, r_{i})$. Keremedis
\cite{bib:1995} and note 43.

\noindent[\textbf{118 X}] If $(L, \leq)$ is a complete linear order and $G=\{(l_{i}, r_{i}):i\in K\}$ is a family of open, non-empty, pairwise disjoint intervals of $L$, then there exists a set $\{f_{i}:i\in K\}$ of non constant continuous real valued functions on $L$ such that for each $i\in K,\,f_{i}$ vanishes outside of $(l_{i}, r_{i})$. Keremedis \cite{bib:1995}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 119.} $C(\aleph_{0}$, uniformly orderable with order type of the integers): Suppose $\{A_{i}:i\in\omega\}$ is a set and there is a function $f$ such that for each $i\in \omega,\,f(i)$ is an ordering of $A_{i}$ of type $\omega^{\ast}+\omega$ (the usual ordering of the integers), then $\{A_{i}:i\in \omega\}$ has a choice function. van Douwen\index{Author}{Douwen} \cite{bib:1985}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 120($K$).} If $K\subseteq\omega -\{0,1\},\, C(LO, K)$: Every linearly ordered set of non-empty sets each of whose cardinality is in $K$ has a choice function. Truss \cite{bib:1973a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 121.} $C(LO, <\aleph_{0})$: Every linearly ordered set of non-empty finite sets has a choice function. Truss\index{Author}{Truss} \cite{bib:1973a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 122.} $C(WO, <\aleph_{0})$:  Every well ordered set of non-empty finite sets has a choice function. Truss \cite{bib:1973a}.

[\textbf{122 A}] $UT(WO, <\aleph_{0}, WO)\ (U_{\aleph_{0}})$: The union of a well ordered set of finite sets is well orderable. Brunner/Howard\index{Author}{Brunner}\index{Author}{Brunner/Howard} \cite{bib:1992}. (See note 27 for more information on $UT(WO, \kappa, WO)$, $\kappa$ a well ordered cardinal. The proof that 122 implies [122 A] is similar to the proof given in Shannon\index{Author}{Shannon} \cite{bib:1988} p 569.)

\noindent\textbf{FORM 123.} $SPI^{\ast}$: Uniform weak ultrafilter principle: For each family $F$ of infinite sets $\exists f$ such that $\forall x\in F,\,f(x)$ is a non-principal ultrafilter on $x$. Halpern\index{Author}{Halpern} \cite{bib:1972}

[\textbf{123 A}] Form 70 + form 344. Morillon\index{Author}{Morillon} \cite{bib:1988}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 124.} Every operator on a Hilbert space with an amorphous base is the direct sum of a finite matrix and a scalar operator. (A set is amorphous if it is not the union of two disjoint infinite sets.) Brunner \cite{bib:1984a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 125.} There does not exist an infinite, compact connected $p$ space. (A $p$ \emph{space} is a $T_{2}$ space in which the intersection of any well orderable family of open sets is open.) Brunner \cite{bib:1984c}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 126.} $MC(\aleph_{0}, \infty)$, Countable axiom of multiple choice: For every denumerable set $X$ of non-empty sets there is a function $f$ such that for all $y\in X,\,f(y)$ is a non-empty finite subset of $y$. Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1984d} and Blass\index{Author}{Blass} \cite{bib:1979}.

[\textbf{126 A}] Every positive functional on a $B$-lattice is continuous. Brunner \cite{bib:1984d} and note 16.

\noindent[\textbf{126 B}] Form 131 + form 350. Keremedis\index{Author}{Keremedis} \cite{bib:1996d} and note 132.

\noindent[\textbf{126 C}] $FSCB$ + form 131. FSCB is ``Every separable first countable space $(X, T)$ has a denumerable $\pi$-base.'' Keremedis \cite{bib:1996d} and note 132.

\noindent[\textbf{126 D}] For every denumerable family $A$ of disjoint non-empty sets there is an infinite set $C\subset\bigcup A$ such that for every $a\in A,\, 0\leq|C\cap a|<\omega$. Keremedis \cite{bib:1996d} and note 132.

\noindent[\textbf{126 E}] If $(X, T)$ is a topological space, then for every family $D=\{D_{i}:i\in \omega\}$ of dense open sets of $X$, there is a countable dense set $S\subseteq X$ such that for all $i\in\omega$ and for all but finitely many $s\in S,\,s\in D_{i}$. Keremedis \cite{bib:1996d} and note 132.

\noindent[\textbf{126 F}] Every denumerable family of sets having the sfip also has a pseudointersection. Keremedis \cite{bib:1996d} and note 132.

\noindent[\textbf{126 G}] DUN$(w)$: The countable disjoint union of normal topological spaces is normal. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin\index{Author}{Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin} \cite{bib:1997a} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{126 H}] DUU$(w)$: If $C$ is a countable collection of pairwise disjoint topological spaces each of which satisfies Urysohn's lemma, then the disjoint union of the spaces in $C$ satisfies Urysohn's lemma. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin \cite{bib:1997a} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{126 I}] DUT$(\omega)$: If $C$ is a countable collection of pairwise disjoint topological spaces each of which satisfies the Tietze-Urysohn extension theorem, then the disjoint union of the spaces in $C$ satisfies the Tietze-Urysohn extension theorem. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin \cite{bib:1997a} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{126 J}] $F_{\sigma}$ subsets of paracompact spaces are paracompact. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin \cite{bib:1997b} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{126 K}] $F_{\sigma}$ subsets of metacompact spaces are metacompact. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin \cite{bib:1997b} and note 141.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 127.} An amorphous power of a compact $T_{2}$ space, which as a set is well orderable, is well orderable. Brunner \cite{bib:1984b}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 128.} Aczel's Realization Principle:\index{Subject}{Aczel's Realization Principle} On every infinite set there is a Hausdorff topology with an infinite set of non-isolated points. Brunner \cite{bib:1984f}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 129.} For every infinite set $A,\,A$ admits a partition into sets of order type $\omega^{\ast}+\omega$. (For every infinite $A$, there is a set $\{\langle C_{j}, <j\rangle:j\in J\}$ such that $\{C_{j}:j\in J\}$ is a partition of $A$ and for each $j\in J, <_{j}$ is an ordering of $C_{j}$ of type $\omega^{\ast}+\omega.)$ Brunner \cite{bib:1984f}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 130.} $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R})$ is well orderable. Brunner \cite{bib:1984f}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 131.} $MC_{\omega}(\aleph_{0}, \infty)$: For every denumerable family $X$ of pairwise disjoint non-empty sets, there is a function $f$ such that for each $x\in X,\,\mathrm{f(x)}$ is a non-empty countable subset of $x$. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin \cite{bib:1997b}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 132.} $PC(\infty<\aleph_{0}, \infty)$: Every infinite family of finite sets has an infinite subfamily with a choice function. Blass \cite{bib:1977a} and Kleinberg\index{Author}{Kleinberg} \cite{bib:1969}.

[\textbf{132 A}] Every set mapping $f:X\rightarrow[X]^{WO}$ (well orderable subsets of $X$) on a Dedekind finite, infinite set $X$ has an infinite free subset. Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1989}. notes 22 and 94.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 133.} Every set is either well orderable or has an infinite amorphous subset. Brunner \cite{bib:1982a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 134.} If $X$ is an infinite $T_{1}$ space and $X^{Y}$ is $T_{5}$, then $Y$ is countable. $(T_{5}$ is ``hereditarily $T_{4}$''.) A. H. Stone\index{Author}{A. H. Stone} \cite{bib:1948}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 135.} If $X$ is a $T_{2}$ space with at least two points and $X^{Y}$ is hereditarily metacompact then $Y$ is countable. (A space is \emph{metacompact} if every open cover has an open point finite refinement. If $B$ and $B^{\prime}$ are covers of a space $X$, then $B^{\prime}$ is a \emph{refinement} of $B$ if $(\forall x\in B^{\prime})(\exists y\in B)(x\subseteq y)$. $B$ is \emph{point finite} if $(\forall t\in X)$ there are only finitely many $x\in B$ such that $t\in x$.) van Douwen\index{Author}{Douwen} \cite{bib:1980}.

\textbf{FORM 136($k$).} Surjective Cardinal Cancellation (depends on $k\in \omega-\{0\})$: For all cardinals $x$ and $y,\,kx\leq^{\ast}ky$ implies $x\leq^{\ast}y$. Truss\index{Author}{Truss} \cite{bib:1984} and note 69.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 137($k$).} Suppose $k\in \omega-\{0\}$. If $f$ is a 1-1 map from $k\times X$ into $k\times Y$ then there are partitions $X=\bigcup_{i<k}X_{i}$ and $Y=\bigcup_{i<k}Y_{i}$ of $X$ and $Y$ such that $f$ maps $\bigcup_{i<k}(\{i\}\times X_{i})$ onto $\bigcup_{i<k}(\{i\}\times Y_{i})$. Truss \cite{bib:1984}.

[\textbf{137 A($k$)}] For all $X$ and $Y\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ form 137($k$) holds. Truss \cite{bib:1984}

\noindent \textbf{FORM 138($k$).} Suppose $k\in \omega$. If $f$ is a partial map from $k\times Y$ onto $k\times X$ (that is, the domain is a subset of $k\times Y$), then there are partitions $X=\bigcup_{i<k}X_{i}$ and $Y=\bigcup_{i<k}Y_{i}$ of $X$ and $Y$ such that $f$ maps $\bigcup_{i<k}(\{i\}\times Y_{i})$ onto $\bigcup_{i<k}(\{i\}\times X_{i})$. Truss \cite{bib:1984}.

[\textbf{138 A($k$)}] For all standard $X$ and $Y$, form $138(k)$ holds. Truss \cite{bib:1984}. This is equivalent to $138(k)$ in $\mathrm{ZF}^{0}$.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 139.} Using the discrete topology on 2, $2^{\mathcal{P}(\omega)}$ is compact. Truss \cite{bib:1984}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 140.} Let $\Omega$ be the set of all (undirected) infinite cycles of reals (Graphs whose vertices are real numbers, connected, no loops and each vertex adjacent to exactly two others). Then there is a function $f$ on $\Omega$ such that for all $s\in\Omega,\,f(s)$ is a direction along $s$. Truss \cite{bib:1984}.

[\textbf{140 A}] (Form 137 with $k=2$): If $f$ is a 1-1 map from $2\times X$ into $2\times Y$ then there are partitions $X=X_{0}\cup X_{1}$ and $Y=Y_{0}\cup Y_{1}$ of $X$ and $Y$ such that $f$ maps $(\{0\}\times X_{0})\cup(\{1\}\times X_{1})$ onto $(\{0\}\times Y_{0})\cup(\{1\}\times Y_{1})$. Truss \cite{bib:1984}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 141.} $[14\ \mathrm{P}(n)]$ with $n=2$: Let $\{A(i):i\in I\}$ be a collection of sets such that $\forall i\in I,\ |A(i)|\leq 2$ and suppose $R$ is a symmetric binary relation on $\bigcup_{i\in I}A(i)$ such that for all finite $W\subseteq I$ there is an $R$ consistent choice function for $\{A(i):i\in W\}$. Then there is an $R$ consistent choice function for $\{A(i):i\in I\}$. Cowen\index{Author}{Cowen} \cite{bib:1977b} and note 109.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 142.} $\neg PB$: There is a set of reals without the property of Baire. Jech\index{Author}{Jech} \cite{bib:1973b} p 7 and note 28.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 143.} $H(C, TR)$: If $(X, R)$ is a connected relation $(u\neq v\rightarrow u\ R\ v$ or $v\ R\ u)$ then $X$ contains a $\subseteq$-maximal transitive subset. Harper/Rubin\index{Author}{Harper/Rubin} \cite{bib:1976} and note 39.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 144.} Every set is almost well orderable. Keisler\index{Author}{Keisler} \cite{bib:1970} and note 25.

[\textbf{144 A}] Every $p$ space is discrete. (A $p$ \emph{space} is a $T_{2}$ space in which the intersection of any well orderable family of open sets is open). Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1984c}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 145.} Compact $P_{0}$-spaces are Dedekind finite. (A $P_{0}$-\emph{space} is a topological space in which the intersection of a countable collection of open sets is open.) Brunner \cite{bib:1984c} and note 94.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 146.} $A(F, A1)$: For every $T_{2}$ topological space $(X, T)$, if $X$ is a continuous finite to one image of an A1 space then $(X, T)$ is an A1 space. $((X, T)$ is A1 means if $U\subseteq T$ covers $X$ then $\exists f:X\rightarrow U$ such that $(\forall x\in X)(x\in f(x)).)$ Brunner \cite{bib:1983d} and note 26.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 147.} $A(D2)$: Every $T_{2}$ topological space $(X, T)$ can be covered by a well ordered family of discrete sets. Brunner \cite{bib:1983d} and note 26.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 148.} $A(W2, B1)$: For every $T_{2}$ topological space $(X, T)$, if $X$ is well ordered, then $X$ has a well ordered base. Brunner \cite{bib:1983d} and note 26.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 149.} $A(F)$: Every $T_{2}$ topological space is a continuous, finite to one image of an A1 space. Brunner \cite{bib:1983d} and note 26.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 150.} $PC(\infty, \aleph_{0}, \infty)$: Every infinite set of denumerable sets has an infinite subset with a choice function.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 151.} $UT(WO, \aleph_{0}, WO)\ (U_{\aleph_{1}})$: The union of a well ordered set of denumerable sets is well orderable. Brunner/Howard\index{Author}{Brunner/Howard} \cite{bib:1992}. (If $\kappa$ is a well ordered cardinal, see note 27 for $UT(WO, \kappa, WO).)$

\noindent\textbf{FORM 152.} $D_{\aleph_{0}}$: Every non-well-orderable set is the union of a pairwise disjoint, well orderable family of denumerable sets. Brunner/Howard \cite{bib:1992}. (See note 27 for $D_{\kappa},\,\kappa$ a well ordered cardinal.)

\noindent\textbf{FORM 153.} The closed unit ball of a Hilbert space is compact in the weak topology. Fossy/Morillon\index{Author}{Fossy/Morillon} \cite{bib:1995} and Rudin\index{Author}{Rudin} \cite{bib:1991}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 154.} Tychonoff's\index{Subject}{Tychonoff's theorem} Compactness Theorem for Countably Many $T_{2}$ Spaces: The product of countably many $T_{2}$ compact spaces is compact. Brunner \cite{bib:1983c}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 155.} $LC$: There are no non-trivial L\"{a}uchli continua. (A \emph{L\"{a}uchli continuum} is a strongly connected continuum. \emph{Continuum} $\equiv$ compact, connected, Hausdorff space; and \emph{strongly connected} $\equiv$ every continuous real valued function is constant.) Brunner \cite{bib:1983a} and L\"{a}uchli\index{Author}{L\"{a}uchli} \cite{bib:1962}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 156.} Theorem of Gelfand and Kolmogoroff: Two compact $T_{2}$ spaces are homeomorphic if their rings of real valued continuous functions are isomorphic. Brunner \cite{bib:1983a} and Gelfand/Kolmogoroff\index{Author}{Gelfand/Kolmogoroff} \cite{bib:1939}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 157.} Theorem of Goodner:\index{Subject}{Goodner's theorem} A compact $T_{2}$ space is extremally disconnected (the closure of every open set is open) if and only if each non-empty subset of $C(X)$ (set of continuous real valued functions on $X$) which is pointwise bounded has a supremum. Goodner\index{Author}{Goodner} \cite{bib:1950}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 158.} In every Hilbert space $H$, if the closed unit ball is sequentially compact, then $H$ has an orthonormal basis. Brunner \cite{bib:1983b}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 159.}\index{Author}{Sierpi\'{n}ski} The regular cardinals are cofinal in the class of ordinals. Blass\index{Author}{Blass} \cite{bib:1983b}.

[\textbf{159 A}]\index{Subject}{Gelfand-Kolmogoroff theorem} Every variety has an initial algebra. Blass \cite{bib:1983b} and note 32.

\noindent[\textbf{159 B}] For every variety $V$ and set $X,\,V$ has a free algebra on $X$. Blass \cite{bib:1983b} and note 32.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 160.} No Dedekind finite set can be mapped onto an aleph. (See [9 E].) Monro\index{Author}{Monro} \cite{bib:1975} and note 94.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 161.} Definability of cardinal addition in terms of $\leq$: There is a first order formula whose only non-logical symbol is $\leq$ (for cardinals) that defines cardinal addition. H\"{a}ussler\index{Author}{H\"{a}ussler} \cite{bib:1983}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 162.} Non-existence of infinite units: There is no infinite cardinal number $A$ such that $A+A>A$ and for all cardinals $x$ and $y,\,x+y=A\rightarrow x=A$ or $y=A$. H\"{a}ussler \cite{bib:1983}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 163.} Every non-well-orderable set has an infinite, Dedekind finite subset. Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1982a} and note 94.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 164.} Every non-well-orderable set has an infinite subset with a Dedekind finite power set. Brunner \cite{bib:1982a}, notes 42 and 94.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 165.} $C(WO, WO)$: Every well ordered family of non-empty, well orderable sets has a choice function.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 166.} $PC(\infty, 2, \infty)$: Every infinite family of pairs has an infinite subfamily with a choice function. Brunner \cite{bib:1982a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 167.} $PKW(\aleph_{0}, \geq 2, \infty)$, Partial Kinna-Wagner Principle: For every denumerable family $F$ such that for all $x\in F,\,|x|\geq 2$, there is an infinite subset $H\subseteq F$ and a function $f$ such that for all $x\in H,\,\emptyset \neq f(x)\subsetneq x$. Brunner \cite{bib:1982a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 168.} Dual Cantor-Bernstein\index{Author}{Bernstein} Theorem:\index{Subject}{Cantor-Bernstein theorem} $(\forall x)(\forall y)(|x|\leq^{\ast}|y|$ and $|y|\leq^{\ast}|x|$ implies $|x|=|y|)$. Banaschewski/Moore\index{Author}{Banaschewski/Moore} \cite{bib:1990} and note 69.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 169.} There is an uncountable subset of $\mathbb{R}$ without a perfect subset. Banaschewski/Moore \cite{bib:1990}, Bernstein \cite{bib:1908}, and note 28.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 170.} $\aleph_{1}\leq 2^{\aleph_{0}}$. Bernstein \cite{bib:1908} and Banaschewski/Moore \cite{bib:1990}.

[\textbf{170 A}] There is a function that assigns to each denumerable set $D$ of real numbers a real number not in $D$. Sierpi\'{n}ski \cite{bib:1954}.

\noindent[\textbf{170 B}] There is an uncountable, well orderable set of reals. Raisonnier\index{Author}{Raisonnier} \cite{bib:1982} and note 3.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 171.} If $(P, \leq)$ is a partial order such that $P$ is the denumerable union of finite sets and all antichains in $P$ are finite then for each denumerable family $\mathcal{D}$ of dense sets there is a $\mathcal{D}$ generic filter. Shannon\index{Author}{Shannon} \cite{bib:1990} and note 47.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 172.} For every infinite set $S$, if $S$ is hereditarily countable (that is, every $y\in TC(S)$ is countable) then $|TC(S)|=\aleph_{0}$. Jech\index{Author}{Jech} \cite{bib:1982}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 173.} MPL: Metric spaces are para-Lindel\"{o}f. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/ Stanley\index{Author}{Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley} \cite{bib:1997} and note 141.

[\textbf{173 A}] MML: Metric spaces are meta-Lindel\"{o}f. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/ Stanley \cite{bib:1997} and note 141.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 174($\alpha$).} $RM1,\,\aleph_{\alpha}$: The representation theorem for multi-algebras with $\aleph_{\alpha}$ unary operations: Assume $(A, F)$ is a multi-algebra with $\aleph_{\alpha}$ unary operations (and no other operations). Then there is an algebra $(B, G)$ with $\aleph_{\alpha}$ unary operations and an equivalence relation $E$ on $B$ such that $(B/E, G/E)$ and $(A, F)$ are isomorphic multi-algebras. H\"{o}ft/Howard\index{Author}{H\"{o}ft/Howard} \cite{bib:1981} and note 50.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 175.} Transitivity Condition: For all sets $x$, there is a set $u$ abd a function $f$ such that $u$ is transitive and $f$ is a one to one function from $x$ onto $u$. von Rimscha\index{Author}{Rimscha} \cite{bib:1982}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 176.} Every infinite, locally finite group has an infinite Abelian subgroup. (\emph{Locally finite} means every finite subset generates a finite subgroup.) Plotkin\index{Author}{Plotkin} \cite{bib:1981}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 177.} An infinite box product of regular $T_{1}$ spaces, each of cardinality greater than 1, is neither first countable nor connected. Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1981a}, Knight\index{Author}{Knight} \cite{bib:1964}, and note 52.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 178($n, N$).} If $n\in\omega$, $n\geq 2$ and $N\subseteq\{1,2, \ldots, n-1\},\, N\neq\emptyset,\, MC(\infty, n, N)$: If $X$ is any set of $n$-element sets then there is a function $f$ with domain $X$ such that for all $A\in X,\,f(A)\subseteq A$ and $|f(A)|\in N$. Zuckerman\index{Author}{Zuckerman} \cite{bib:1969a}, \cite{bib:1981}, and note 53.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 179($\epsilon$).} Suppose $\epsilon>0$ is an ordinal. $\forall x, x\in W(\epsilon)$. David\index{Author}{David} \cite{bib:1980} and note 25.

\noindent \textbf{FORM 180.} Every Abelian group has a divisible hull. (If $A$ and $B$ are groups, $B$ \emph{is a divisible hull of} $A$ means $B$ is a divisible group, $A$ is a subgroup of $B$ and for every non-zero $b\in B,\, \exists n\in\omega$ such that $0\neq nb\in A$.) Fuchs \cite{bib:1970}, Theorem~24.4 p 107, Hodges\index{Author}{Hodges} \cite{bib:1980}, and note 24.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 181.} $C(2^{\aleph_{0}}, \infty)$: Every set $X$ of non-empty sets such that $|X|=2^{\aleph_{0}}$ has a choice function. Freyd\index{Author}{Freyd} \cite{bib:1980}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 182.} There is an aleph whose cofinality is greater than $\aleph_{0}$. Gitik\index{Author}{Gitik} \cite{bib:1980}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 183($\alpha$).} There are no $\aleph_{\alpha}$ minimal sets. That is, there are no sets $X$ such that

(1) $|X|$ is incomparable with $\aleph_{\alpha}$

\noindent(2) $\aleph_{\beta}<|X|$ for every $\beta<\alpha$ and

\noindent(3) $\forall Y\subseteq X,\,|Y|<\aleph_{\alpha}$ or $|X-Y|<\aleph_{\alpha}$.

\noindent Hickman\index{Author}{Hickman} \cite{bib:1980b} and note 56.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 184.} Existence of a double uniformization: For all $X$ and $Y$, for all $E\subseteq X\times Y$, if there is an infinite cardinal $\kappa$ satisfying:

\noindent(1) $\forall y_{0}\in Y,\,|\{(x, y_{0}):x\in X\}\cap E|=\kappa$ and

\noindent(2) $\forall x_{0}\in X,\,|\{(x_{0}, y):y\in Y\}\cap E|=\kappa$,

\noindent then $\exists U\subseteq E$ such that for all $(x, y)\in E,\,\exists!z\in X$ such that $(z, y)\in U$ and $\exists!z\in Y$ such that $(x, z)\in U$. ($U$ is called a \emph{double uniformization} of $E$.) Kaniewski/Rogers\index{Author}{Kaniewski/Rogers} \cite{bib:1980}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 185.} Every linearly ordered Dedekind finite set is finite. Hickman \cite{bib:1979a} and note 94.

[\textbf{185 A}] If $X$ is a linearly ordered set and there is neither an increasing nor a decreasing injection $f:\omega\rightarrow X$, then $X$ is finite. Hickman\index{Author}{Hickman} \cite{bib:1979a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 186.} Every pair\index{Subject}{double uniformization} of cardinal numbers has a least upper bound (in the usual cardinal ordering.) Hickman \cite{bib:1979b}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 187.} Every pair of cardinal numbers has a greatest lower bound (in the usual cardinal ordering.) Hickman \cite{bib:1979b}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 188.} $EP$ \emph{Ab}: For every Abelian group $A$ there is a projective Abelian group $G$ and a homomorphism from $G$ onto $A$. Blass\index{Author}{Blass} \cite{bib:1979} and note 60.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 189.} $EI$ \emph{Ab}: For every Abelian group $A$ there is an injective Abelian group $G$ and a one to one homomorphism from $A$ into $G$. Blass \cite{bib:1979} and note 60.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 190.} There is a non-trivial injective Abelian group. Blass \cite{bib:1979} and note 60.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 191.} $SVC$: There is a set $S$ such that for every set $a$, there is an ordinal $\alpha$ and a function from $S\times\alpha$ onto $a$. Blass \cite{bib:1979}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 192.} $EP$ sets: For every set $A$ there is a projective set $X$ and a function from $X$ onto $A$. Blass \cite{bib:1979} and note 60.

[\textbf{192 A}] $(\forall x)(\exists y)$ ($x\leq^{\ast}y$ and $y$ indexed choice holds). Blass in Mathias\index{Author}{Mathias} \cite{bib:1977b}, notes 60 and 69.

\noindent \textbf{FORM 193.} $EFP$ \emph{Ab}: Every Abelian group is a homomorphic image of a free projective Abelian group. Blass \cite{bib:1979} and note 60.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 194.} $C(\varPi_{2}^{1})$ or $AC(\varPi_{2}^{1})$: If $P\in \omega \times^{\omega} \omega,\,P$ has domain $\omega$, and $P$ is in $\varPi_{2}^{1}$, then there is a sequence of elements $\langle x_{k}: k\in \omega\rangle$ of $^{\omega}\omega$ with $\langle k,\,x_{k}\rangle\in P$ for all $k\in\omega$. Kanovei\index{Author}{Kanovei} \cite{bib:1979} and note 61.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 195.} Every general linear system has a linear global reaction. Note 62 and Harazisville (see Kharazishvili\index{Author}{Kharazishvili} \cite{bib:1979}).

\noindent\textbf{FORM 196($\alpha$).} $\aleph_{\alpha}$ and $\aleph_{\alpha+1}$ are not both measurable. Bull\index{Author}{Bull} \cite{bib:1978} and note 20.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 197.} $\mathbb{R}^{2}$ is the union of three sets $C$ with the property that for all $x\in C$ there is a straight line $L$ such that $L\cap C=\{x\}$. Davies \cite{bib:1978}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 198.} For every set $S$, if the only linearly orderable subsets of $S$ are the finite subsets of $S$, then either $S$ is finite or $S$ has an amorphous subset. Hickman \cite{bib:1978b} and note 57.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 199($n$).} (For $n\in \omega-\{0, 1\})$ If all $\varSigma_{n}^{1}$, Dedekind finite subsets of $^{\omega}\omega$ are finite, then all $\varPi_{n}^{1}$ Dedekind finite subsets of $^{\omega}\omega$ are finite. Kanovei \cite{bib:1978}, notes 57 and 61.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 200.} For all infinite $x,\,|2^{x}|=|x!|$. Dawson/Howard\index{Author}{Dawson/Howard} \cite{bib:1976} and note 64.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 201.} Linking Axiom for Boolean Algebras: Every Boolean algebra has a maximal linked system. ($L\subseteq B$ is \emph{linked} if $a\wedge b\neq 0$ for all $a$ and $b\in L$.) Schrijver\index{Author}{Schrijver} \cite{bib:1978}.

[\textbf{201 A}] Strong Linking Axiom for Boolean Algebras: Each linked system in a Boolean algebra is contained in some maximal linked system. (If $B$ is a Boolean algebra, $L\subseteq B$ is \emph{linked} if $a\wedge b\neq 0$ for all $a$ and $b\in L$.) Schrijver \cite{bib:1978}.

\noindent[\textbf{201 B}] Disjoint Transversal axiom (2,2): If $X$ is a set and $\mathcal{U}$ and $\mathcal{V}$ are subsets of $\{y\subseteq X:|y|\leq 2\}$ and if for each two finite subsets $\mathcal{U}_{0}\subseteq \mathcal{U}$ and $\mathcal{V}_{0}\subseteq \mathcal{V}$ there are transversals $Y_{1}$ and $Y_{2}$ for $\mathcal{U}_{0}$ and $\mathcal{V}_{0}$ respectively such that $Y_{1}\cap Y_{2}=\emptyset$, then there are disjoint transversals $X_{1}$ and $X_{2}$ for $\mathcal{U}$ and $\mathcal{V}$ respectively. $(Y\subseteq X$ is a \emph{transversal} for $\mathcal{U}$ if for all $y\in CalU,\, y\cap Y\neq\emptyset$.) Schrijver\index{Author}{Schrijver} \cite{bib:1978}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 202.} $C(LO, \infty)$: Every linearly ordered family of non-empty sets has a choice function. Truss\index{Author}{Truss} \cite{bib:1978}.

[\textbf{202 A}] $H(TR\& C, P)$: If $(X, R)$ is a transitive, connected relation. Then $X$ has a $\subseteq$-maximal partially ordered subset. Harper/Rubin\index{Author}{Harper/Rubin} \cite{bib:1976} and note 39.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 203.} $C$(disjoint,$\subseteq \mathbb{R})$: Every partition of $\mathcal{P}(\omega)$ into non-empty subsets has a choice function. Truss \cite{bib:1978}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 204.} For every infinite $X$, there is a function from $X$ onto $2X$. Truss \cite{bib:1978}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 205.} For all cardinals $m$ and $n$, if $m\leq^{\ast}n$ and $\neg(n\leq^{\ast}m)$ then there is a cardinal $k<n$ such that $m\leq^{\ast}k$. Pelc\index{Author}{Pelc} \cite{bib:1978} and note 69.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 206.} The existence of a non-principal ultrafilter: There exists an infinite set $X$ and a non-principal ultrafilter on $X$. Blass\index{Author}{Blass} \cite{bib:1977b}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 207($\alpha$).} $UT(\aleph_{\alpha}, \aleph_{\alpha}, <2^{\aleph_{\alpha}})$: The union of $\aleph_{\alpha}$ sets each of cardinality $\aleph_{\alpha}$ has cardinality less than $2^{\aleph_{\alpha}}$. Figura\index{Author}{Figura} \cite{bib:1977}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 208.} For all ordinals $\alpha,\,\aleph_{\alpha+1}\leq 2^{\aleph_{\alpha}}$. Figura \cite{bib:1977}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 209.} There is an ordinal $\alpha$ such that for all $X$, if $X$ is a denumerable union of denumerable sets then $\mathcal{P}(X)$ cannot be partitioned into $\aleph_{\alpha}$ non-empty sets. Morris\index{Author}{Morris} \cite{bib:1970}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 210.} The commutator subgroup of a free group is free. L\"{a}uchli\index{Author}{L\"{a}uchli} \cite{bib:1962}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 211.} $DCR$: Dependent choice for relations on $\mathbb{R}$: If $R\subseteq \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}$ satisfies $(\forall x\in \mathbb{R})(\exists y\in \mathbb{R})(x\,R\,y)$ then there is a sequence $\langle x(n): n\in\omega\rangle$ of real numbers such that $(\forall n\in \omega)(x(n)\, R\, x(n+1))$. Mathias\index{Author}{Mathias}
\cite{bib:1977a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 212.} $C(2^{\aleph_{0}}, \subseteq \mathbb{R})$: If $R$ is a relation on $\mathbb{R}$ such that for all $x\in \mathbb{R}$, there is a $y\in \mathbb{R}$ such that $x\,R\,y$, then there is a function $f:\mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that for all $x\in \mathbb{R},\,x\,R\,f(x)$. Mathias \cite{bib:1977a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 213.} $C(\infty, \aleph_{1})$: If $(\forall y\in X)(|y|=\aleph_{1})$ then $X$ has a choice function. Pincus\index{Author}{Pincus} \cite{bib:1977a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 214.} $Z(\omega)$: For every family $A$ of infinite sets, there is a function $f$ such that for all $y\in A,\,f(y)$ is a non-empty subset of $y$ and $|f(y)|=\aleph_{0}$. Pincus \cite{bib:1977a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 215.} If $(\forall y\subseteq X)(y$ can be linearly ordered implies $y$ is finite), then $X$ is finite. Pincus \cite{bib:1972a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 216.} Every infinite tree has either an infinite chain or an infinite antichain. Pincus \cite{bib:1972a} and note 21.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 217.} Every infinite partially ordered set has either an infinite chain or an infinite antichain. Pincus \cite{bib:1972a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 218.} $(\forall n\in\omega -\{0\})MC(\infty, \infty$, relatively prime to $n$): $\forall n\in \omega-\{0\}$, if $X$ is a set of non-empty sets, then there is a function $f$ such that for all $x\in X,\,f(x)$ is a non-empty, finite subset of $x$ and $|f(x)|$ is relatively prime to $n$. Bleicher\index{Author}{Bleicher} \cite{bib:1965}.

[\textbf{218 A}]\index{Author}{Pineus/Solovay} Existence of Complementary Subspaces: For every field $F$, every vector space $V$ over $F$ has the property that if $S\subseteq V$ is a subspace of $V$, then there is a subspace $S^{\prime}\subseteq V$ such that $S\cap S^{\prime}=\{0\}$ and $S\cup S^{\prime}$ generates $V$. Bleicher
\cite{bib:1964}, \cite{bib:1965}, H. Rubin/J. Rubin\index{Author}{H. Rubin/J. Rubin} \cite{bib:1985}, pp 123ff, Theorems 6.36, 6.37, and 6.38.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 219.} $(\forall n\in \omega -\{0\})MC(\infty, WO$, relatively prime to $n)$: For all non-zero $n\in \omega$, if $X$ is a set of non-empty well orderable sets, then there is a function $f$ such that for all $x\in X,\, f(x)$ is a non-empty, finite subset of $x$, and $|f(x)|$ is relatively prime to $n$. Pincus\index{Author}{Pincus} \cite{bib:1972a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 220($p$).} Suppose $p\in\omega$ and $p$ is a prime. Any two elementary Abelian $p$-groups (all non-trivial elements have order $p$) of the same cardinality are isomorphic. Hickman\index{Author}{Hickman} \cite{bib:1977b}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 221.} For all infinite $X$, there is a non-principal measure on $\mathcal{P}(X)$. Pincus/Solovay \cite{bib:1977} and note 147.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 222.} There is a non-principal measure on $\mathcal{P}(\omega)$. Pincus/Solovay \cite{bib:1977} and note 147.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 223.} There is an infinite set $X$ and a non-principal measure on $\mathcal{P}(X)$. Pincus/Solovay \cite{bib:1977} and note 147.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 224.} There is a partition of the real line into $\aleph_{1}$ Borel sets $\{B_{\alpha}:\alpha<\aleph_{1}\}$ such that for some $\beta<\aleph_{1},\,\forall\alpha<\aleph_{1},\, B_{\alpha}\in G_{\beta}$. $(G_{\beta}$ for $\beta<\aleph_{1}$ is defined by induction, $G_{0}=$\{$A: A$ is an open subset of $\mathbb{R}$\} and for $\beta>0$,

$G_{\beta}=\{\bigcap_{i=0}^{\infty}A_{i}:(\forall i\in w)(\exists\xi<\beta)(A_{i}\in G_{\xi})\}\ \mathrm{if}\ \beta\ \mathrm{is\ even\ and}$

\noindent $G_{\beta}=\{\bigcup_{i=0}^{\infty}A_{i}:(\forall i \in \omega)(\exists\xi<\beta)(A_{i}\in G_{\xi})\}\ \mathrm{if}\ \beta\ \mathrm{is\ odd}.)$

\noindent Stern\index{Author}{Stern} \cite{bib:1979}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 225.} Every proper filter on $\omega$ can be extended to an ultrafilter. Rav\index{Author}{Rav} \cite{bib:1977}.

[\textbf{225 A}] There exists a compact, extremally disconnected topological space having a Dedekind infinite set of clopen subsets. Morillon\index{Author}{Morillon} \cite{bib:1993}, notes 94 and 114.

\noindent[\textbf{225 B}] There exists a compact, $\sigma$-extremally disconnected topological space having a Dedekind infinite set of clopen subsets. Morillon \cite{bib:1993}, notes 94 and 114.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 226.} Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity, $B$ a proper subring containing 1 and $q$ a prime ideal in $B$. Then there is a subring $A$ of $R$ and a prime ideal $p$ in $A$ such that (a) $B\subseteq A$ (b) $q=B\cap p$ (c) $R-p$ is multiplicatively closed and (d) if $A\neq R$, then $R-A$ is multiplicatively closed. Rav \cite{bib:1977}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 227.} For all groups $G$, if every finite subgroup of $G$ can be fully ordered then $G$ can be fully ordered. Rav \cite{bib:1977} and note 79.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 228.} Every torsion free Abelian group can be fully ordered. Rav \cite{bib:1977} and note 79.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 229.} If $(G, \circ, \leq)$ is a partially ordered group, then $\leq$ can be extended to a linear order on $G$ if and only if for every finite set $\{a_{1}, \ldots, a_{n}\}\subseteq G$, with $a_{i}\neq$ the identity for $i=1$ to $n$, the signs $\epsilon_{1},\,\ldots,\,\epsilon_{n}\
(\epsilon_{i}=\pm 1)$ can be chosen so that $P\cap S(a_{1}^{\epsilon_{1}}, \ldots, a_{n}^{\epsilon_{n}})=\emptyset$ (where $S(b_{1}, \ldots, b_{n})$ is the normal sub-semi-group of $G$ generated by $b_{1},\,\ldots,\,b_{n}$ and $P=\{g\in G:e\leq g\}$ where $e$ is the identity of $G$.) Rav\index{Author}{Rav} \cite{bib:1977}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 230.} $L^{1}=HOD$.\index{Subject}{Artin-Schreier theorem} Szczepaniak\index{Author}{Szczepaniak} \cite{bib:1977} and note 82.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 231.} $UT(WO, WO, WO)$: The union of a well ordered collection of well orderable sets is well orderable. Tsukada\index{Author}{Tsukada} \cite{bib:1977}.

[\textbf{231 A}] Every almost well orderable set ($W$-set) is well orderable. Note 25.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 232.} Every metric space ($X, d$) has a $\sigma$-point finite base. Howard/ Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley\index{Author}{Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley} \cite{bib:1997} and note 141.

[\textbf{232 A}] Every metric space has a $\gamma$-point finite base, for some ordinal $\gamma$. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley \cite{bib:1997} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{232 B}] Every metric space has a $\sigma$-locally finite base. Howard/Keremedis/ Rubin/Stanley \cite{bib:1997} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{232 C}] Every metric space has a $\gamma$-locally finite base, for some ordinal $\gamma$. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley \cite{bib:1997} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{232 D}] Every metric space ($X, d$) has a $\sigma$-discrete base. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley \cite{bib:1997} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{232 E}] Every metric space ($X, d$) has a $\gamma$-discrete base, for some ordinal $\gamma$. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley \cite{bib:1997} and note 141.

\noindent[\textbf{232 F}] Every metric space ($X, d$) has a $\sigma$-disjoint base. Howard/Keremedis/ Rubin/Stanley \cite{bib:1997} and note 141.

\noindent [\textbf{232 G}] Every metric space ($X, d$) has a $\gamma$-disjoint base for some ordinal $\gamma$. Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley \cite{bib:1997} and note 141.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 233.} If a field has an algebraic closure it is unique up to isomorphism. Mathias\index{Author}{Mathias} \cite{bib:1977b}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 234.} There is a non-Ramsey set: There is a set $A$ of infinite subsets of $\omega$ such that for every infinite subset $N$ of $\omega,\,N$ has a subset which is in $A$ and a subset which is not in $A$. Prikry\index{Author}{Prikry} \cite{bib:1976} and Mathias \cite{bib:1968}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 235.} If $V$ is a vector space and $B_{1}$ and $B_{2}$ are bases for $V$ then $|B_{1}|$ and $|B_{2}|$ are comparable. Gross\index{Author}{Gross} \cite{bib:1976}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 236.} If $V$ is a vector space with a basis and $S$ is a linearly independent subset of $V$ such that no proper extension of $S$ is a basis for $V$, then $S$ is a basis for $V$. Gross \cite{bib:1975}, \cite{bib:1976}.

[\textbf{236 A}] If $V$ is a vector space with a basis, then every linearly independent subset is contained in a basis.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 237.} The order of any group is divisible by the order of any of its subgroups, (i.e., if $H$ is a subgroup of $G$ then there is a set $A$ such that $|H\times A|=|G|.)$ Hickman\index{Author}{Hickman} \cite{bib:1976}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 238.} Every elementary Abelian group (that is, for some prime $p$ every non identity element has order \emph{p}) is the direct sum of cyclic subgroups. Hickman \cite{bib:1976}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 239.} For all $X$, if $X\neq\emptyset$, then there is a binary operation on $X$ that makes $X$ a group. Hickman\index{Author}{Hickman} \cite{bib:1976}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 240.} If a group $G$ satisfies ``every ascending chain of subgroups is finite,'' then every subgroup of $G$ is finitely generated. Hickman \cite{bib:1976}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 241.} Every algebraic closure of $\mathbb{Q}$ has a real closed subfield. Hodges\index{Author}{Hodges} \cite{bib:1976a}, L\"{a}uchli\index{Author}{L\"{a}uchli} \cite{bib:1962} and note 84.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 242.} There is, up to an isomorphism, at most one algebraic closure of $\mathbb{Q}$. Hodges \cite{bib:1976a}, L\"{a}uchli \cite{bib:1962} and note 84.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 243.} Every principal ideal domain is a unique factorization domain. Hodges \cite{bib:1976a} and note 84.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 244.} Every principal ideal domain has a maximal ideal. Hodges \cite{bib:1976a} and note 84.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 245.} There is a function $f:\omega_{1}\rightarrow\omega_{1}^{\omega}$ such that for every $\alpha,\, 0<\alpha<\omega_{1},\,f(\alpha)$ is a function from $\omega$ onto $\alpha$. Litman\index{Author}{Litman} \cite{bib:1976}.

[\textbf{245 A}] There is a function $g:\omega_{1}\rightarrow \omega_{1}^{\omega}$ such that for all limit ordinals $\alpha<\omega_{1},\,g(\alpha)$ is an increasing function from $\omega$ into $\alpha$ with the range of $g$ cofinal in $\alpha$. Litman \cite{bib:1976}

\noindent[\textbf{245 B}] Every closed set A in $\omega_{1}$ which contains only limit ordinals is a derivative (that is, $\exists B\subseteq\omega_{1}$ such that $A=\{x:x$ is a limit and $\{t:t\in B\}$ is cofinal in $x\}.)$ Litman \cite{bib:1976}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 246.} The monadic theory theory $MT(\omega_{1}, <)$ of $\omega_{1}$ is recursive. Litman \cite{bib:1976} and note 85.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 247.} Every atomless Boolean algebra is Dedekind infinite. Plotkin\index{Author}{Plotkin} \cite{bib:1976}, notes 86 and 94.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 248.} For any $\kappa,\,\kappa$ is the cardinal number of an infinite complete Boolean algebra if and only if $\kappa^{\aleph_{0}}=\kappa$. Plotkin \cite{bib:1976} and note 86.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 249.} If $T$ is an infinite tree in which every element has exactly 2 immediate successors then $T$ has an infinite branch. Truss\index{Author}{Truss} \cite{bib:1975}, note 87 and note 21.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 250.} $(\forall n\in \omega-\{0,1\})(C(WO, n))$: For every natural number $n\geq 2$, every well ordered family of $n$ element sets has a choice function. Truss \cite{bib:1975}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 251.} The additive groups $(\mathbb{R}, +)$ and $(\mathbb{C}, +)$ are isomorphic. Ash\index{Author}{Ash} \cite{bib:1975}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 252.} The additive groups of $\mathbb{Q} \oplus \mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{R}$ are isomorphic. Ash \cite{bib:1975}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 253.} {\L}o\'{s}' Theorem: If $M=\langle A,\,R_{j}\rangle_{j\in J}$ is a relational system, $X$ any set and $\mathcal{F}$ an ultrafilter in $\mathcal{P}(X)$, then $M$ and $M^{X}/\mathcal{F}$ are elementarily equivalent. Howard\index{Author}{Howard} \cite{bib:1975}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 254.} $Z(D, R, l)$: Every directed relation $(P, R)$ in which ramified subsets have least upper bounds, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin\index{Author}{Harper/Rubin} \cite{bib:1976} and note 39.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 255.} $Z(D, R)$: Every directed relation $(P, R)$ in which every ramified subset $A$ has an upper bound, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin \cite{bib:1976} and note 39.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 256.} $Z(P, F)$: Every partially ordered set $(X, R)$ in which every forest $A$ has an upper bound, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin\index{Author}{Harper/Rubin} \cite{bib:1976} and note 39.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 257.} $Z(TR, P)$:\index{Subject}{{\L}os' theorem}
 Every transitive relation $(X, R)$ in which every partially ordered subset has an upper bound, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin \cite{bib:1976} and note 39.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 258.} $Z(D, L)$: Every directed relation $(X, R)$ in which linearly ordered subsets have upper bounds, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin \cite{bib:1976} and note 39.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 259.} $Z(TR\& C, W)$: If ($X,\, R)$ is a transitive and connected relation in which every well ordered subset has an upper bound, then $(X, R)$ has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin \cite{bib:1976} and note 39.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 260.} $Z(TR\& C, P)$: If $(X, R)$ is a transitive and connected relation in which every partially ordered subset has an upper bound, then $(X, R)$ has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin \cite{bib:1976} and note 39.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 261.} $Z(TR, T)$: Every transitive relation $(X, R)$ in which every subset which is a tree has an upper bound, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin \cite{bib:1976} and note 39.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 262.} $Z(TR, R)$: Every transitive relation $(X, R)$ in which every ramified subset $A$ has an upper bound, has a maximal element. Harper/Rubin \cite{bib:1976} and note 39.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 263.} $H(AS\& C, P)$: Every every relation $(X, R)$ which is antisymmetric and connected contains a $\subseteq$-maximal partially ordered subset. Harper/Rubin \cite{bib:1976} and note 39.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 264.} $H(C, P)$: Every connected relation $(X, R)$ contains a $\subseteq$-maximal partially ordered set. Harper/Rubin \cite{bib:1976} and note 39.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 265.} $H(A, TR)$: Every relation $(X, R)$ contains a $\subseteq$-maximal transitive subset. Harper/Rubin \cite{bib:1976} and note 39.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 266.} $H(AS, P)$: Every antisymmetric relation contains $\subseteq$-maximal partially ordered subset. Harper/Rubin \cite{bib:1976} and note 39.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 267.} There is no infinite, free complete Boolean algebra. Stavi\index{Author}{Stavi} \cite{bib:1975} and note 89.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 268}. If $\mathcal{L}$ is a lattice isomorphic to the lattice of subalgebras of some unary universal algebra (a unary universal algebra is one with only unary or nullary operations) and $\alpha$ is an automorphism of $\mathcal{L}$ of order 2 (that is, $\alpha^{2}$ is the identity) then there is a unary algebra $\mathfrak{A}$ and an isomorphism $\rho$ from $\mathcal{L}$ onto the lattice of subalgebras of $\mathfrak{A}^{2}$ with $\rho(\alpha(x))=(\rho(x))^{-1}(=\{(s, t):(t, s)\in\rho(x)\}\rangle$ for all $x\in \mathcal{L}$. Lampe\index{Author}{Lampe} \cite{bib:1974}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 269}. For every cardinal $m$, there is a set $A$ such that $2^{|A|^{2}}\geq m$ and there is a choice function on the collection of 2-element subsets of $A$. Lampe \cite{bib:1974}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 270}. $CT_{\mathrm{fin}}$: The compactness theorem for propositional logic restricted to sets of formulas in which each variable occurs only in a finite number of formulas. Kolany/Wojtylak\index{Author}{Kolany/Wojtylak} \cite{bib:1991}.

[\textbf{270 A}] $C(\infty, <\aleph_{0})\wedge CT_{2}\ (CT_{2}$ is the compactness theorem for propositional logic restricted to sets of formulas in which each variable occurs in at most two formulas. See form $271(n).)$ Kolany/Wojtylak\index{Author}{Kolany}\index{Author}{Kolany/Wojtylak} \cite{bib:1991}.

\noindent[\textbf{270 B}] $F_{\mathrm{fin}}$: For any family $\mathcal{F}$ of pairwise disjoint, non-empty, finite sets if $R$ is a symmetric binary relation on $\bigcup \mathcal{F}$ which satisfies (i) the set $\{b\in\bigcup \mathcal{F}:\neg a\,R\,b\}$ is finite for every $a\in\bigcup \mathcal{F}$ and (ii) every finite subfamily of $\mathcal{F}$ has an $R$-consistent choice function, then $\mathcal{F}$ has an $R$-consistent choice function. Kolany/Wojtylak \cite{bib:1991}.

\noindent [\textbf{270 C(n)}] $F_{n}^{\mathrm{fin}}$ ($n\geq 3$ a natural number): For any family $\mathcal{F}$ of pairwise disjoint, $n$ element sets if $R$ is a symmetric binary relation on $\bigcup \mathcal{F}$ which satisfies (i) the set $\{b\in\bigcup \mathcal{F}:\neg a\ R\ b\}$ is finite for every $a\in\bigcup \mathcal{F}$ and (ii) every finite subfamily of $\mathcal{F}$ has an $R$-consistent choice function, then $\mathcal{F}$ has an $R$-consistent choice function. Kolany \cite{bib:1992}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 271 ($n$)}. If $n\in \omega-\{0,1\},\,CT_{n}$: The compactness theorem for propositional logic restricted to sets of formulas in which each variable occurs in at most $n$ formulas. Kolany/Wojtylak \cite{bib:1991}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 272}. There is an $X\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ such that neither $X$ nor $\mathbb{R} -X$ has a perfect subset. Truss\index{Author}{Truss} \cite{bib:1974b} and note 28.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 273}. There is a subset of $\mathbb{R}$ which is not Borel. Truss \cite{bib:1974b}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 274}. There is a cardinal number $x$ and an $n\in \omega$ such that $\neg (x\ \mathrm{adj}^{n}\,x^{2}$). (The expression ``$x\,\mathrm{adj}^{n}\, ya^{\prime\prime}$ means there are cardinals $z_{0},\,\ldots,\,z_{n}$ such that $z_{0}=x$ and $z_{n}=y$ and for all $i,\,0\leq i<n,\,z_{i}<z_{i+1}$ and if $z_{i}<z\leq z_{i+1}$, then $z=z_{i+1}$.) (Compare with [$0$ A]). Truss \cite{bib:1974b}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 275}. The sequence of cardinals $\langle\aleph_{n}: n\in \omega\rangle$ has a unique minimal upper bound. Truss \cite{bib:1974b}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 276}. $E(V^{\prime\prime}, III)$: For every set $A,\,\mathcal{P}(A)$ is Dedekind finite if and only if $A=\emptyset$ or $2|\mathcal{P}(A)|>|\mathcal{P}(A)|$. Howard/Spi\u{s}iak\index{Author}{Howard/Spi\u{s}iak} \cite{bib:1994} and note 94.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 277.} $E(D, VII)$: Every non-well-orderable cardinal is decomposable. Monro\index{Author}{Monro} \cite{bib:1973a} and note 94.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 278}. In an integral domain $R$, if every ideal is finitely generated then $R$ has a maximal proper ideal. Hodges\index{Author}{Hodges} \cite{bib:1974} and note 45 E.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 279}. The Closed Graph Theorem for operations between Fr\'{e}chet Spaces: Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are Fr\'{e}chet spaces, $T:X\rightarrow Y$ is linear and $G=\{(x, Tx): x\in X\}$ is closed in $X\times Y$. Then $T$ is continuous. Rudin\index{Author}{Rudin} \cite{bib:1991} p. 51, Wright\index{Author}{Wright} \cite{bib:1973}, note 96.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 280.} There is a complete separable metric space with a subset which does not have the Baire property. Wright \cite{bib:1973} and note 28.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 281.} There is a Hilbert space $H$ and an unbounded linear operator on $H$. Wright \cite{bib:1973}, note 96.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 282.} $\omega\not\rightarrow (\omega)^{\omega}$. Erd\"{o}s/Rado\index{Author}{Erd\"{o}s/Rado} \cite{bib:1952}, Kleinberg/Seiferas\index{Author}{Kleinberg/Seiferas} \cite{bib:1973} and note 97.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 283.} Cardinality of well ordered subsets: For all $n\in \omega$ and for all infinite $x,\,|x^{n}|<|s(x)|$ where $s(x)$ is the set of all well orderable subsets of $x$. Truss\index{Author}{Truss} \cite{bib:1973d}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 284.} A system\index{Subject}{closed graph theorem} of linear equations over a field $F$ has a solution in $F$ if and only if every finite sub-system has a solution in $F$. Cowen/Emerson\index{Author}{Cowen/Emerson} \cite{bib:1995}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 285.} Let $E$ be a set and $f:E\rightarrow E$, then $f$ has a fixed point if and only if $E$ is not the union of three mutually disjoint sets $E_{1},\,E_{2}$ and $E_{3}$ such that $E_{i}\cap f(E_{i})=\emptyset$ for $i=1,2,3$. Makowski/Wi\'{s}niewski\index{Author}{Makowski/Wi\'{s}niewski}\index{Author}{Wi\'{s}niewski} \cite{bib:1969}, Abian\index{Author}{Abian} \cite{bib:1968}, Baker\index{Author}{Baker} \cite{bib:1964}, and Kenyon\index{Author}{Kenyon} \cite{bib:1963}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 286.} Extended Krein-Milman Theorem:\index{Subject}{Krein-Milman theorem} Let K be a quasicompact (sometimes called convex-compact), convex subset of a locally convex topological vector space, then K has an extreme point. H. Rubin/J. Rubin\index{Author}{H. Rubin/J. Rubin} \cite{bib:1985}, p. 177--178 and note 23.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 287.} The Hahn-Banach Theorem\index{Subject}{Hahn-Banach theorem} for Separable Normed Linear Spaces: Assume $V$ is a separable normed linear space and $p:V\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ satisfies $p(x+y)\leq p(x)+p(y)$ and $(\forall t\geq 0)(\forall x\in V)(p(tx)=tp(x))$ and assume $f$ is a linear function from a subspace $S$ of $V$ into $\mathbb{R}$ which satisfies $(\forall x\in S)(f(x)\leq p(x))$, then $f$ can be extended to $f^{\ast}:V\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ so that $f^{\ast}$ is linear and $(\forall x\in V)(f^{\ast}(x)\leq p(x))$. Note 145.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 288($n$).} If $n\in\omega -\{0,1\}, C(\aleph_{0}, n)$: Every denumerable set of $n$-element sets has a choice function. Wi\'{s}niewski \cite{bib:1972}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 289.} If $S$ is a set of subsets of a countable set and $S$ is closed under chain unions, then $S$ has a $\subseteq$-maximal element. Smullyan\index{Author}{Smullyan} \cite{bib:1994} and note 102.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 290.} For all infinite $x,\,|2^{x}|=|x^{x}|$. Pincus\index{Author}{Pincus} \cite{bib:1978} and note 64.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 291.} For all infinite $x,\,|x!|=|x^{x}|$. Pincus \cite{bib:1978} and note 64.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 292.} $MC(LO, \infty)$: For each linearly ordered family of non-empty sets $X$, there is a function $f$ such that for all $x\in X\
f(x)$ is non-empty, finite subset of $x$). Howard/Rubin\index{Author}{Howard/Rubin} \cite{bib:1977}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 293.} For all sets $x$ and $y$, if $x$ can be linearly ordered and there is a mapping of $x$ onto $y$, then $y$ can be linearly ordered.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 294.} Every linearly ordered $W$-set is well orderable. Morris\index{Author}{Morris} \cite{bib:1969} and note 25.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 295.} DO: Every infinite set has a dense linear ordering. Gonzalez\index{Author}{Gonzalez} \cite{bib:1995a}.

\textbf{[295 A]} DUO: Every infinite set has a dense unbounded linear ordering. (An ordering is \emph{unbounded} if there is neither a least element nor a greatest element.) Pincus \cite{bib:1997}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 296.} Part-$\infty$: Every infinite set is the disjoint union of infinitely many infinite sets. Gonzalez \cite{bib:1995b}, Pincus \cite{bib:1997}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 297.} Extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff spaces are projective in the category of all compact Hausdorff spaces. Banaschewski\index{Author}{Banaschewski} \cite{bib:1988}, Bell\index{Author}{Bell} \cite{bib:1988}, notes 60 and 114.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 298.} Every compact Hausdorff space has a Gleason cover. Bell\index{Author}{Bell} \cite{bib:1988}, Gleason\index{Author}{Gleason} \cite{bib:1958}, and note 114.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 299.} Any extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff space is projective in the category of Boolean topological spaces. Bell \cite{bib:1988}, notes 60 and 114.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 300.} Any continuous surjection between extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff spaces has an irreducible restriction to a closed subset of its domain. Bell \cite{bib:1988} and note 114.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 301.} Any continuous surjection between Boolean spaces has an irreducible restriction to a closed subset of its domain. Bell \cite{bib:1988} and note 114.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 302.} Any continuous surjection between compact Hausdorff spaces has an irreducible restriction to a closed subset of its domain. Bell \cite{bib:1988} and note 114.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 303.} If $B$ is a Boolean algebra, $S\subseteq B$ and $S$ is closed under $\wedge$, then there is a $\subseteq$-maximal proper ideal $I$ of $B$ such that $I \cap S=\{0\}$. H. Rubin/J. Rubin\index{Author}{H. Rubin/J. Rubin} \cite{bib:1985}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 304.} There does not exist a $T_{2}$ topological space $X$ such that every infinite subset of $X$ contains an infinite compact subset. Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1985c}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 305.} There are $2^{\aleph_{0}}$ Vitali equivalence classes.\index{Subject}{Vitali equivalence classes} (\emph{Vitali equivalence classes} are equivalence classes of the real numbers under the relation $x\equiv y\leftrightarrow(\exists q\in \mathbb{Q})(x-y=q).)$. Kanovei\index{Author}{Kanovei} \cite{bib:1991}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 306.} The set of Vitali equivalence classes is linearly orderable. (\emph{Vitali equivalence classes} are equivalence classes of the real numbers under the relation $x\equiv y\leftrightarrow(\exists q\in \mathbb{Q})(x-y=q).)$. Kanovei \cite{bib:1991}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 307.} If $m$ is the cardinality of the set of Vitali equivalence classes, then $H(m)=H(2^{\aleph_{0}})$, where $H$ is Hartogs aleph function and the \emph{Vitali equivalence classes} are equivalence classes of the real numbers under the relation $x\equiv y\leftrightarrow(\exists q\in \mathbb{Q})(x-y=q)$. Kanovei \cite{bib:1991}.

\noindent \textbf{FORM 308($p$).} If $p$ is a prime and if $\{G_{y}:y\in Y\}$ is a set of finite groups, then the weak direct product $\prod_{y\in Y}G_{y}$ has a maximal $p$-subgroup. Howard/Yorke\index{Author}{Howard/Yorke} \cite{bib:1987} and note 24.

\textbf{[308 A($p$)]} If $p$ is a prime and if $Y$ is a set of non-empty, finite sets, then the weak direct product $\prod_{y\in Y}S_{y}$ has a maximal $p$-subgroup. $(S_{y}$ is the symmetric group on $y$.) Howard/Yorke \cite{bib:1987} and note 24.

\noindent \textbf{[308 B($p$)]} If $p$ is a prime and if $Y$ is a set of non-empty finite sets such that $(\forall y\in Y)(\gcd(|y|,p)=1)$, then $Y$ has a choice function. (This is similar to form $46(K)$, but in $46(K)$ the set $K$ is required to be finite.) Howard/Yorke \cite{bib:1987}.

\noindent \textbf{[308 C($p$)]} If $p$ is a prime and if $Y$ is a set of non-empty finite sets such that $(\forall y\in Y)(|y|\equiv 1\mod p)$, then $Y$ has a choice function. (This is similar to form $46(K)$, but in $46(K)$ the set $K$ is required to be finite.) Howard/Yorke \cite{bib:1987}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 309.} The Banach-Tarski Paradox: There are three finite partitions $\{P_{1},\,\ldots,\,P_{n}\}$, $\{Q_{1},\ldots, Q_{r}\}$ and $\{S_{1}, \ldots, S_{n}, T_{1}, \ldots, T_{r}\}$ of $B^{3}=\{x\in \mathbb{R}^{3}:|x|\leq 1\}$ such that $P_{i}$ is congruent to $S_{i}$ for $1\leq i\leq n$ and $Q_{i}$ is congruent to $T_{i}$ for $1\leq i\leq r$. Banach/Tarski\index{Author}{Banach/Tarski} \cite{bib:1924}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 310.} The Measure Extension Theorem: Suppose that $\mathcal{A}_{0}$ is a subring (that is, $a, b\in \mathcal{A}_{0}\rightarrow a\vee b\in \mathcal{A}_{0}$ and $a-b\in \mathcal{A}_{0})$ of a Boolean algebra $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mu$ is a measure on $\mathcal{A}_{0}$ (that is, $\mu : \mathcal{A}\rightarrow[0, \infty],\, \mu(a\vee b)=\mu(a)+\mu(b)$ for $a\wedge b=0$, and $\mu(0)=0.)$ then there is a measure on $\mathcal{A}$ that extends $\mu$. Wagon\index{Author}{Wagon} \cite{bib:1985}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 311.} Abelian groups are amenable. $(G$ is \emph{amenable} if there is a finitely additive measure $\mu$ on $\mathcal{P}(G)$ such that $\mu(G)=1$ and $\forall A\subseteq G,\,\forall g\in G,\,\mu(gA)=\mu(A).)$
Wagon \cite{bib:1985}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 312.} A subgroup of an amenable group is amenable. $(G$ is \emph{amenable} if there is a finitely additive measure $\mu$ on $\mathcal{P}(G)$ such that $\mu(G)=1$ and $\forall A\subseteq G,\,\forall g\in G,\,\mu(gA)=\mu(A).)$ Wagon \cite{bib:1985}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 313.} $\mathbb{Z}$ (the set of integers under addition) is amenable. $(G$ is \emph{amenable} if there is a finitely additive measure $\mu$ on $\mathcal{P}(G)$ such that $\mu(G)=1$ and $\forall A\subseteq G,\,\forall g\in G,\,\mu(gA)=\mu(A).)$ Wagon \cite{bib:1985}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 314.} Every permutation on a non-empty set can be expressed as a product of two reflections. (A reflection is a permutation $\phi$ such that $\phi^{2}$ is the identity.) Degen\index{Author}{Degen} \cite{bib:1988}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 315.} $\Omega=\omega_{1}$, where $\Omega=\{\alpha\in$ On: $(\forall\beta\leq\alpha)(\beta=0\vee(\exists\gamma)(\beta=\gamma+1)\vee$
there is a sequence $\langle\gamma_{n}: n\in \omega\rangle$ such that for each $n\ \gamma_{n}<\beta$ and $\beta=\bigcup_{n<\omega}\gamma_{n}$\} Gitik\index{Author}{Gitik} \cite{bib:1980}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 316.} If a linearly ordered set $(A, \leq)$ has the fixed point property then $(A, \leq)$ is complete. $((A, \leq)$ has the \emph{fixed point property} if every function $f:A\rightarrow A$ satisfying $(x\leq y\Rightarrow f(x)\leq f(y))$ has a fixed point, and $((A, \leq)$ is \emph{complete} if every subset of $A$ has a least upper bound.) H\"{o}ft/Howard\index{Author}{H\"{o}ft/Howard} \cite{bib:1994}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 317.} Weak Sikorski Theorem: If $B$ is a complete, well orderable Boolean algebra and $f$ is a homomorphism of the Boolean algebra $A^{\prime}$ into $B$ where $A^{\prime}$ is a subalgebra of the Boolean algebra $A$, then $f$ can be extended to a homomorphism of $A$ into $B$. Howard\index{Author}{Howard} \cite{bib:1973}.

[\textbf{317 A}] If $B$ is a complete, well orderable Boolean algebra and $A$ is a Boolean algebra of which $B$ is a subalgebra, then there is an ideal $I$ of $A$ satisfying $I\cap B =\{0\}$ and $I$ is maximal among those ideals $J$ of $A$ satisfying $J\cap B =\{0\}$. Howard \cite{bib:1973}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 318.} $\aleph_{1}$ is not measurable. Jech\index{Author}{Jech} \cite{bib:1968a} and note 20.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 319.} Measurable cardinals are inaccessible. Drake\index{Author}{Drake} \cite{bib:1974} and note 20.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 320.} No successor cardinal, $\aleph_{\alpha+1}$, is measurable. Drake \cite{bib:1974} and note 20.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 321.} There does not exist an ordinal $\alpha$ such that $\aleph_{\alpha}$ is weakly compact and $\aleph_{\alpha+1}$ is measurable. Bull\index{Author}{Bull} \cite{bib:1978} and note 20.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 322.}\index{Author}{Brunner} $KW(WO, \infty)$, The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a well ordered family of sets: For every well ordered set $X$ there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in M$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$. (See form 15). Kinna/Wagner \cite{bib:1955}, Brunner \cite{bib:1982a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 323.} $KW(\infty, WO)$, The Kinna-Wagner\index{Author}{Kinna/Wagner} Selection Principle for a family of well orderable sets: For every set $X$ of well orderable sets there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in X$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$. (See form 15.) Howard/A. Rubin/J. Rubin\index{Author}{Howard/A. Rubin/J. Rubin} \cite{bib:1997}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 324.}\index{Subject}{Sikorski's extension theorem} $KW(WO, WO)$, The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a well ordered family of well orderable sets: For every well ordered set $X$ of well orderable sets, there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in X$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$. (See form 15.) Howard/A. Rubin/J. Rubin \cite{bib:1997}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 325.} Ramsey's\index{Author}{Ramsey} Theorem II: $\forall n,\,m\in \omega$, if A is an infinite set and the family of all $m$ element subsets of $A$ is partitioned into $n$ sets $S_{j},\,1\leq j\leq n$, then there is an infinite subset $B\subseteq A$ such that all $m$ element subsets of $B$ belong to the same $S_{j}$. (Also, see form 17.) Ramsey \cite{bib:1929}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 326.} 2-SAT: Restricted Compactness Theorem for Propositional Logic III: If $\Sigma$ is a set of formulas in a propositional language such that every finite subset of $\Sigma$ is satisfiable and if every formula in $\Sigma$ is a disjunction of at most two literals, then $\Sigma$ is satisfiable. (A \emph{literal} is a propositional variable or its negation.) Wojtylak\index{Author}{Wojtylak}
\cite{bib:1995}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 327.} $KW(WO, <\aleph_{0})$, The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a well ordered family of finite sets: For every well ordered set $X$ of finite sets there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in X$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$. (See form 15.) Howard/A. Rubin/J. Rubin \cite{bib:1997}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 328.} $MC(WO, \infty)$: For every well ordered set $X$ such that for all $x\in X,\,|x|\geq 1$, there is a function $f$ such that and for every $x\in X,\,f(x)$ is a finite, non-empty subset of $x$. (See form 67.) Howard/A. Rubin/J. Rubin \cite{bib:1997}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 329.} $MC(\infty, WO)$: For every set $M$ of well orderable sets such that for all $x\in X,\,|x|\geq 1$, there is a function $f$ such that for every $x\in X,\,f(x)$ is a finite, non-empty subset of $x$. (See form 67.) Howard/A. Rubin/J. Rubin \cite{bib:1997}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 330.} $MC(WO, WO)$: For every well ordered set $X$ of well orderable sets such that for all $x\in X,\, |x|\geq 1$, there is a function $f$ such that for every $x\in X,\,f(x)$ is a finite, non-empty subset of $x$. (See form 67.) Howard/A. Rubin/J. Rubin \cite{bib:1997}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 331.} If $(X_{i})_{i\in I}$ is a family of compact non-empty topological spaces then there is a family $(F_{i})_{i\in I}$ such that $\forall i\in I,\,F_{i}$ is an irreducible closed subset of $X_{i}$. Morillon\index{Author}{Morillon} \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 332.} A product of non-empty compact sober topological spaces is nonempty. Morillon \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 333.} $MC(\infty, \infty, \mathrm{odd})$: For every set $X$ of sets such that for all $x\in X,\,|x|\geq 1$, there is a function $f$ such that for every $x\in X,\,f(x)$ is a finite, non-empty subset of $x$ and $|f(x)|$ is odd. Keremedis\index{Author}{Keremedis} \cite{bib:1996a}.

[\textbf{333 A}] In every vector space $B$ over the two element field, every subspace of $B$ has a complementary subspace. Keremedis \cite{bib:1996a}.

\noindent[\textbf{333 B}]\index{Subject}{Ramsey's theorem} Every quotient group of an Abelian group each of whose non-unit elements has order 2 has a set of representatives. Keremedis \cite{bib:1996a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 334.} $MC(\infty, \infty, \mathrm{even})$: For every set $X$ of sets such that for all $x\in X,\,|x|\geq 2$, there is a function $f$ such that for every $x\in X,\,f(x)$ is a finite, non-empty subset of $x$ and $|f(x)|$ is even. Keremedis\index{Author}{Keremedis} \cite{bib:1996a}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 335($n$).} Every quotient group of an Abelian group each of whose elements has order $\leq n$ has a set of representatives. Keremedis \cite{bib:1996c}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 336($n$).} (For $n\in \omega,\,n\geq 2.)$ For every infinite set $X$, there is an infinite $Y\subseteq X$ such that the set of all $n$-element subsets of $Y$ has a choice function. Note 111.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 337.} Every separable metric space is Lindel\"{o}f. Good/Tree\index{Author}{Good/Tree} \cite{bib:1995}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 338.} Every second countable metric space is Lindel\"{o}f. Good/Tree \cite{bib:1995}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 339.} Every second countable metric space is separable. Good/Tree \cite{bib:1995}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 340.} Every Lindel\"{o}f metric space is separable. Good/Tree \cite{bib:1995}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 341.} Every Lindel\"{o}f metric space is second countable. Good/Tree \cite{bib:1995}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 342($n$).} (For $n\in \omega, n\geq 2.)\ PC(\infty, n, \infty)$: Every infinite family of $n$-element sets has an infinite subfamily with a choice function. (See form 166.) Note 111.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 343.} A product of non-empty, compact $T_{2}$ topological spaces is non-empty. Morillon\index{Author}{Morillon} \cite{bib:1988}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 344.} If $(E_{i})_{i\in I}$ is a family of non-empty sets, then there is a family $(U_{i})_{i\in I}$ such that $\forall i\in I,\,U_{i}$ is an ultrafilter on $E_{i}$. Morillon \cite{bib:1988}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 345.} Rasiowa-Sikorski Axiom: If $(B, \wedge, \vee)$ is a Boolean algebra, $a$ is a non-zero element of $B$, and $\{X_{n}:n\in \omega\}$ is a denumerable set of subsets of $B$ then there is a maximal prime filter $F$ of $B$ such that $a\in F$ and for each $n\in \omega$, if $X_{n}\subseteq F$ and $\bigwedge X_{n}$ exists then $\bigwedge X_{n}\in F$. Morillon \cite{bib:1988}.

[\textbf{345 A}] Form 14 + form 43. Morillon \cite{bib:1988}.

\noindent[\textbf{345 B}] Form 14 + form 106. Morillon \cite{bib:1988}.

\noindent[\textbf{345 C}] Every bounded, distributive lattice has the strong Rasiowa-Sikorski property. Morillon \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{345 D}] Every bounded, distributive lattice has the Rasiowa-Sikorski property. Morillon \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent[\textbf{345 E}] Every Boolean algebra has the Rasiowa-Sikorski property. Morillon \cite{bib:1988} and note 71.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 346.} Vector Space Kinna-Wagner Principle: For every family $V=\{V_{i}:i\in K\}$ of non-trivial vector spaces there is a family $F=\{F_{i}:i\in K\}$ such that for each $i\in K,\,F_{i}$ is a non-empty, independent subset of $V_{i}$. Note 127.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 347.} Idemmultiple Partition Principle: If $y$ is idemmultiple $(2\times y\approx y)$ and $x\precsim^{\ast} y$, then $x\precsim y$. Higasikawa\index{Author}{Higasikawa} \cite{bib:1995} and note 69.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 348.} If $G$ is a group and $X$ and $Y$ both freely generate $G$ then $|X|=|Y|$. Federer/Jonsson \cite{bib:1950} and Howard \cite{bib:1985}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 349.}\index{Author}{Sierpi\'{n}ski} $MC(\infty, \aleph_{0})$: For every set $X$ of non-empty denumerable sets there is a function $f$ such that for all $x\in X,\,f(x)$ is a finite, non-empty subset of $x$.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 350.}\index{Subject}{Rasiowa-Sikorski property}\index{Author}{Federer/Jonsson}\index{Author}{Howard} $MC(\aleph_{0}, \aleph_{0})$: For every denumerable set $X$ of non-empty denumerable sets there is a function $f$ such that for all $x\in X,\,f(x)$ is a finite, non-empty subset of $x$. Keremedis\index{Author}{Keremedis} \cite{bib:1996d} and note 132.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 351.} A countable product of metrizable spaces is metrizable. Keremedis \cite{bib:1996d} and note 132.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 352.} A countable product of second countable spaces is second countable. Keremedis \cite{bib:1996d} and note 132.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 353.} A countable product of first countable spaces is first countable. Keremedis \cite{bib:1996d} and note 132.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 354.} A countable product of separable $T_{2}$ spaces is separable. Keremedis \cite{bib:1996d} and note 132.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 355.} $KW(\aleph_{0}, \infty)$, The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a denumerable family of sets: For every denumerable set $X$ there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in X$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 356.} $KW(\infty, \aleph_{0})$, The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a family of denumerable sets: For every set $X$ of denumerable sets there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in X$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 357.} $KW(\aleph_{0}, \aleph_{0})$, The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a denumerable family of denumerable sets: For every denumerable set $X$ of denumerable sets there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in X$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 358.} $KW(\aleph_{0}, <\aleph_{0})$, The Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle for a denumerable family of finite sets: For every denumerable set $X$ of finite sets there is a function $f$ such that for all $A\in X$, if $|A|>1$ then $\emptyset \neq f(A)\subsetneq A$.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 359.} If $\{A_{x}:x\in S\}$ and $\{B_{x}:x\in S\}$ are families of pairwise disjoint sets and $|A_{x}|\leq|B_{x}|$ for all $x\in S$, then $|\bigcup_{x\in S}A_{x}|\leq |\bigcup_{x\in S}B_{x}|$. Higasikawa\index{Author}{Higasikawa} \cite{bib:1995}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 360.} Every second countable topological space is Lindel\"{o}f. G. Moore\index{Author}{G. Moore} \cite{bib:1982} p 236.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 361.} In $\mathbb{R}$, the union of a denumerable number of analytic sets is analytic. G. Moore \cite{bib:1982}, pp 181 and 325.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 362.} In $\mathbb{R}$, every Borel set is analytic. G. Moore \cite{bib:1982}, pp 181 and 325.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 363.} There are exactly $2^{\aleph_{0}}$ Borel sets in $\mathbb{R}$. G. Moore \cite{bib:1982}, p 325.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 364.} In $\mathbb{R}$, there is a measurable set that is not Borel. G. Moore \cite{bib:1982}, p 325.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 365.} For every uncountable set $A$, if $A$ has the same cardinality as each of its uncountable subsets then $|A|=\aleph_{1}$. Sierpi\'{n}ski \cite{bib:1918}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 366.} There is a discontinuous function $f:\mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that for all real $x$ and $y,\,f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)$. Hamel\index{Author}{Hamel} \cite{bib:1905}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 367.} There is a Hamel basis for $\mathbb{R}$ as a vector space over $\mathbb{Q}$. Hamel \cite{bib:1905}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 368.} The set of all denumerable subsets of $\mathbb{R}$ has power $2^{\aleph_{0}}$. Sierpi\'{n}ski \cite{bib:1917}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 369.}\index{Author}{Sierpi\'{n}ski} If\index{Author}{Hamel} $\mathbb{R}$ is partitioned into two sets, at least one of them has cardinality $2^{\aleph_{0}}$. Luzin/Sierpi\'{n}ski\index{Author}{Luzin/Sierpi\'{n}ski} \cite{bib:1917}.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 370.} Weak Gelfand Extreme Point Theorem: If $A$ is a non-trivial Gelfand algebra then the closed unit ball in the dual of $A$ has an extreme point $e$. Morillon\index{Author}{Morillon} \cite{bib:1986}, notes 23 and 29.

[\textbf{370 A}] Measured Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem: If $\mathcal{B}$ is a Boolean algebra and there is a measure on $\mathcal{B}$ then there is an ultrafilter on $\mathcal{B}$. Morillon \cite{bib:1989}, \cite{bib:1990} and note 147.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 371.} There is an infinite, compact, Hausdorff, extremally disconnected topological space. Morillon \cite{bib:1993} and note 114.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 372.} Generalized Hahn-Banach Theorem: Assume that $X$ is a real vector space, $(Z,\preccurlyeq)$ is a Dedekind complete ordered vector space and $X_{0}$ is a subspace of $X$. If $\lambda_{0}:X_{0}\rightarrow Z$ is linear and $p:X\rightarrow Z$ is sublinear and if $\lambda_{0}\preccurlyeq p$ on $X_{0}$ then $\lambda_{0}$ can be extended to a linear map $\lambda:X\rightarrow Z$ such that $\lambda\preccurlyeq p$ on $X$. Schechter \cite{bib:1996b} and note 31.

[\textbf{372 A}] Existence of Banach Limits: For any directed set $(\Delta, \sqsubseteq)$ and any Dedekind complete ordered vector space $(Z,\preccurlyeq)$ there exists a $Z$-valued Banach limit. Schechter\index{Author}{Schechter} \cite{bib:1996b} and note 31.

\noindent[\textbf{372 B}] Generalized Convex Domination Theorem: For every real vector space $X$, every Dedekind complete ordered vector space $(Z, \preccurlyeq)$, every subspace $X_{0}\subseteq X$, every linear $\lambda_{0}:X_{0}\rightarrow Z$ and every convex $p:X\rightarrow Z$, if $\lambda_{0}\preccurlyeq p$ on $X_{0}$ then $\lambda_{0}$ can be extended to a linear map $\lambda:X\rightarrow Z$ such that $\lambda\preccurlyeq p$ on $X$. Schechter \cite{bib:1996b} and note 31.

\noindent[\textbf{372 C}] Generalized Support Theorem: For every real vector space $X$ and every Dedekind complete ordered vector space $(Z, \preccurlyeq)$, every convex function $p:X\rightarrow Z$ is a pointwise maximum of affine functions. Schechter \cite{bib:1996b} and note 31.

\noindent[\textbf{372 D}] Generalized Sandwich Theorem: For every real vector space $X$ and every Dedekind complete ordered vector space $(Z,\preccurlyeq)$, if $e:X\rightarrow Z$ is a concave function, $g:X\rightarrow Z$ is a convex function, and $e\leq g$ everywhere on $X$, then there exists an affine function $f:X\rightarrow Z$ satisfying $e\leq f\leq g$ everywhere on $X$. Schechter \cite{bib:1996b} and note 31.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 373($n$).} (For $n\in w, n\geq 2$.) $PC(\aleph_{0}, n, \infty)$: Every denumerable set of $n$-element sets has an infinite subset with a choice function.

\textbf{[373 A($n$)]} (For $n\in \omega, n\geq 2.)\ PC(WO, n, \infty)$: Every infinite well ordered set of $n$-element sets has an infinite subset with a choice function.

\noindent\textbf{[373 B($n$)]} $PUT(\aleph_{0}, n, \aleph_{0})$ for $n\in\omega -\{0,1\}$: The union of a denumerable set of pairwise disjoint $n$-element sets has a denumerable subset.

\noindent\textbf{[373 C($n$)]} $PUT(WO, n, WO)$ for $n\in w-\{0, 1\}$: The union of an infinite well ordered set of pairwise disjoint $n$-element sets has an infinite well ordered subset.

\noindent\textbf{FORM 374($n$).} $UT(\aleph_{0}, n, \aleph_{0})$ for $n\in \omega-\{0,1\}$: The union of a denumerable set of $n$-element sets is denumerable.

\textbf{[374 A($n$)]} For each $i,\,2\leq i\leq n\in\omega -\{0,1\}, C(\aleph_{0}, i)$: Every denumerable set of $i$-element sets has a choice function.
