$\mathcal{M}39(\kappa,\,\lambda)$: Kanovei's model II. This model depends on the two cardinals $\kappa <\lambda$ such that both $\kappa$ and $\lambda$ have cofinality $>\omega$ and neither $\kappa$ nor $\lambda$ can be written as $\theta^{+}$ where $\theta$ is a cardinal of countable cofinality and such that $\aleph_{2}\leq \kappa$.

Suppose $\kappa$ and $\lambda$ are cardinals in a model $\mathcal{M}$ of ZFC + V = L. Assume that $\kappa$ and $\lambda$ satisfy the properties of the preceding paragraph in $\mathcal{M}$. Let $P=\{p:p$ is a function such that $\mathrm{dom}(p)\subseteq\lambda\times \omega$ is finite and $\mathrm{ran}(p)\subseteq\{0, 1\}\}$ and let $G$ be $P$ generic over $M$. For each $\zeta <\lambda$, let $a_{\zeta}(k)=i$ if and only if $(\exists p\in G)(p(\zeta,\,k)=i)$. $a_{\zeta}$ is a function from $\omega$ to $\{0, 1\}$ which we identify with a real number between 0 and 1 whose binary expansion has digits $a_{\zeta}(0), a_{\zeta}(1), a_{\zeta}(2),\ldots$ and use $[a_{\zeta}]$ to denote the Vitali equivalence class of this real number. (Vitali equivalence classes are equivalence classes or real numbers under the relation $x\equiv y\leftrightarrow(\exists q\in \mathbb{Q})(x-y=q).)$ Now define the following
\begin{enumerate}
\item[1.] $B=\{b\in\mathcal{M}:b$ is a bijection from $\lambda$ onto $\lambda$\}.
\item[2.] $Z=\{z\subseteq\lambda\times \omega:z$ is finite\}
\item[3.] For $b\in B,\,z\in Z$ and $\zeta <\lambda\ za_{\zeta}(k)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}
    a_{\zeta}(k) & \mathrm{for}\,(\zeta,\,k)\not\in z\\
    1-a_{\zeta}(k) & \mathrm{for}\,(\zeta,\,k)\in z \end{array}\right.$
\item[4.] $zb\,|\,u=\langle za_{b(\zeta)}:\zeta \in u\rangle$
\item[5.] $|zb\,|\,u|=\langle|za_{b(\zeta)}|:\zeta \in u\rangle$
\item[6.] $C_{\theta}=\{u\subseteq\lambda:u\in \mathcal{M}$ has cardinality $<\theta$ in $\mathcal{M}$\}
\item[7.] $W_{\kappa}=\{zb\,|\,u:z\in Z\wedge b\in B\wedge u\in C_{\kappa}\}$
\item[8.] $[W_{\lambda}]=\{|zb\,|\,u|:z\in Z \wedge b\in B\wedge u\in C_{\lambda}\}$
\end{enumerate}

The model $\mathcal{M}39(\kappa,\,\lambda)$ is HOD$(W_{\kappa}\cup[W_{\lambda}]\cup\{W_{\kappa},\,[W_{\lambda}]\})$. In Kanovei \cite{bib:1991} it is shown that the Principle of Dependent Choices (43) is true and that $H(2^{\aleph_{0}})< H(m)$ where $m$ is the cardinality of the set of Vitali equivalence classes and $H$ is Hartogs' function (307 is false). $(H(x)$ is the smallest ordinal that is not similar to a subset of $x$.) Since 43 implies 8 $(C(\aleph_{0},\,\infty))$, it follows from Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1982a} that in this model there is a set that cannot be well ordered and does not have an infinite Dedekind finite subset, (163 is false). (Form 8 plus form 163 iff AC.)

$\mathcal{M}39(\kappa,\,\lambda)\models$ 43 but 91, 163, and 307 are false. References Kanovei \cite{bib:1991}, Brunner \cite{bib:1982a}, and note 18.

$\mathcal{M}40(\kappa)$: Pincus' Model IV. The ground model $\mathcal{M}$, is a model of ZF + the class form of AC. In $\mathcal{M},\,\kappa$ is a regular cardinal larger than $\aleph_{0}$ such that $2^{\kappa}=\kappa^{+}$. Pincus\index{Author}{Pincus} constructs a generic extension of $\mathcal{M}$ using $\kappa^{+}$ generic iterations. To assure that all the sets added in this manner have canonical supports, he enumerates the sets at each level using hereditarily almost disjoint sets. (See Pincus \cite{bib:1977a} p 125 for definitions.) The construction is made is such a way that at each level DC (43) holds, but AC does not. In Pincus \cite{bib:1977a} it is shown that in this model, every set can be linearly ordered (30 is true), $C(\infty,\,WO)$ (60) is true; and for all $\aleph_{\alpha}<\kappa,\,\mathrm{DC}(\aleph_{\alpha})\ (87(\alpha))$ is true. Pincus \cite{bib:1977b} proves that the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem (14) is also true. Since 87 implies 8 $(C(\aleph_{0},\,\infty))$, it follows from Brunner \cite{bib:1982a} that in this model there is a set that cannot be well ordered and does not have an infinite Dedekind finite subset, (163 is false). (Form 8 plus form 163 iff AC.) Form 14 implies 49 (Every partial ordering can be extended to a linear ordering.) and 49 + 51 (Every linear ordering has a cofinal sub well ordering.) iff AC. (See Morris\index{Author}{Morris} \cite{bib:1969} and note 121.) Thus, form 51 is false. Since form 30 is true and form $87(\alpha)$ implies form 296 (Every infinite set is the disjoint union of infinitely many infinite sets.), it follows from Pincus \cite{bib:1997} that form 295 (Every infinite set has a dense linear ordering.) is true. Since 43 + 14 is equivalent to 345 ([345 A]), form 345 is true.

$\mathcal{M}40(\kappa)\models$ 14, 30, 43, 60, 87$(\alpha)$ for $\aleph_{\alpha}<\kappa$, 165, 295, and 345, but 51, 91, 144, 152, 163, 253, and 286 are false. References Pincus \cite{bib:1977a}, \cite{bib:1977b}, \cite{bib:1997}, Brunner \cite{bib:1982a}, Morris \cite{bib:1969}, notes 18, 120(26, 28, 34, 43, and 45) and 121.

$\mathcal{M}41$ Kanovei's Model III. Let $\mathbb{P}$ be the set of conditions from the model in Jensen\index{Author}{Jensen} \cite{bib:1968}. $\mathbb{P}$ is a subset of the set of all constructible perfect trees. $\mathcal{M}41$ is the symmetric part of $L[\boldsymbol{\alpha}]$ where $\boldsymbol{\alpha}=\langle\alpha_{n}: n\in\omega\rangle$ is $\mathbb{P}^{w}$ generic. In Kanovei\index{Author}{Kanovei} \cite{bib:1976} it is shown that there is a $\varPi_{2}^{1}$ subset $P$ of $\omega \times{^{\omega}\omega}$ with dom $P=\omega$ and for which no sequence $\langle x_{n}:n\in\omega\rangle$ with $\langle k,\,x_{k}\rangle\in P$ for all $k\in \omega$ exists (form 194 is false).

In $\mathcal{M}41$, form 194 is false. Reference Kanovei \cite{bib:1976}.

$\mathcal{M}42$ Bull's Model. Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a countable transitive model of ZFC + ``There are uncountable regular cardinals $\aleph_{\alpha}<\aleph_{\beta}<\aleph_{\gamma}$ such that $\aleph_{\alpha}$ is $\aleph_{\gamma}$-supercompact; $\aleph_{\beta}$ is the first measurable cardinal greater than $\aleph_{\alpha}$; and $\aleph_{\gamma}=|2^{\aleph_{\beta}}|.$'' Using backward Easton forcing (which is due to Silver), Bull constructs a generic extension of $\mathcal{M}$. Then using collapsing functions, he constructs an inner model, $\mathcal{M}42$, in which $\aleph_{\beta}$ is collapsed to $\aleph_{\alpha+1}$. He proves that $\aleph_{\alpha}$ is an uncountable, weakly compact cardinal and $\aleph_{\alpha+1}$ is measurable (321 is false). Bull\index{Author}{Bull} also proves that $C(\aleph_{\alpha},\,\infty)$ (86) is true in this model. Since $\alpha\geq 1$, form 39 $(C(\aleph_{1},\,\infty))$ is also true. Form 163 (Every set is either well orderable or has an infinite Dedekind finite subset.) is false because 39 implies 8 and 8 + 163 implies AC (Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1982a}).

$\mathcal{M}42 \models$ 39 and 86, but 91, 163, and 321 are false. References Bull \cite{bib:1978}, Brunner \cite{bib:1982a}, notes 18 and 20.

\section{Fraenkel-Mostowski Models, Models of $\mathrm{ZF}^{0}\ (\mathcal{N})$}\label{pt03:sec02}\index{Subject}{Fraenkel-Mostowski (FM) models}

The models we give here are all permutation models (FM models) of $\mathrm{ZF}^{0}.$ We shall describe the models by specifying the set $A$ of urelements\index{Subject}{urelements} (or atoms)\index{Subject}{atoms} in the ground model; the group of permutations, $\mathcal{G}$ of $A$; and the set of supports\index{Subject}{supports}, $S$, an ideal of subsets of $A$. (On occasion, we shall give a filter of subgroups of $\mathcal{G}$ rather than $S$. See, for example, Jech\index{Author}{Jech} \cite{bib:1973b}, Chapter 4, for details.)

In all the models of $\mathrm{ZF}^{0}$ given below all the standard properties of the reals are true, PW (91) (The power set of a well ordered set can be well ordered.) is true, but the Axiom of Choice is false and the Kinna-Wagner Principle (15) is false. Blass\index{Author}{Blass} \cite{bib:1979} has shown that in every permutation model with a set of atoms there is a set $X$ such that for each set $a$ there is an ordinal $\alpha$ and a function $f$ mapping $X\times\alpha$ onto $a$ (191 is true). Blass also shows that form 192 (For every set $A$ there is a projective set $X$ and a function $f$ mapping $A$ onto $X$.) + 191 implies AC, so 192 is false in every permutation model with a set of atoms. (See notes 59 and 60.) Thus, each of the following is true in each model: 5, 6, 11, 12, 13, 35, 36, 37, 38, 70, 73, 74, 79, 91, 92, 93, 94, 108, 130, 142, 145, 169, 170, 194, 197, 199, 203, 206, 211, 212, 222, 223, 251, 252, 272, 273, 280, 289, 305, 306, 307, 309, 313, 361, 362, 363, 364, 366, 367, 368, and 369. (Each one of these 53 forms is implied by one of the following 16 forms: 6, 11, 37, 73, 91, 92, 130, 273, 305, 309, 313, 361, 363, 368, 369.) However, 15 is false in each permutation model. In addition, 182, 189, 190, and 191 are true in every permutation model in which the class of atoms is a set and 192 is false in all such models.

Many of the results obtained for $\mathrm{ZF}^{0}$ models can be transferred to ZF models because of the work of Jech/Sochor\index{Author}{Jech/Sochor} \cite{bib:1966a}, \cite{bib:1966b}, and Pincus\index{Author}{Pincus} \cite{bib:1971}, \cite{bib:1972a}, \cite{bib:1974c}, \cite{bib:1977a}. (See note 103 for a summary of the transfer results.) If a result is transferable\index{Subject}{transferable}, one of the numerals 3 or 4 will occur in the appropriate position in Table 1. In the corresponding place in part V, REFERENCES FOR RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN FORMS, we will give the $\mathrm{ZF}^{0}$ model with a ``T'' following its number. (The following subset of the above list of forms that are true in every permutation model are boundable statements so they are transferable: 5, 6, 11, 12, 13, 35, 36, 37, 38, 70, 73, 74, 79, 92, 93, 94, 130, 142, 169, 170, 194, 197, 199, 203, 206, 211, 212, 222, 223, 251, 252, 272, 273, 280, 289, 305, 306, 307, 309, and 313. (Each one of these 42 forms is implied by one of the following 12 forms: 6, 11, 37, 73, 92, 130, 170, 273, 305, 309, 313.) In addition, the following forms are transferable: 8, 9, 10, 14, 18, 17, 30, 31, 32, 39, 40, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 48, 52, 60, 61, 64, 71, 80, 82, 83, 85, 86, 87, 88, 98, 119, 120, 121, 122, 123, 128, 132, 163, 165, 166, 178, 185, 213, 216, 217, 250, 295, 336, 342, 350, 357, 358, 373, 374, 376, 377, and 378. See note 103.) Since the lists of forms given above occur in note 18, we shall give a reference to that note when, in the description of a model, we assert that one of the forms listed above is true (or false) in the model.

Also, there are several implications involving more than two forms that are known to hold in $\mathrm{ZF}^{0}.$ These are listed with references in note 120. Most are of the form A + B implies C, where A, B, and C are form numbers. When it follows from these implications that a certain form is true or false in a model we will, in the description of the model, assert that the form is true (or false) and give a reference to the appropriate part of note 120.

Finally, in note 2 we give a list of implications which hold in every FM model and involve more than two forms. When the truth of falsity of a form in an FM model follows from one of these, we shall refer to the relevant part of note 2.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}1$: The Basic Fraenkel Model. The set of atoms, $A$ is denumerable; $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations on $A$; and $S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. In $\mathcal{N}1,\,A$ is infinite, but neither $A$ nor $\mathcal{P}(A)$ have a denumerable subset (9 and 82 are false); $A$ is amorphous (64 is false); $|A|^{2}\not\leq 2^{|A|}$ (53 is false); and $MC_{\omega}(\aleph_{0},\,\infty)$ (131) is false because if $F_{n}$ is the set of all $n$-element subsets of $A$, then $\{F_{n}:n\in\omega\}$ has no countable multiple choice function. However, $A$ (Antichain Condition 89) is true; the Weak Ultra Filter Principle (63) is true, but the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem (14) is false; Ramsey's Theorem (17) is true; every set that cannot be well ordered has an infinite subset in one-to-one correspondence with a subset of $A$ (133 is true) (Blass\index{Author}{Blass} \cite{bib:1977a}); there is a free group that has a subgroup that is not free (68 is false); and there is a field that does not have an algebraic closure (69 is false). (See L\"{a}uchli\index{Author}{Lauchli@L\"{a}uchli} \cite{bib:1962} and Jech\index{Author}{Jech} \cite{bib:1973b} p145ff for these last two results.) Also, AC for a set of pairs (88) is false.

In Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1984b} it is shown that 17 + 133 implies 134, so 134 is true. It is shown in note 123 that 133 implies 231 $(UT(WO,\,WO,\,WO))$. In every FM model 231 implies 23 $((\forall\alpha)UT(\aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha}))$. It follows that 23 is also true. It is shown in note 88 that the Countable Union Theorem (31) is true. Brunner \cite{bib:1984b} has shown that an amorphous power of a compact $T_{2}$ space is compact (127 is true) and that if $X$ is a $T_{2}$ space with at least two points and $X^{Y}$ is hereditarily metacompact, then $Y$ is countable (135 is true). Also, in this paper, Brunner shows that the Baire Category Theorem for compact Hausdorff spaces (106) is false (127 + 106 implies 64). In Howard/Rubin\index{Author}{Howard/Rubin} \cite{bib:1977} it is shown that $MC(\infty,\,LO)$ (112) is true, but $MC(LO,\,\infty)$ (292) is false. Brunner \cite{bib:1985a} shows that a product of weakly Loeb $T_{2}$-spaces is weakly Loeb (115 is true) and that every compact $T_{2}$-space is weakly Loeb (116 is true). In Brunner \cite{bib:1983d} it is shown that there is a $T_{2}$-space $X$ which is $F$ (a continuous finite-to-one image of an $A_{1}$-space), but not $A_{1}$ (for every open covering $O$ of $X$ there is a mapping $f:X\rightarrow O$ such that for each $x\in X,\,x\in f(x))$ (146 is false) and also that every $T_{2}$ topological space can be covered by a well ordered family of discrete sets (147 is true). Brunner \cite{bib:1984f} shows that in this model there is an infinite $T_{2}$-space which does not have an infinite set of non-isolated points (128 is false). (Note that the statement that $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R})$ can be well ordered (130) is true in every model of $\mathrm{ZF}^{0}$.)

Brunner \cite{bib:1981a} shows that the box product $\mathbb{R}^{A}$ is metrizable and connected (177 is false). (See note 52.) Dawson/Howard show that $|A!|$ and $|2^{A}|$ are incomparable (200 is false). (See note 64.) Hickman proves that in this model it is not possible to construct a binary operation on $A$ which makes $A$ a group (239 is false). Stavi proves that there exist an infinite, free, complete Boolean algebra on $A$(267 is false). (See note 89 for definitions.) Hodges proves that if $R$ is the polynomial ring over $A$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Q}$ then $R$ is an integral domain such that every ideal in $R$ is finitely generated, but $R$ has no maximal proper ideal (278 is false). It is shown in Harper/Rubin that in this model every set on which there is a relation $R$ which is anti-symmetric and connected has a maximal subset on which $R$ is transitive (263 is true). In Brunner \cite{bib:1985a} it is shown that in this model for $T_{2}$ spaces, $A$-bounded is equivalent to weakly Loeb (114 is true). In this model, every infinite partially ordered set has either an infinite chain or an infinite antichain (217 is true). (See note 105.)

In note 41 we show that in $\mathcal{N}1$ algebraic closures of fields are unique when they exist (233 is true). In note 116 we show that in $\mathcal{N}1$ every $\mathrm{T}_{2}$ topological space contains an infinite subset which has no infinite compact subsets (304) is true. In note 66 we show that $KW(WO,\,\infty)$ (322) is true. (This result also appears in Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1982a}, Proposition 4.5.) The set of all finite subsets of $A$ that have at least two elements is a set of well orderable sets for which there is no Kinna-Wagner selection function. Therefore, $KW(\infty,\,WO)$ (323) is false. Ramsey's Theorem II (325) is true (see note 46). Form 40 $(C(WO,\,\infty))$ is false because 40 implies 64 and form 122 $(C(WO,\,<\aleph_{0}))$ is true because 133 implies 122. Therefore, form 328 $(MC(WO,\,\infty))$ is false because 122 + 328 $\rightarrow$ 40. De la Cruz and Di Prisco have shown that every infinite collection of non-empty well orderable sets has an infinite subfamily with a choice function (380 is true). It is shown in Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley\index{Author}{Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Stanley} \cite{bib:1997} that form 232 (Every metric space $(X, d)$ has a $\sigma$-discrete basis.) is true. Since form 165 $(C(WO,\,WO))$ is true, (133 implies 165) it follows from note 2(8 and 9) that 16 and 24 are also true.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}2$: The Second Fraenkel Model. $A=\{a_{i}:i\in\omega\}$. Let $B=\{\{a_{2i},\,a_{2i+1}\}:i\in \omega\}$. $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of permutations on $A$ that leaves $B$ point-wise fixed. $S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. In $\mathcal{N}2$, MC (67) is true. (In fact, $MC(\infty,\,\infty,$ even) (334) is true. See note 93.) However, the set $B$ is a denumerable set of pairs that has no choice function $(C(\aleph_{0},2)$, form 80 is false) and has no Kinna-Wagner selection function $(KW(\aleph_{0},\, <\aleph_{0})$, form 358, is false). $A$ is infinite, but has no countably infinite subset (9 is false); $B$ does have a countably infinite subset (98 is false), but $\bigcup B$ does not (18 is false); the Hahn-Banach Theorem (52) and the Krein-Milman Theorem (65) are true, but the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem (14) is false.

It also follows from results of Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1984b} that in $\mathcal{N}2$, there is a compact $T_{2}$ topological space $X$ such that $X^{\omega}$ is not compact, thus 154 is false. (See note 95.) Brunner \cite{bib:1982a} shows that in this model every set that cannot be well ordered has an infinite Dedekind finite subset (163 is true). Howard\index{Author}{Howard} proves that Rado's Selection Lemma (99) is true. Hickman\index{Author}{Hickman} proves that the only subsets of $A$ that can be linearly ordered are finite, but $A$ has no amorphous subset (198 is false). However, no infinite set in this model is $T$ finite (83 is true). (See note 105.) The set of all $n$-element subsets of $A$ has no choice function for each $n\geq 2\ (45(n)$ is false).

Since 106 (the Baire Category Theorem for compact Hausdorff spaces) is true (67 implies 106) and 43 (Dependent Choices) is false (43 implies 18), it follows that the Tychonoff Theorem for countably many $T_{2}$ spaces (154) is false because it is shown in Brunner \cite{bib:1983c} that 106 + 154 implies 43. Form 130 $(\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R})$ is well orderable.) is true in every FM model, 18 is false in $\mathcal{N}2$, and Brunner \cite{bib:1984f} has shown that 130 + 128 (On every infinite set there is a $T_{2}$ topology with an infinite set of non-isolated points.) implies 18. Thus, 128 must be false in $\mathcal{N}2$.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}2(n)$: A generalization of $\mathcal{N}2$. This is a generalization of $\mathcal{N}2$ in which there is a denumerable set of $n$ element sets for $n\in \omega-\{0, 1\}$. $A=\bigcup B$, where $B$ is a set of pairwise disjoint $n$ element sets $b_{i}$ with $i\in\omega$; $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations that leave $B$ point-wise fixed $(\phi(b_{i})=b_{i}$ for each $i\in\omega)$; and $S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. In this model, the Axiom of Multiple Choice (67) is true, but $C(WO,\,n)\ (47(n))$, $C(\aleph_{0},\,n)\ (288(n))$ and $PC(\aleph_{0},\,n,\,\infty)\ (373(n))$ are false. Let $K$ be a non-empty set of positive integers, then for $n\in K,\,C(\infty,\,K)$ is false. For $n\in K$, we shall denote $C(\infty,\,K)$ by $46(n\in K)$.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}2^{\ast}(3)$: Howard's\index{Author}{Howard} variation\index{Author}{Fraenkel} of $\mathcal{N}2(3)$. $A=\bigcup B$, where $B$ is a set of pairwise disjoint 3 element sets, $T_{i}=\{a_{i},\,b_{i},\,c_{i}\}$. For each $i\in\omega$ define a function $\eta_{i}:T_{i}\rightarrow T_{i}$ such that $\eta_{i}:a_{i}\mapsto b_{i}\mapsto c_{i}$. $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations $\phi$ of $A$ such that for each $i\in \omega,\,\phi|T_{i}$ is either the identity, $\eta_{i}$, or $\eta_{i}^{2}$. $S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. In this model, $B$ is a denumerable set of triples that has no choice function and has no Kinna-Wagner selection function so $(\forall n\in \omega-\{0, 1\})C(\aleph_{0},\,n)$ (288) is false and $KW(\aleph_{0},\,<\aleph_{0})$ (358) is false. (Since the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem (14) implies 288, form 14 is also false.) Howard shows that if $P$ is any set of pairs in the model and $R$ is a symmetric relation on $\bigcup P$ such that every finite subset of $P$ has an $R$-consistent choice function, (A choice function $f$ on $X$ is $R$-consistent if for all $u,\,v\in X,\,u\neq v$ implies $f(u)Rf(v)$.) then $P$ has an $R$-consistent choice function (141 is true). It is shown in note 93 that $MC(\infty,\,\infty,\mathrm{odd})$ (333) is true. Keremedis\index{Author}{Keremedis} \cite{bib:1996a} proves that $333 + 334(MC(\infty,\,\infty,\mathrm{even})$ iff AC, so 334 is false.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}2(n,\,M)$: Mostowski's variation of $\mathcal{N}2(n)$. $A,\,B$, and $S$ are the same as in $\mathcal{N}2(n)$. In this model, $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations of $A$ such that for each $\phi \in \mathcal{G},\, \phi(b_{i})=b_{i}$ (as in $\mathcal{N}2(n)$), but in addition $\phi$ is different from the identity on $b_{i}$ for at most a finite number of $i\in\omega$. Let $K$ be a non-empty set of positive integers. The condition $M(K,\, n)$ holds if for every decomposition of $n$ into a sum of primes, $n=p_{1}+p_{2}+\cdots+p_{m}$, there is a sequence of $m$ non-negative integers, $q_{1},\,q_{2},\,\cdots,\,q_{m}$, such that $p_{1}q_{1}+p_{2}q_{2}+\cdots+p_{m}q_{m}\in K$. Mostowski proves that $C(\infty,\,K)$ (46) is true in this model if $M(K,\,n)$ is false. We shall denote $C(\infty,\,K)$ by $46(\neg M)$ when condition $M(K,\,n)$ is false. Also, it is clear that $C(WO,\,n)\ (47(n))$ and $C(\infty,\,K)\ (46(n\in K))$ are false in this model.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}2(\aleph_{\alpha})$: Jech's Model. This is an extension of $\mathcal{N}2$ in which $A=\{a_{\gamma}:\gamma\in \omega_{\alpha}\}$; $B$ is the corresponding set of $\aleph_{\alpha}$ pairs of elements of $A$; $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations on $A$ that leave $B$ point-wise fixed; and $S$ is the set of all subsets of $A$ of cardinality less than $\aleph_{\alpha}$. $(\mathcal{N}2(\aleph_{0})$ is $\mathcal{N}2$.) If $\aleph_{\alpha}$ is regular and $\alpha>1$, then $DC(\omega_{1})$ (44) is true in this model; and if $\alpha>\beta$, then $DC(\omega_{\beta})\ (87(\beta))$ is true. (Therefore, the Principle of Dependent Choices (DC, 43) is true if $\alpha>0$.) On the other hand, $C(WO,\,<\aleph_{0})$ (122) is false for all $\alpha\geq 0,\,C(\infty,\,n)$ (45$(n)$ and 88) is false for each $n\geq 2$ and $\alpha\geq 0$, and $KW(WO,\,<\aleph_{0})$ (327) is false for all $\alpha\geq 0$.

Since BPI (14) implies 88, 14 is also false. Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1982a} has shown that for all $\alpha>0$ there is a set that cannot be well ordered and does not have an infinite Dedekind finite subset (163 is false) because 44 implies 8 $(C(\aleph_{0},\,\infty))$ and 8 plus 163 iff AC. Also, Jech\index{Author}{Jech} (\cite{bib:1973b}, p 132, prob 5) notes that if $\alpha\geq 1$, since there is a non-trivial ultrafilter on $\omega$ (70 is true) and every infinite set has a countably infinite subset (9 is true), the weak ultrafilter principal (63) is true. Form 44 implies forms 39 $(C(\aleph_{1},\,\infty))$ and 41 (Every cardinal is comparable with $\aleph_{1}$.). van Douwen\index{Author}{Douwen} \cite{bib:1980} has shown that 39 + 41 implies 135 (If $X$ is a $T_{2}$ space with at least two points and $X^{Y}$ is hereditarily metacompact, then $Y$ is countable.). Therefore, form 135 is also true. Blass\index{Author}{Blass} \cite{bib:1979} has shown that 191 (There is a set $X$ such that for each set $a$ there is an ordinal $\alpha$ and a function $f$ mapping $X\times\alpha$ onto $a$.) is true in every permutation model with a set of atoms. He has also shown that 8 $(C(\aleph_{0},\,\infty)) +191+193$ (Every Abelian group is a homomorphic image of a free projective Abelian group.) iff AC. Thus, form 193 must be false if $\aleph_{\alpha}$ is regular and $\alpha>1$. (See note 60 for definitions.) It follows from note 104 that the $2m=m$ principle (3) is false in this model.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}2(\mathrm{LO}):$ van Douwen's Model. This model is another variation of $\mathcal{N}2$. The set of atoms, $A=\bigcup_{n\in \omega}B_{n}$ where the $B_{n}$'s are pairwise disjoint sets each of which is ordered like the integers, $\mathbb{Z}$. $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations which fix each $B_{n}$ and also preserve the ordering on each $B_{n},\,n\in\omega$. $S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. In $\mathcal{N}2(\mathrm{LO})$, $\{B_{n}:n\in\omega\}$ is a denumerable set of sets each of which is ordered like $\mathbb{Z}$ which has no choice function, so form 119 is false.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}3$: Mostowski's Linearly Ordered Model. $A$ is countably infinite; $\precsim$ is a dense linear ordering on $A$ without first or last elements $((A,\,\precsim)\cong(\mathbb{Q},\,\leq));\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all order automorphisms on $(A,\,\precsim)$; and $S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. In $\mathcal{N}3,\, PW$ (91) is true, but LW (90) is false. The set $A$ is infinite, but neither $A$ nor $\mathcal{P}(A)$ have a countably infinite subset (9 and 82 are false); every $T$ finite set is finite (83 is true); $A$ is not $T$ finite, but $\mathcal{P}(A)$ is Dedekind finite (84 is false); every set can be linearly ordered (30 is true); the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem (14) is true; AC for a family of well orderable sets (60) is true; the Cardinal Representative Theorem (97) is false; and the Baire category theorem for compact Hausdorff spaces (106) is false. Also, $MC_{\omega}(\aleph_{0},\,infty)$ (131) is false because if $F_{n}$ is the set of all $n$-element subsets of $A$, then $\{F_{n}:n\in\omega\}$ has no countable multiple choice function.

It is shown in note 88 that the Countable Union Theorem (31) is true. Form 23 is true because 60 implies $UT(WO,\,WO,\,WO)$ (231) and, in every FM model, 231 implies $(\forall\alpha)UT(\aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha})$ (23). Brunner \cite{bib:1984c} has shown that there does exist an infinite connected compact P-space (125 is false) and in Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1982a} it is shown that every infinite set that cannot be well ordered has an infinite subset with a Dedekind finite power set (164 is true). In Brunner \cite{bib:1983a} it is shown that in $\mathcal{N}3$ there is a non-trivial L\"{a}uchli continuum (155 is false), there are two compact $T_{2}$ spaces which have isomorphic rings of real valued continuous functions, but are not homeomorphic (156 is false), and there is a compact $T_{2}$, space, $X$, with the property that every non-empty subset of $C(X)$ (the set of continuous real valued functions on $X$) which is point-wise bounded has a supremum, but $X$ is not extremely disconnected (the closure of every open set is open) (157 is false). In Brunner \cite{bib:1983d} it is shown that if $a,\,b\in A,\,a\prec b$, then the closed interval $[a,\, b]$ is a compact $T_{2}$ space that cannot be covered by a well ordered set of discrete sets (147 is false). Dawson/Howard show that $|A!|>|2^{A}|$ (200 is false), and since it is clear that $|A!|\leq|A^{A}|$, 290 is false. (See note 64).

Gonzalez has shown that there is an infinite set in $\mathcal{N}3$ which does not have a dense linear ordering in $\mathcal{N}3$ (295 is false). Since form 295 is false and 30 is true it follows from Pincus\index{Author}{Pincus} \cite{bib:1997} that form 296 (Every infinite set is the disjoint union of infinitely many infinite sets.) is false. (30 + 296 implies 295.) Using the fact that the Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle (15) is false and that the Ordering Principle (30) is true, Krom proves that there is an ordered topological space that is not normal (118 is false). Brunner \cite{bib:1985c} comments that the order topology on $A$ is $T_{2}$ and each infinite subset of $A$ contains a closed interval which is compact (304 is false). In Brunner \cite{bib:1982a}, it is shown that in this model, every set is either well orderable or contains a copy of sub-intervals of $A$. It is noted in Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1984f} that an interval with the order-topology is a $T$-2 space with an infinite number of non-isolated points so it follows that form 128 is true. Howard\index{Author}{Howard} \cite{bib:1973} has shown that in every FM model 14 implies the Weak Sikorski Theorem (317), so 317 is true,

For each $i\in\omega-\{0\}$, let $c_{i}$ be the set of all $i$-element subsets of $A$. Then the set $\{c_{i}:i\in \omega-\{0\}\}$ is a denumerable set that has no multiple choice function $(MC(\aleph_{0},\, \infty)$ (126) is false) and no Kinna-Wagner Selection function $(KW(\aleph_{0},\,\infty)$ (355) is false). It is shown in Howard/Keremedis/Rubin/Rubin \cite{bib:1997b} that form 381 (DUM) is true. Since form 165 $(C(WO,\,WO))$ is true, (60 implies 165) it follows from note 2(8 and 9) that 16 and 24 are also true.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}4$: The Mathias/Pincus Model I. $A$ is countably infinite; $\precsim$ is a universal homogeneous partial ordering on $A$ (See Jech \cite{bib:1973b} p 101 for definitions.); $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all order automorphisms on $(A,\,\precsim)$; and $S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. In $\mathcal{N}4$, every linearly ordered set can be well ordered (90) is true but the Antichain Principle (89) is false. There are no amorphous sets (64 is true) and the set of atoms is an infinite $T$ finite set (83 is false). (See note 105.) Since form 64 is true and AC is false, form 133 (Every set is either well orderable or has an infinite amorphous subset.) is false. The set of atoms with the discrete topology is a $T_{2}$-space which is not weakly Loeb (114 is false). Since form 118 (Every orderable topological space is normal.) is true (90 implies 118), it follows from Krom \cite{bib:1986} that not every set can be linearly ordered (30 is false). (The Kinna-Wagner Principle (15) is false in every FM model and Krom proves that $\neg 15+30\rightarrow\neg 118$.)

\noindent $\mathcal{N}5$: The Mathias/Pincus Model II (an extension of $\mathcal{N}4$). $A$ is countably infinite, $\precsim$ and $\leq$ are universal homogeneous partial and linear orderings, respectively, on $A$, (See Jech \cite{bib:1973b} p 101 for definitions.); $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all order automorphisms on $(A,\precsim,\,\leq)$; and $S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. In $\mathcal{N}5,\precsim$ cannot be extended to a linear ordering on $A$ (49 is false), but every set can be linearly ordered (30 is true). Also, the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem (14) is false. Since 30 is true, a set is $T$ finite iff it is finite (Levy\index{Author}{Levy} \cite{bib:1958}), so $A$ is not $T$ finite, but $\mathcal{P}(A)$ is Dedekind finite (84 is false). ($T$ finite is equivalent to II-finite from note 94.) Using the fact that the Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle (15) is false and that the Ordering Principle (30) is true, Krom\index{Author}{Krom} proves that there is an ordered topological space that is not normal (118 is false). Since form 14 is false and form 30 implies form 62 $(C(\infty,\,<\aleph_{0}))$, Blass has shown that Rado's Selection Principle (99) is false. (See note 33 for the proof that 62 + 99 implies 14.) Howard\index{Author}{Howard} \cite{bib:1973} has shown that in every FM model, 62 implies 60 $(C(\infty,\,WO))$, so 60 is true. Moreover, in every FM model, 60 + 40 $(C(WO,\,\infty))$ implies AC, so 40 is false. (See Howard/Rubin\index{Author}{Howard/Rubin} \cite{bib:1995b}.) Since form 165 $(C(WO,\,WO))$ is true, (60 implies 165) it follows from note 2(8 and 9) that 16 and 24 are also true.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}6$: Levy's Model I. $A=\{a_{n}:n\in \omega\}$ and $A=\bigcup\{P_{n}:n\in\omega\}$, where $P_{0}=\{a_{0}\},\, P_{1}=\{a_{1},\,a_{2}\},\,P_{2}=\{a_{3},\,a_{4},\,a_{5}\},\,P_{3}=\{a_{6},\,a_{7},\,a_{8},\,a_{9},\, a_{10}\},\,\cdots$; in general for $n>0,\,|P_{n}|=p_{n}$, where $p_{n}$ is the $n$th prime. $\mathcal{G}$ is the group generated by $\{\pi_{n}:n\in\omega\}$, where, if $P_{n}=\{a_{m+1},\,a_{m+2},\,\cdots,\, a_{m+p_{n}}\}$, then

\begin{equation*}
\pi_{n}:a_{m+1}\mapsto a_{m+2}\mapsto\cdots a_{m+p_{n}}\mapsto a_{m+1}\ \mathrm{and}\ \pi_{n}(x)=x,\ \mathrm{for\ all}\,x\not\in P_{n}.
\end{equation*}
$S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. Levi proves in $\mathcal{N}6$ that there is no choice function on $\{P_{n}:n\in\omega\}$ so $C(\aleph_{0},\,<\aleph_{0})$ (10) is false, but for each $n\in\omega, n>0,\, C(\infty,\,n)$ (61) is true. (It is also clear that there is no Kinna/Wagner selection function on $\{P_{n}:n\in\omega\}$ so $KW(\aleph_{0},\,<\aleph_{0})$ (358) is also false.) Levy\index{Author}{Levy}, also proves the axiom of Multiple Choice (67) is true. However, Bleicher has shown that $(\forall n\in \omega)MC(\infty,\, \infty$, relatively prime to $n$) (218) is equivalent to 61 + 67, so 218 is also true. Since 218 implies 333 $(MC(\infty,\,\infty,\mathrm{odd}))$ and Keremedis has shown that 333 + 334$(MC(\infty,\,\infty,\mathrm{even}))\leftrightarrow$ AC, it follows that 334 is false. Since 218 is true, and therefore, [218 A] (Existence of Complementary Subspaces) is also true, it follows that 95$(F)$ (Existence of Complementary Subspaces over a Field $F$) is true.

Shannon proves if $T=\{f:\exists nf$ is a choice function on $\{P_{0},\,P_{1},\,\cdots,\,P_{n}\}$\} with the partial order $f\leq g$ iff $g\subseteq f$, then $T$ is a denumerable union of finite sets, all antichains are finite, and there is a denumerable family of dense sets for which there in no generic filter (171 is false). See note 47 for definitions. In Howard/Yorke\index{Author}{Howard/Yorke} \cite{bib:1987} it is shown that for any prime $p$, there is a set of finite groups $\{G_{y}:y\in Y\}$ such that the weak direct product has no maximal $p$-subgroup $(308(p)$ is false in $\mathcal{N}6$ for any prime $p$). Since form 106 (Baire category Theorem for compact Hausdorff spaces) is true (218 implies 106) and 43 (Principle of Dependent Choices) is false (43 implies 171), form 154 (the Tychonoff theorem for countably many $T_{2}$ spaces.) must be false. (106 + 154 implies 43. See Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1983c}) Degen has shown that if $\rho_{i}=\pi_{i}/P_{i},\,\rho_{i}$ is not defined on $A-P_{i}$, and $\phi =\bigcup_{i\in\omega}\rho_{i}$, then $\phi$ cannot be expressed as the product of two reflections. ($\phi$ is a reflection if $\phi^{2}=\phi$.) Consequently, form 314 (Every permutation on a non-empty set can be expressed as a product of two reflections.) is false.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}7$: L\"{a}uchli's Model I. $A$ is countably infinite. The group $\mathcal{G}$ is a permutation group on $A$ with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[1.] If $E_{1}$ and $E_{2}$ are finite subsets of $A$ and if $\phi\in \mathcal{G}$ is the identity on $E_{1}\cap E_{2}$, then there exist $\pi_{i}$ and $\rho_{i}$ in $\mathcal{G},\,i=1, 2,\cdots n$, such that $\phi=\pi_{1}\cdot \rho_{1}\cdot\pi_{2}\cdot \rho_{2}\cdots\pi_{n}\cdot \rho_{n}$ where $\pi_{i}$ is the identity on $E_{1}$ and $\rho_{i}$ is the identity on $E_{2}$.
\item[2.] If $E$ is a finite subset of $A$ and $\phi\in \mathcal{G}$ is such that $\phi(E)=E$, then $\phi$ is the identity on $E$.
\item[3.] For each finite $E\subset A$, there are distinct elements $a,\,b,\,c\in A$ and $\phi,\,\rho \in \mathcal{G}$ which are the identity on $E$ such that $\phi:a\mapsto b\mapsto c$ and $\rho:c\mapsto a\mapsto b$.
\end{enumerate}
$S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. L\"{a}uchli proves that in this model, AC for a set of finite sets (62) and AC for a set of well orderable sets (60) are true, but the Ordering Principle (30) is false. Since 60 implies $UT(WO,\,WO,\,WO)$ (231) and in every FM model 231 implies $(\forall\alpha)UT(\aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha})$, form 23 is true. Also, 60 implies that there is no amorphous set (64 is true), and 64 implies 133 (Every set is either well orderable or has an infinite amorphous subset.) is false. Pincus proves that there is a function which associates each infinite set with a nonprincipal ideal in its power set (123 is true). Moreover, Rado's Lemma (99) is false in this model because BPI (14) is false (14 implies 30) and 99 + 62 implies 14 (note 33). Since 60 is true, AC for a well ordered set of sets (40) is false. (See Howard/Rubin\index{Author}{Howard/Rubin} \cite{bib:1995b}.) Form 40 is false and form 122 $(C(WO,\,<\infty))$ is true because 60 implies 122. Therefore, form 328 $(MC(WO,\,\infty))$ is false because 122 + 328 $\rightarrow$ 40. Since form 165 $(C(WO,\,WO))$ is true, (60 implies 165) it follows from note 2(8 and 9) that 16 and 24 are also true.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}8$: L\"{a}uchli's Model II. $A$ is countably infinite, ordered like the rational numbers; $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all order automorphisms of $A$; and $S$ is the set of all subsets $E$ of $A$ such that $E$ has at most a finite number of accumulation points and every infinite subset of $E$ has an accumulation point. L\"{a}uchli\index{Author}{Lauchli@L\"{a}uchli} shows that Urysohn's Lemma (78) is false in this model.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}9$: Halpern/Howard Model. $A$ is a set of atoms with the structure of the set $\{s:s:\omega\rightarrow \omega\wedge(\exists n)(\forall j>n)(s_{j}=0)\}$. We identify $A$ with this set to simplify the description of $\mathcal{G}$. $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations $\phi$ on $A$ such that $\{a\in A$: $\phi(a)\neq a\}$ is bounded; and $S=\{A_{0}^{n}:n\in \omega\}$, where $A_{0}^{n}$ is the set of all sequences $s$ such that $s_{j}=0$ for all $j\geq n$. (The set $x$ has support $A_{0}^{n}$ if all permutations in $\mathcal{G}$ that leave $A_{0}^{n}$ pointwise fixed and leave the first $n$ coordinates of each $s\in A$ pointwise fixed, also leave $x$ fixed.) In this model, the axiom of choice for 2-element sets (88) is false, but the $2m=m$ principle (3) is true. Form 3 implies that there are no amorphous sets (64) is true and 64 implies that 133 (Every set is either well orderable or has an infinite amorphous subset.) is false. Since 3 implies 9 (Every Dedekind finite set is finite.) and 70 (There is a non-trivial ultrafilter on $\omega$.) is true in every FM model, it follows that 63 (Every infinite set has a non-trivial ultrafilter.) is also true.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}10$: H\"{o}ft/Howard\index{Author}{Hoft/Howard@H\"{o}ft/Howard}/Mostowski Model. (The model is a variation of $\mathcal{N}3$.) $A$ as ordered by $\precsim$ has the same order type as the rationals; $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all order automorphisms of $A$; $S$ is the set of all subsets $E$ of $A$ that satisfy the following three conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[1.] $E$ is well ordered by $\precsim$.
\item[2.] $E$ is bounded in $A$.
\item[3.] If $b:\alpha\rightarrow E$ is an order preserving bijection from $\alpha$ onto $E$ and if $\lambda<\alpha$ is a limit ordinal then $\{b(\beta):\beta<\gamma\}$ has no least upper bound in $(A,\,\precsim)$.
\end{enumerate}
In H\"{o}ft/Howard \cite{bib:1994} it is shown that, in $\mathcal{N}10$, every Dedekind finite set is finite (9 is true), but $(A,\,\precsim)$ is a linearly ordered set with no infinite descending sequences that cannot be well ordered (77 is false). In addition (see note 113) there is an infinite set of pairs with no choice function (88 is false). Since 70 (There is a nontrivial ultrafilter on $\omega$.) is true in every FM model and 9 + 70 implies 63 (Every infinite set has a non-trivial ultrafilter.), 63 is also true.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}11$: Jech's Model. Let $(I,\,\precsim)$ be a partially ordered set in the kernel (in the base model without atoms). Let $A=\{a_{i,n}:i\in I,\,n\in \omega\}$. For each $p\subseteq I$, let $S_{p}=\{a_{i,n}:i\in p,\, n\in \omega\}$. $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations of $A$ that leave $S_{\{i\}}$ fixed, for each $i\in I$. $S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. In this model, there is a set of cardinals that is isomorphic to $(I,\,\precsim)$. Thus, form $59(\precsim)$ is false.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}12(\aleph_{1})$: A variation of Fraenkel's model, $\mathcal{N}1$. The cardinality of $A$ is $\aleph_{1}$, $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations on $A$, and $S$ is the set of all countable subsets of $A$. In $\mathcal{N}12(\aleph_{1})$, every Dedekind finite set is finite (9 is true), but the $2m=m$ principle (3) is false. Also, AC for a well ordered set of sets (40) is true, but not all cardinals are comparable with $\aleph_{1}$ (41 is false) and for each $n\geq 2$ the set of $n$-element subsets of $A$ has no choice function (45$(n)$ is false). A. Rubin\index{Author}{A. Rubin} shows that each pair of cardinals has a greatest lower bound (187 is true). (See note 108.) Truss\index{Author}{Truss} proves that every linearly ordered set has a choice function (202 is true). Since 202 implies $UT(WO,\,WO,\,WO)$ (231) and in every FM model 231 implies $(\forall\alpha)UT(\aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha})$, form 23 is true. Since 202 implies 8 $(C(\aleph_{0},\,\infty))$, it follows from Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1982a} that in this model there is a set that cannot be well ordered and does not have an infinite Dedekind finite subset, (163 is false). (Form 8 plus form 163 iff AC.) Since 70 (There is a non-trivial ultrafilter on $\omega$.) is true in every FM model and 9 + 70 implies 63 (Every infinite set has a non-trivial ultra filter.), 63 is also true. Blass\index{Author}{Blass} \cite{bib:1979} has shown that 191 (There is a set $X$ such that for each set $a$ there is an ordinal $\alpha$ and a function $f$ mapping $X\times\alpha$ onto $a$.) is true in every permutation model with a set of atoms. He has also shown that 8 $(C(\aleph_{0},\,\infty))+191+193$ (Every Abelian group is a homomorphic image of a free projective Abelian group.) iff AC. Since 202 implies 8, form 193 must be false. (See note 60 for definitions.) The set of all pairs of atoms is a set of well orderable sets that has no choice function. Thus, $C(\infty,\,2)$ (88) and $KW(\infty,\,WO)$ (323) are false. Since $C(WO,\,<\aleph_{0})$ (122) is true (202 implies 122) it follows that MC (67) is false because 67 + 122 implies AC. (See [67 B].) It is shown in Higasikawa\index{Author}{Higasikawa} \cite{bib:1995} that the Idemmultiple Partition Principle, form 347, is false.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}12(\aleph_{2})$: Another variation of $\mathcal{N}1$. Change ``$\aleph_{1}$'' to $``\aleph_{2}$'' in $\mathcal{N}12(\aleph_{1})$ above. Thus, $A$ has cardinality $\aleph_{2}$, $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations of $A$, and $S$ is the set of all subsets of $A$ of cardinality at most $\aleph_{1}$. It follows from Jech\index{Author}{Jech} \cite{bib:1973b}(p 127, Theorem 8.9), that the Axiom of Choice for a well ordered family of sets (40) is true, the Principle of Dependent Choices for $\omega_{1}$ sets (44) is true, but the $2m=m$ principle (3) is false. Since 40 implies $UT(WO,\,WO,\,WO)$ (231) and in every FM model 231 implies $(\forall\alpha)UT(\aleph_{\alpha},\, \aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha})$, form 23 is true. H\"{a}ussler\index{Author}{Haussler@H\"{a}ussler} \cite{bib:1983} has shown that cardinal addition is not definable in terms of $\leq$ in this model. Thus, 161 is false. Since 40 implies 8 $(C(\aleph_{0},\,\infty))$, it follows from Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1982a} that in this model there is a set that cannot be well ordered and does not have an infinite Dedekind finite subset, (163 is false). (Form 8 plus form 163 iff AC.) Since 40 implies 9 (Every Dedekind finite set is finite.) and 70 (There is a non-trivial ultrafilter on $\omega$.) is true in every FM model, it follows that 63 (Every infinite set has a non-trivial ultrafilter.) is also true. Form 44 implies forms 39 $(C(\aleph_{1},\,\infty))$ and 41 (For each cardinal $m,\,m\leq\aleph_{1}$ or $\aleph_{1}\leq m$.). van Douwen\index{Author}{Douwen} \cite{bib:1980} has shown that 39 + 41 implies 135 (If $X$ is a $T_{2}$ space with at least two points and $X^{Y}$ is hereditarily metacompact, then $Y$ is countable.), so form 135 is also true. Blass\index{Author}{Blass} \cite{bib:1979} has shown that 191 (There is a set $X$ such that for each set $a$ there is an ordinal $\alpha$ and a function $f$ mapping $X\times\alpha$ onto $a$.) is true in every permutation model with a set of atoms. He has also shown that 8 $(C(\aleph_{0},\,\infty))+191+193$ (Every Abelian group is a homomorphic image of a free projective Abelian group.) iff AC. Since 40 implies 8, form 193 must be false. (See note 60 for definitions.) It is shown in Howard/Rubin\index{Author}{Howard/Rubin} \cite{bib:1995b} that in every FM model $40 + 60\ (C(\infty,\,WO))$ implies AC, so 60 is false. Howard\index{Author}{Howard} \cite{bib:1973} proves that in every FM model 62 $(C(\infty,\,<\aleph_{0}))$ implies 60, so 62 is also false. Since $C(WO,\,<\aleph_{0})$ (122) is true (40 implies 122) it follows that MC (67) is false because $67 + 122$ implies AC. (See [67 B].) It is shown in Higasikawa\index{Author}{Higasikawa} \cite{bib:1995} that the Idemmultiple Partition Principle, form 347, is false.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}12(\aleph_{\alpha})$: A generalization of $\mathcal{N}12(\aleph_{1})$. Replace ``$\aleph_{1}$'' by ``$\aleph_{\alpha}$'' where $\aleph_{\alpha}$ is a singular cardinal. Thus, $|A|=\aleph_{\alpha}$; $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations on $A$; and $S$ is the set of all subsets of $A$ with cardinality less than $\aleph_{\alpha}$. Jech\index{Author}{Jech} shows that $DC(\aleph_{\beta})$ holds for all $\aleph_{\beta}<\mathrm{cf}(\aleph_{\alpha})$ ($87(\beta)$ for $\aleph_{\beta}<\mathrm{cf}(\aleph_{\alpha})$ is true); $W_{\aleph_{\beta}}$ (For all cardinals $m,\, m\leq\aleph_{\beta}$ or $\aleph_{\beta}\leq m.)$ holds for all $\beta<\alpha$ ($71(\beta)$ is true for $\beta<\alpha$); but $71(\alpha)$ and $C(\infty,\mathrm{cf}\aleph_{\alpha})$ are false. It follows from note 104 that the $2m=m$ principle (3) is false. Since 87 implies 8 $(C(\aleph_{0},\,\infty))$, it follows from Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1982a} that in this model there is a set that cannot be well ordered and does not have an infinite Dedekind finite subset, which implies that 163 is false. (Form 8 plus form 163 iff AC.) Since 87$(\beta)$ implies 9 (Every Dedekind finite set is finite.) and 70 (There is a non-trivial ultrafilter on $\omega$.) is true in every FM model, it follows that 63 (Every infinite set has a non-trivial ultrafilter.) is also true. Blass\index{Author}{Blass} \cite{bib:1979} has shown that 191 (There is a set $X$ such that for each set $a$ there is an ordinal $\alpha$ and a function $f$ mapping $X\times\alpha$ onto $a$.) is true in every permutation model with a set of atoms. He has also shown that 8 + 191 + 193 (Every Abelian group is a homomorphic image of a free projective Abelian group.) iff AC. Thus, form 193 must be false if $\aleph_{\beta}<\mathrm{cf}(\aleph\alpha)$. (See note 60 for definitions.)

\noindent $\mathcal{N}13$: L\"{a}uchli/Jech Model. $A=B_{1}\cup B_{2}$, where $B_{1}=\bigcup\{A_{j1}:j\in \omega\}$, and $B_{2}=\bigcup\{A_{j2}:j\in \omega\}$, and each $A_{ji}$ is a 6-element set. Consider the following permutations on 6 elements: $\alpha_{1}=(12)(34)(5)(6)$, $\beta_{1}=(13)(24)(5)(6)$, $\gamma_{1}=(14)(23)(5)(6)$, $\alpha_{2}=\alpha_{1}$, $\beta_{2}=(12)(3)(4)(56)$, and $\gamma_{2}=(1)(2)(34)(56)$. For each $j,\,\alpha$ is the permutation on $A_{j1}\cup A_{j2}$ that acts like $\alpha_{1}$ on $A_{j1}$ and $\alpha_{2}$ on $A_{j2}$; similarly for $\beta$ and $\gamma$. $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations on $A$ that preserves $A_{j1}$ and $A_{j2}$ and acts on $A_{j1}\cup A_{j2}$ like the identity, $\alpha,\,\beta$, or $\gamma$. $S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. In $\mathcal{N}13$, there are two isomorphic vector spaces, one with $B_{1}$ as a basis and the other with $B_{2}$ as a basis, but $|B_{1}|\neq|B_{2}|$ because $B_{1}$ contains a countably infinite subset, but $B_{2}$ does not. And in L\"{a}uchli \cite{bib:1962} it is shown that $|B_{1}|$ and $|B_{2}|$ are incomparable.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}14$: Morris/Jech Model. $A=\bigcup\{A_{\alpha}:\alpha<\omega_{1}\}$, where the $A_{\alpha}$'s are pairwise disjoint, each is countably infinite, and each is ordered like the rationals; $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations on $A$ that leave each $A_{\alpha}$ fixed and preserve the ordering on each $A_{\alpha}$; and $S=\{B_{\gamma}:\gamma<\omega_{1}\}$, where $B_{\gamma}=\bigcup\{A_{\alpha}:\alpha<\gamma\}$. Let $P=A\cup\omega_{1}$ and order $P$ so that the elements in $A_{\alpha}$ precede those in $A_{\beta}$ if $\alpha<\beta$, the elements in each $A_{\alpha}$ are ordered like the rationals as above, and each $\alpha\in \omega_{1}$ precedes $A_{\alpha}$ and follows all $A_{\beta}$ for $\beta<\alpha$. Then $P$ is a linearly ordered set such that $|P|>\aleph_{1}$, but each initial segment of $P$ is countable. Thus, form 103 is false. In note 144 we show dependent choice (form 43) is true.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}15$: Brunner/Howard\index{Author}{Howard} Model I. $A=\{a_{i,\alpha}:i\in \omega\wedge\alpha\in \omega_{1}\}$. Let $\Gamma$ be the group of all even permutations on $\omega$. $\mathcal{G}=\{g:(\forall\alpha\in\omega_{1})(\exists\gamma\in\Gamma)(\forall i\in \omega)g(a_{i,\alpha})=a_{\gamma(i),\alpha}\}$. $S$ is the set of all countable subsets of $A$. In this model, $|A|<|A|+|A|$ (3 is false). The axiom of choice for a denumerable set of sets (8) is true and it is also true that every infinite set is the union of a disjoint well orderable family of denumerable sets (152 is true). If $B_{\alpha}=\{a_{i,\alpha}:i\in \omega\}$, then $\bigcup\{B_{\alpha}:\alpha\in \omega_{1}\}$ cannot be well ordered (151 is false), but the union of a well ordered family of finite sets can be well ordered ([122 A] is true). $C(\infty,\,WO)$ (60) implies 151 and in every FM model $C(\infty,\,<\aleph_{0})$ (62) implies 60 (Howard \cite{bib:1973}). Thus, 62 is false. It follows from Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1982a} that in this model there is a set that cannot be well ordered and does not have an infinite Dedekind finite subset, (163 is false). (Form 8 plus form 163 iff AC.) Since 8 implies 9 (Every Dedekind finite set is finite.) and 70 (There is a non-trivial ultrafilter on $\omega$.) is true in every FM model, it follows that 63 (every infinite set has a non-trivial ultrafilter) is also true. Blass\index{Author}{Blass} \cite{bib:1979} has shown that 191 (There is a set $X$ such that for each set $a$ there is an ordinal $\alpha$ and a function $f$ mapping $X\times\alpha$ onto $a$.) is true in every permutation model with a set of atoms. He has also shown that 8 + 191 + 193 (Every Abelian group is a homomorphic image of a free projective Abelian group.) iff AC. Thus, 193 is false. (See note 60 for definitions.) $KW(WO,\,WO)$ (324) and $MC(WO,\, WO)$ (330) are false because $\{B_{\alpha}:\alpha\in \omega_{1}\}$ is a well ordered set of well orderable sets that has no Kinna-Wagner selection function and no multiple choice function. In note 144 we show dependent choice (form 43) is true.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}16$: Jech/Levy/Pincus Model. $A$ has cardinality $\aleph_{\omega}$; $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations on $A$; and $S$ is the set of all subsets of $A$ of cardinality less that $\aleph_{\omega}$. In this model, every infinite set has a countably infinite subset (9 is true), but not every set of denumerable sets has a choice function (8 is false). Also, in $\mathcal{N}16$, for every cardinal $\kappa <\aleph_{\omega}$ every cardinal is comparable to $\kappa$ (41 is true), but there are cardinals that are not comparable to $\aleph_{\omega}$. Form 41 implies that there are no amorphous sets (64 is true), but 64 implies that 133 (Every set is either well orderable or has an infinite amorphous subset.) is false. Since 70 (There is a non-trivial ultrafilter on $\omega.)$ is true in every FM model and 9 + 70 implies 63 (Every infinite set has a non-trivial ultrafilter.), 63 is also true.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}16(\aleph_{\gamma})$: Levy's Model II. This is an extension of $\mathcal{N}16$ in which $A$ has cardinality $\aleph_{\gamma}$ where $\mathrm{cf}(\aleph_{\gamma})=\aleph_{0}$; $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations on $A$; and $S$ is the set of all subsets of $A$ of cardinality less that $\aleph_{\gamma}$. Form $71(\alpha)$ implies that there are no amorphous sets (64 is true) and 64 implies that 133 (Every set is either well orderable or has an infinite amorphous subset.) is false. Since 70 (There is a non-trivial ultrafilter on $\omega$.) is true in every FM model, and 9 + 70 implies 63 (Every infinite set has a non-trivial ultra filter.), it follows that 63 is also true.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}17$: Brunner/Howard\index{Author}{Brunner/Howard} Model II. $A=\{a_{\alpha,i}:\alpha\in \omega_{1}\wedge i\in\omega\}$. Let $\Gamma$ be the group of all permutations on $\omega_{1}$. $\mathcal{G}\ =\{g:(\exists\gamma\in\Gamma)(\forall\alpha\in \omega_{1})(\forall i\in \omega)g(a_{\alpha,i})=a_{\gamma(\alpha),i}\}$. $S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. In this model, the union of a denumerable number of denumerable sets is denumerable (31 is true), but $C(\aleph_{0},2^{\aleph_{0}})$ (28) is false. If we assume that $2^{\aleph_{0}}=\aleph_{1}$ in the ground model, then $C(\aleph_{0},\,\aleph_{1})$ is also false. Therefore, $UT(\aleph_{0},\,\aleph_{1},\, \aleph_{1})$ (27) (which implies $C(\aleph_{0},\,\aleph_{1})$) is also false. Form 23 $((\forall\alpha)UT(\aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha}))$ is false because 23 implies 27. Since 231 $(UT(WO,\,WO,\,WO)$ implies 23 in every FM model,\index{Author}{Pincus} it follows that 231 is false.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}18$: Howard's Model I. Let $B=B_{n}:n\in\omega$ where the $B_{n}$'s are pairwise disjoint and each is countably infinite and let $A=\bigcup B$. For each $n\in \omega$, let $F_{n}$ be a non-principal ultrafilter in $\mathcal{P}(B_{n})$ and let $I_{n}$ be the corresponding non-principal maximal ideal. $\mathcal{G}$ is the set of all permutations $\sigma$ of $A$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item[1.] $\sigma(B_{n})=B_{n}$, for each $n\in \omega$.
\item[2.] For each $n\in \omega$ there is a $u\in F_{n}$ such that $\sigma$ fixes $u$ pointwise.
\end{enumerate}
$S$ is the set of all sets of the form $C\cup\bigcup_{n\in\omega}g(n)$ where $C$ is a finite union of the $B_{n}$'s and $g:\omega \rightarrow \mathcal{P}(A)$ satisfies $g(n)\in I_{n}$ for each $n\in \omega$. In $\mathcal{N}18,\,\{B_{n}:n\in \omega\}$ is a denumerable collection of denumerable sets whose union is not denumerable (31 is false), but AC for a denumerable number of denumerable sets ([32 A]) is true. Form 23 $((\forall\alpha)UT(\aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha}))$ is false because 23 implies 31. Since 231 $(UT(WO,\,WO,\,WO)$ implies 23 in every FM model, it follows that 231 is false.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}19(\precsim)$: Tsukada's Model. Let $(P,\,\precsim)$ be a partially ordered set that is not well ordered; Let $Q$ be a countably infinite set, disjoint from $P$; and let $I=P\cup Q$. Let $A=$\{ $a_{iq}:i\in I,\,q$ a rational number\}; let $\mathcal{G}$ be the set of all permutations $\pi$ of $A$ such that $\pi(a_{iq})=a_{i\pi_{i}(q)}$ where for each $i\in I,\,\pi_{i}$ is an order automorphism of the rationals. $S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. In this model, the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem (14) is true and every set of well orderable sets has a choice function (60) is true. (Since 60 implies $UT(WO,\,WO,\, WO)$ (231) and in every FM model 231 implies $(\forall\alpha)UT(\aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha})$ (23), form 23 is true.) However, the set $(P,\,\precsim)$ can be embedded into the natural ordering of the cardinals so 59$(\precsim)$ is false. AC for a well ordered family of sets (40) is false. (In every FM model, 40 + 60 $\rightarrow$ AC, Howard/Rubin\index{Author}{Howard/Rubin} \cite{bib:1995b}.) Using the fact that the Kinna-Wagner Selection Principle (15) is false and that the Ordering Principle (30) is true, Krom proves that there is an ordered topological space that is not normal (118 is false). Form 14 implies 49 (Every partial ordering can be extended to a linear ordering.) and 49 + 51 (Every linear ordering has a cofinal sub-well ordering) iff AC. (See Morris \cite{bib:1969} and note 121.) Thus, form 51 is false. Howard \cite{bib:1973} has shown that in every FM model 14 implies the Weak Sikorski Theorem (317), so 317 is true. Form 40 is false and form 122 $(C(WO,\,<\infty))$ is true because 60 implies 122. Therefore, form 328 $(MC(WO,\,\infty))$ is false because 122 + 328 $\rightarrow$ 40. Since form 165 $(C(WO,\,WO))$ is true, (60 implies 165) it follows from note 2(8 and 9) that 16 and 24 are also true.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}20$: Truss'\index{Author}{Truss} Model\index{Author}{Morris} II. Let $X=\{a(i,\,k,\,l):i\in 2,\,k\in \mathbb{Z},\,l\in \omega\},\,Y=\{a(i,j,\,k,\,l):i,\,j\in 2,\,k\in \mathbb{Z},\,i\in \omega\}$ and $A$ is the disjoint union of $X$ and $Y$. The set of atoms is countable with order type $(2\times \mathbb{Z}\times \omega)\cup(2^{2}\times \mathbb{Z}\times \omega)$. Let $V(k,\,l)=\{a(i,\,k,\,l):i\in 2\},\,W(k,\, l)=\{a(i,j,\,k,\,l):i,\,j\in 2\},\,S=\{V(k,\,l):k\in \mathbb{Z},\,l\in \omega\},\, T=\{W(k,\,l):k\in \mathbb{Z},\,l\in \omega\}$, and $U=\{\{V(k,\,l),\,W(k,\,l)\}:k\in \mathbb{Z},\,l\in \omega\}\cup\{\{V(k+1,\,l),\,W(k,\,l)\}$: $k\in \mathbb{Z},\,l\in \omega\}$. Using forcing, construct a generic choice function $F$ on the set of all pairs of elements in $S\cup T$. Using $F$, it is possible to construct a function $f$ that maps $2\times Y$ onto $2\times X$. $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations of $A$ that leaves $f,\,X,\,Y,\,S,\,T$, and $U$ fixed. The set of supports is the finite subsets of \emph{A}. (This is a Fraenkel-Mostowski-Cohen model.) In this model, there is a mapping of $2\times Y$ onto $2\times X$, but no mapping of $Y$ onto $X$.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}21(\aleph_{\alpha+1})$: Jensen's Model. We assume $\aleph_{\alpha+1}$ is a regular cardinal. Let $A= \{(a_{i_{1}},\,a_{i_{2}},\, \ldots,\,a_{i_{n}}):n\in \omega\wedge(\forall j\leq n)(i_{j}<\aleph_{\alpha+1})\}$. $A$ is partially ordered by extension. Let $\mathcal{G}$ be the group of all permutations of $A$ that preserves the partial ordering, and let $S$ be the set of all subsets $E$ of $A$ that satisfy the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] The cardinality of $E$ is less than $\aleph_{\alpha+1}$;
\item[(2)] If $s\subseteq t$ and $t\in E$, then $s\in E$; and
\item[(3)] There is no function $f:\omega\rightarrow\aleph_{\alpha+1}\,f|n\in E$ for all $n\in\omega$.
\end{enumerate}
In this model, the Principle of Dependent Choices (43) is false. The Axiom of choice for a family of $\aleph_{\beta}$ sets $(86(\beta))$ is true for all $\beta<\alpha+1$ and, therefore, the Axiom of Choice for a family of $\aleph_{1}$ sets (39) is true for all $\alpha\geq 1$. For all cardinals $\kappa,\,\kappa$ is comparable with $\aleph_{\beta}(71(\beta))$ is true for each $\beta<\alpha+1$. Since 39 implies 9 (Every Dedekind finite set is finite.) and 70 (There is a non-trivial ultrafilter on $\omega$.) is true in every FM model, it follows that 63 (Every infinite set has a non-trivial ultrafilter.) is also true. Since 39 implies 8 $(C(\aleph_{0},\,\infty))$, it follows from Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1982a} that in this model there is a set that cannot be well ordered and does not have an infinite Dedekind finite subset, (163 is false). (Form 8 plus form 163 iff AC.) Blass\index{Author}{Blass} \cite{bib:1979} has shown that 191 (There is a set $X$ such that for each set $a$ there is an ordinal $\alpha$ and a function $f$ mapping $X\times\alpha$ onto $a$.) is true in every permutation model with a set of atoms. He has also shown that 8 + 191 + 193 (Every Abelian group is a homomorphic image of a free projective Abelian group.) iff AC. Since 8 and 191 are true, 193 must be false. (See note 60 for definitions.)

See, also, Jech\index{Author}{Jech} \cite{bib:1973b} (p 130) and Felgner\index{Author}{Felgner} \cite{bib:1971a} (pp 151-159), notes 18 and 120(4 and 55).

\noindent $\mathcal{N}22(K,p)$: Makowski/Wi\'{s}niewski/Mostowski Model. $K$ is a finite subset of $\omega$. Let $p$ be a prime that is greater than every element of $K$. Let $A=\bigcup\{A_{i}:i\in \omega\}$ where The $A_{i}$'s are pairwise disjoint and each has cardinality $p$. For each $i\in\omega$, let $g_{i}$ be a permutation of $A_{i}$ which is a $p$-cycle. Let $\mathcal{G}$ be the group of all permutations of $A$ which are the identity on all but a finite number of the $A_{i}$'s and are equal to some power of $g_{i}$ on the others. Let $S$ be the set of all finite subsets of $A$. In this model, $C(\infty,\,K)$ (46$(K)$ is true. Thus, $C(\infty,\, n)(45(n))$ is true if $K=\{n\}$, and $C(\infty,\,2)$ (88) is true if $K=\{2\}$. However, there is a set $E$ and a function $f:E\rightarrow E$ such that $f$ has no fixed point and $E$ is not the union of three mutually disjoint sets, $E_{1},\,E_{2}$, and $E_{3}$, such that $E_{i}\cap f(E_{i})=\emptyset$, for $i=1,2,3$ (285 is false). In Howard/Yorke \cite{bib:1987}, it is shown that every group has a maximal $p$-subgroup in $\mathcal{N}22(K,p)$ (form $308(p)$ is true) and that $C(\aleph_{0},p)$ is false (form $288(p)$ is false).

\noindent $\mathcal{N}23$: Howard/Mostowski\index{Author}{Mostowski}\index{Author}{Makowski/Wisniewski@Makowski/Wi\'{s}niewski} Linearly Ordered Model. This model is a modification of $\mathcal{N}3$. $A$ is countably infinite; $<$ is a dense linear ordering on $A$ without first or last elements $((A,\,<)\cong(\mathbb{Q},\, <))$; $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all order automorphisms on $(A,\,<)$; and $S$ is the set of all subsets of $A$ that are well ordered by $<$. P. Howard\index{Author}{Howard/Yorke} has shown that AC for pairs (88) is false in this model and A. Rubin has shown that AC for a denumerable number of sets (8) is true. See note 100. It follows from Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1982a} that in this model there is a set that cannot be well ordered and does not have an infinite Dedekind finite subset, (163 is false). (Form 8 plus form 163 iff AC.) Since 8 implies 9 (Every Dedekind finite set is finite.) and 70 (There is a non-trivial ultrafilter on $\omega$.) is true in every FM model, it follows that 63 (Every infinite set has a non-trivial ultrafilter.) is also true. Blass\index{Author}{Blass} \cite{bib:1979} has shown that 191 (There is a set $X$ such that for each set $a$ there is an ordinal $\alpha$ and a function $f$ mapping $X\times\alpha$ onto $a$.) is true in every permutation model with a set of atoms. He has also shown that 8 + 191 + 193 (Every Abelian group is a homomorphic image of a free projective Abelian group.) iff AC. Thus, 193 is false. (See note 60 for definitions.)

\noindent $\mathcal{N}24$: Hickman's Model I. This model is a variation of $\mathcal{N}2$. Let $A=\{a_{i}: i\in \omega\}\cup\{b_{i}:i\in \omega\}$, a union of pairwise disjoint denumerable sets; $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations on $A$ such that for each $\sigma\in \mathcal{G}$, and for each $i\in \omega,\,\sigma(\{a_{i},\,b_{i}\})= \{a_{j},\, b_{j}\}$, for some $j\in\omega$; and $S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. Then both $A$ and $P=\{\{a_{i},\,b_{i}\}:i\in \omega\}$ are amorphous sets in $\mathcal{N}24$ (64 is false), so it follows from Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1984a}, that in this model there is a Hilbert Space $H$ and an operator on $H$ which is not the direct sum of a finite matrix and a scalar operator (124 is false). Also, every denumerable family of finite sets has a choice function (10 is true) and every linearly ordered family of finite sets has a choice function (121 is true), but it is not the case that every infinite family of pairs has an infinite subfamily with a choice function (166 is false). There is an amorphous power of a compact $T_{2}$ space which is well orderable, but not compact (127 is false). In Brunner \cite{bib:1982a}, it is shown that if a set cannot be well ordered, then it has an amorphous subset (133 is true). It follows from Brunner \cite{bib:1982a} that MC (67) is false because 133 implies 164 (Every non well orderable set has an infinite subset with a Dedekind finite power set.) and 67 + 164 iff AC. It is shown in note 123 that 133 implies 231 $(UT(WO,\,WO,\,WO))$. In every FM model 231 implies 23 $((\forall\alpha)UT(\aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha}))$. It follows that 23 is also true. Since form 165 $(C(WO,\,WO))$ is true, (133 implies 165) it follows from note 2(8 and 9) that 16 and 24 are also true.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}24(n,\,LO)$: Truss' Model III. This is a variation of $\mathcal{N}24(n)$ in which the set $B$ is linearly ordered. Suppose that $n>1$ and let $A=\{a_{qi}:q\in \mathbb{Q},\,i\in n\}$. For each $q\in \mathbb{Q}$, let $b_{q}=\{a_{qi}:i\in n\}$ and let $B=\{b_{q}:q\in \mathbb{Q}\}$. We define a linear ordering, $\precsim$, on $B$ so that for all $p,\,q\in \mathbb{Q},\, b_{p}\precsim b_{q}$ iff $p\leq q$. $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations on $A$ which are order automorphisms on $(B,\precsim)$ and $S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. In this model $B$ is a linearly ordered set of $n$-element sets that does not have a choice function (33$(n)$ is false). However, every well ordered set of finite sets has a choice function (122 is true). Since 122 + 67 (MC) implies AC (see [67 B]), it follows that MC is false.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}25$: Brunner's Model I. The set of atoms, $A$, is equipped with the structure of the Hilbert space $\ell_{2},\, \mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations on $A$ that preserve the norm (unitary operators), and $S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} has shown that in this model $A$ is a Hilbert space in which the unit ball is sequentially compact, but $A$ has no orthonormal basis (158 is false).

\noindent $\mathcal{N}26$: Brunner/Pincus\index{Author}{Pincus} Model, a variation of $\mathcal{N}2$. The set of atoms $A=\bigcup_{n\in\omega}P_{n}$, where the $P_{n}$'s are pairwise disjoint denumerable sets; $\mathcal{G}$ is the set of all permutations $\sigma$ on $A$ such that $\sigma(P_{n})=P_{n}$, for all $n\in \omega$; and $S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. Each $P_{n}$ for $n\in \omega$ is amorphous (64 is false) and each set that cannot be well ordered has an infinite subset in 1-1 correspondence with $A$. Thus, Brunner proves that every set is either well orderable or has an infinite amorphous subset (133 is true). It is clear that the partial Kinna-Wagner Principle, $PKW(\aleph_{0},\,\infty,\,\infty)$ (167), the Kinna-Wagner Principle, $KW(\aleph_{0},\,\infty)$ (355), and the multiple-choice axiom, $MC_{\omega}(\aleph_{0},\,\infty)$ (131), are all false for the set $\{P_{n}:n\in \omega\}$. It is shown in note 123 that 133 implies 231 $(UT(WO,\,WO,\,WO))$. In every FM model 231 implies 23 $((\forall\alpha)UT(\aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha}))$. It follows that 23 is also true. De la Cruz and Di Prisco have shown that every infinite collection of non-empty well orderable sets has an infinite subfamily with a choice function (380 is true). Since form 165 $(C(WO,\,WO))$ is true, (133 implies 165) it follows from note 2(8 and 9) that 16 and 24 are also true.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}27$: Hickman's Model II. Let $A$ be a set with cardinality $\aleph_{1}$ such that $A= \{(a_{\alpha},\, b_{\beta}):\alpha<\omega,\,\beta<\omega_{1}\}$. Let $<$ be the reverse lexicographic order on $A$, i.e., $(a_{\alpha},\,b_{\beta})<(a_{\gamma},\,b_{\delta})$ iff $\beta<\delta$, or $\beta=\delta$ and $\alpha<\gamma$. $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all automorphisms on $A$ that preserve $<$, and $S$ is the set of all countable subsets of $A$. Hickman\index{Author}{Hickman} \cite{bib:1980b} has shown that if $\aleph_{\alpha}$ is a successor cardinal, then there exists an $\aleph_{\alpha}$ minimal set ($183(\alpha)$ is false for successor cardinals). In note 144 we show dependent choice (form 43) is true.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}28$: Blass' Permutation Model. The set $A=\{a_{\xi}^{i}:i\in \mathbb{Z},\,\xi\,\in\aleph_{1}\}$. For each $\xi \in\aleph_{1}$, let $g_{\xi}$ be the permutation of $A$ such that
\begin{equation*}
g_{\xi}(a_{\eta}^{i})=\left\{\begin{matrix}
a_{\eta}^{i+1} & \mathrm{if}\,\eta=\xi\\ a_{\eta}^{i} & \mathrm{if}\,\eta\,\neq\xi
\end{matrix}\right.
\end{equation*}
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be the group of permutations generated by all the $g_{\xi}$'s for $\xi \in\aleph_{1}$. Let
\begin{equation*}
S=\{\{a_{\xi}^{i}:i\in \mathbb{Z},\,\xi \in E\}:E\ \mathrm{a\,finite\,subset\,of}\,\aleph_{1}\}.
\end{equation*}
Let $\mathcal{N}$ be the permutation model generated by $A,\,\mathcal{G}$, and $S$. For any set $x,\,x$ is called \emph{small} if $A \cap TC(x)$ is countable. ($TC(x)$ is the transitive closure of $x$.) Let the universe of $\mathcal{N}28$ be the class of all small sets in $\mathcal{N}$. Blass shows that $\mathcal{N}28$ is a model of $\mathrm{ZF}^{0}$ in which $A$ is a proper class and he also shows that there is no non-trivial injective Abelian group in this model (190 is false). Blass also proves that form 190 is true in every permutation model in which the class of atoms is a set. Let $A^{\prime}=\Big\{a_{\xi}^{i}: i\in \mathbb{Z}\wedge\xi \in\aleph_{0}\Big\}$. $A^{\prime}$ is a denumerable subset of the atoms (in the ground model) and is therefore a set in the model. Further, $A^{\prime}$ is linearly orderable in $\mathcal{N}28$. For each $\xi \in\aleph_{0}$, let $O_{\xi}=\{a_{\xi}^{2i}:i\in \mathbb{Z}\}$ and $E_{\xi}=\{a_{\xi}^{2i+1}:i\in \mathbb{Z}\}$. The set $B=\{O_{\xi}:\xi\,\in\aleph_{0}\}\cup\{E_{\xi}:\xi\, \in\aleph_{0}\}$ cannot be linearly ordered in $\mathcal{N}28$ so form 293 is false. Form 129 is false because the set $B$ cannot be partitioned into sets of order type $^{\ast} \omega+\omega$. (See model $\mathcal{N}37$.)

\noindent $\mathcal{N}29$: Dawson/Howard\index{Author}{Dawson/Howard} Model. Let $A=\bigcup\{B_{n};n\in \omega\}$ is a disjoint union, where each $B_{n}$ is denumerable and ordered like the rationals by $\leq_{n}$. Thus, for each $n\in \omega,\,(B_{n},\, \leq_{n})\cong(\mathbb{Q},\,\leq)$. $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all permutations on $A$ such that for all $n\in \omega$, and all $\phi\in \mathcal{G},\,\phi$ is an order automorphism of $(B_{n},\,\leq_{n})$ and $S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. In Dawson/Howard it is shown that $|A!|<|2^{A}|$, thus form 200 $((\forall x)(|2^{x}|=|x!|))$ is false. Also, since $|2^{A}|$ is clearly $\leq|A^{A}|$, form 291 $((\forall x)(|x!|=|x^{x}|))$ is also false. In note 136 we prove that BPI (14) is true. Thus, $C(\infty,\, <\aleph_{0})$ (62) is true. Howard\index{Author}{Howard} \cite{bib:1973} proves that in every FM model 62 implies 60 $(C(\infty,\,WO))$. However, the set $\{B_{n}:n\in \omega\}$ is a denumerable set that has no multiple choice function $(MC(\aleph_{0},\,\infty)$ (126) is false) nor does it have an infinite subset with a Kinna-Wagner selection function $(PKW(\aleph_{0},\,\geq 2,\,\infty)$ (167) is false). Since form 165 $(C(WO,\,WO))$ is true, (60 implies 165) it follows from note 2(8 and 9) that 16 and 24 are also true.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}31$: L\"{a}uchli's Model IV. The set $A$ is denumerable. A field, $F$ is constructed with base set $A$ which is isomorphic to the algebraic closure of $\mathbb{Q}$. $\mathcal{G}$ is the set of all permutations on $A$ that are automorphisms on $F$. $S$ is the set of all finite subsets of $A$. L\"{a}uchli proves that in this model, $F$ has no real closed subfield so 241 is false. Also, Hodges\index{Author}{Hodges} proves that if $R$ is the ring of integers in $F$, then $R$ is a principal ideal domain that is not a unique factorization domain and has no maximal ideal (243 and 244 are false).

\noindent $\mathcal{N}32$: Hickman's Model III. This is a variation of $\mathcal{N}1$. Let $A$ be denumerable. Construct an elementary Abelean $p$-group $G$ on $A$ where $p$ is a prime. (Every non-identity element has order $p$.) Let $\mathcal{G}$ be the group of automorphisms of $G$, and let $S$ be the set of finite subsets of $A$. Hickman proves that if $H$ is any nontrivial subgroup of $G$, then the order of $H$ does not divide the order of $G$ (237 is false). Thus, it follows that $G$ is not the direct sum of cyclic groups (238 is false). Hickman also shows that in $G$ every ascending chain of subgroups is finite, but $G$ is not finitely generated (240 is false).

\noindent $\mathcal{N}33$: Howard\index{Author}{Howard}/H.Rubin/J.Rubin\index{Author}{Howard/H.Rubin/J.Rubin} Model. $A$ is countably infinite; $\precsim$ is a dense linear ordering on $A$ without first or last elements $((A,\,\precsim)\cong(\mathbb{Q},\,\leq))$; $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of all order automorphisms on $(A,\,\precsim)$; and $S$ is the set of all bounded subsets of $A$. It is shown that the axiom of choice for a well ordered set of non-empty sets (40) is true. (Since 40 implies $UT(WO,\,WO,\,WO)$ (231) and in every FM model 231 implies $(\forall\alpha)UT(\aleph_{\alpha},\, \aleph_{\alpha},\,\aleph_{\alpha})$ (23), form 23 is true.) However, a set $x\subseteq A\times A$ and a transitive relation $R$ on $x$ are constructed so that every subset of $x$ on which $R$ is antisymmetric has an upper bound, but $x$ has no maximal element (260 is false). AC for a set of well orderable sets (60) is false. (In every FM model, 40 + 60 $\rightarrow$ AC, Howard/Rubin \cite{bib:1995b}.) In every FM model $C(\infty,\,<\aleph_{0})$ (62) implies 60 (Howard \cite{bib:1973}). Thus, 62 is false. Since 40 implies 8 $(C(\aleph_{0},\,\infty))$, it follows from Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} \cite{bib:1982a} that in this model there is a set that cannot be well ordered and does not have an infinite Dedekind finite subset, (163 is false). (Form 8 plus form 163 iff AC.) Since 8 implies 9 (Every Dedekind finite set is finite.) and 70 (There is a non-trivial ultrafilter on $\omega$.) is true in every FM model, it follows that 63 (Every infinite set has a non-trivial ultrafilter.) is also true. Blass\index{Author}{Blass} \cite{bib:1979} has shown that 191 (There is a set $X$ such that for each set $a$ there is an ordinal $\alpha$ and a function $f$ mapping $X\times\alpha$ onto $a$.) is true in every permutation model with a set of atoms. He has also shown that 8 + 191 + 193 (Every Abelian group is a homomorphic image of a free projective Abelian group.) iff AC. Since 40 implies 8, form 193 must be false. (See note 60 for definitions.) Form 3 $(2m=m)$ is false because $2|A|\neq|A|$. Forms 349 $(MC(\infty,\,\aleph_{0}))$ and 356 $(KW(\infty,\,\aleph_{0}))$ are also false because the set of all infinite bounded intervals of $A$ is a set of denumerable sets which has no multiple choice function and no Kinna-Wagner selection function.

\noindent $\mathcal{N}34$: Pincus'\index{Author}{Pincus} Model X. For each $q\in \mathbb{Q}$, let $C_{q}=\{a_{q},\,b_{q}\}$, a pair of atoms and let $A=\bigcup_{q\in \mathbb{Q}}C_{q}$. Let $\mathscr{C} =\{C_{q}:q\in \mathbb{Q}\,\}$ and let $\preceq$ be the ordering $\mathscr{C}$ inherits from $\mathbb{Q}$. (I. e., $C_{q}\preceq C_{r}\Leftrightarrow q\leq r$ where $\leq$ is the usual ordering on $\mathbb{Q}$.) Let $\mathcal{G}$ be the group of permutations of $A$ generated by the the two groups
\begin{align*}
G_{1}=\{\phi:&(\exists f)[f\,\mathrm{is\,an\,order\,automorphism\,of}\,\mathbb{Q}\\
&\wedge(\forall q\in \mathbb{Q})(\phi(a_{q})=a_{f(q)}\wedge\phi(b_{q})=b_{f(q)})]\}
\end{align*}
and
\begin{align*}
G_{2}=\{\psi:&\psi\ \mathrm{is\ a\ finite\ product\ of\ transposition},\\
&\psi=(a_{q_{1}},\,b_{q_{1}})\circ\cdots \circ(a_{q_{n}},\,b_{a_{n}})\ \mathrm{for\,some}\,q_{1},\ldots,\,q_{n}\in \mathbb{Q}\}.
\end{align*}
$G_{1}$ could also be described as $\{\phi:\phi:A\rightarrow A$ is one to one and onto and (the extension of) $\phi$ is an order isomorphism of $(\mathscr{C},\,\preceq)\}$. $S$ is the set of finite subsets of $A$. In this model, each infinite tree has either an infinite chain or an infinite antichain (216 is true), but there is an infinite partially ordered set that has neither an infinite chain nor an infinite antichain (217) is false. (See note 105.)

\noindent $\mathcal{N}35$: Truss' Model IV. The set of atoms, $A$, is denumerable and each element of $A$ is associated with a finite sequence of zeros and ones. We define a partial ordering $\precsim$ on $A$ such that if $a_{i},\, a_{j}\in A,\,a_{i}\precsim a_{j}$ if $a_{i}$ is an initial segment of $a_{j}$. Then, $(A,\,\precsim)$ is a tree. $\mathcal{G}$ is the group of permutation of $A$ which is generated by the set $\{\sigma_{a}:a\in A\}$ where if $\tau$ is the transposition (0, 1) and $a\precsim b$ then if $b=\langle a,\,i,\, b^{\prime}\rangle$, then $\sigma_{a}(b)=\langle a,\,\tau(i), b^{\prime}\rangle$, otherwise, $\sigma_{a}(b)=b$. For this model, it is easier to describe the filter $F$ of subgroups of $G$ rather than the ideal of supports $S$. $F$ is generated by $\{\mathcal{G}_{m}:m\in \omega\}$ where $\mathcal{G}_{0}=\mathcal{G}$, and $\mathcal{G}_{m+1}=\bigcap\{K:K$ is a subgroup of $\mathcal{G}_{m}\wedge|\mathcal{G}_{m}$: $K|=2\}$. In this model $(A,\,\precsim)$ is a binary tree with no infinite branch (249) is false, but for each $n\in \omega$ the Axiom of Choice for a well ordered family of $n$-element sets (250) is true.
