\chapter{References for Relationships Between Forms}\label{pt05:part05}

\section*{Introduction}

To explain this part of the book, it is helpful to consider some examples. Five typical lines are below.

\begin{table}[h]
\begin{tabular}{llll}
43 & 63 & (3) & Felgner\index{Author}{Felgner} [\textbf{1971a}] (M2)\\
85 & 78 & (3) & Brunner\index{Author}{Brunner} [\textbf{1980}] (N3T)\\
67 & 80 & (5) & Fraenkel\index{Author}{Fraenkel} [\textbf{1922}], Jech \cite{bib:1973b} (N2)\\
87 & 86 & (1) & Jech\index{Author}{Jech} \cite{bib:1973b} p 120 thm 8.1, Levy\index{Author}{Levy} [\textbf{1963a}], note 9\\
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

The first two numbers are form numbers. The third number which occurs in parentheses is a code number for the status of the implication. For example, in the first line above, the number 3 means that the implication ``form 43 implies form 63'' is not provable in Zermelo-Fraenkel (ZF) set theory. The other code numbers that we use are
\begin{enumerate}
\item[0] for ``The status of the implication is unknown.''
\item[1] for ``The implication is provable.''
\item[2] for ``The implication is provable and this fact follows from implications whose code numbers are 1.''
\item[3] for ``The implication is not provable in ZF.''
\item[4] for ``The implication is not provable in ZF and this fact follows from implications whose code numbers are 1 or 3.''
\item[5] for ``The implication is not provable in $\mathrm{ZF}^{0}$.''
\item[6] for ``The implication is not provable in $\mathrm{ZF}^{0}$ and this fact follows from implications whose code numbers are odd.''
\item[7] for ``The status of the implication is unknown and we have found the question asked somewhere in the literature.''
\end{enumerate}
(See the introduction for the definition of $\mathrm{ZF}^{0}$.)

The implication codes are odd numbers for the most part. In a typical line following the code number, is a reference to a bibliography item and possibly a note and, in the case of a non-implication, a model number. (We normally only list one model even if there are several models with this property.) In the first example above, Felgner [\textbf{1971a}] refers to the Bibliography and M2 refers to the model $\mathcal{M}2$ of ZF from our models section. ($\mathcal{M}2$ is a model in which form 43 is true and form 63 is false.)

In the second example above we see that form 85 implies form 78 is not provable in ZF set theory; the reference is Brunner [\textbf{1980}]; and the model is the permutation model $\mathcal{N}3$. $\mathcal{N}3$ is a model of $\mathrm{ZF}^{0}$. However, many of the results obtained for permutation models can be transferred to ZF models because of the work of Jech/Sochor\index{Author}{Jech/Sochor} [\textbf{1966a}], [\textbf{1966b}], and Pincus\index{Author}{Pincus} [\textbf{1971}], [\textbf{1972a}], [\textbf{1974c}], [\textbf{1977a}]. If a result is transferable, the numeral 3 will occur in the line to mean that the implication is not provable in ZF set theory. Following the reference, we give the permutation model with a ``$\mathrm{T}$'' following its number to indicate the result is transferable. (See note 18 for a list of forms that are transferable and note 103 for a summary of the transfer results of Jech/Sochor\index{Author}{Jech}\index{Author}{Jech/Sochor} [\textbf{1966a}] and [\textbf{1966b}] and Pincus\index{Author}{Pincus} [\textbf{1971}], [\textbf{1972a}], and [\textbf{1977a}].)

The letters ``IC'' following a model number indicate that an inaccessible cardinal was used to construct the model. In some cases, the reference is just a model. In these cases it is clear from the model itself why the implication does not hold. (See, for example, the line at position (317,3) and model $\mathcal{N}$38.)

It follows from example 3 above that form 67 implies form 80 is not provable in $\mathrm{ZF}^{0}$, the references are Fraenkel\index{Author}{Fraenkel} [\textbf{1922}] and Jech \cite{bib:1973b}, and the permutation model is $\mathcal{N}2$. The last example above tells us that form 87 implies form 86 in $\mathrm{ZF}^{0}$. The references are Jech \cite{bib:1973b} (p 120 theorem 8.1), Levy\index{Author}{Levy} [\textbf{1964}], and additional information can be found in note 9 in the notes section of the book. When note 120 is the reference, we state which part of the note applies. For example, at position (152,67) the reference is note 120(41). This means that we are using item 41 in note 120 ($67+122\leftrightarrow 1$, where form 1 is AC) to obtain the independence result. Form 122 is true in $\mathcal{N}$15, so by note 120 part 41, form 67 must be false. (AC is false in all our models.) In addition, form 152 is true in this model. Consequently, there is a 5 at position (152,67) below.

If the reference is note 18, we mean that either the first form listed is true in every permutation (FM) model, the second form is false in each such model, or the second form is false in every Cohen model. We have several forms that depend on parameters. (See note 18 for a list of these forms.) Sometimes the relationships between such forms depend on the value of the parameters. For example, we have the following line below:
\begin{equation*}
120\qquad 33\qquad (0)\qquad \mathrm{note}15\ (\mathrm{see}\ \mathrm{M}47(n, M))
\end{equation*}
Both forms 120 and 33 depend upon parameters. The notation means that for certain values of the parameters, form 120 is true in the model $M47(n, M)$ and form 33 is false. The reader should look at the model to determine when this holds.

Each of our weak forms of the Axiom of Choice is implied by AC (form 1), but for some of our forms, it is unknown whether they imply AC. Each one of these forms, $n$, is listed below in the form:
\begin{equation*}
n\qquad 1\qquad (7)\qquad \mathrm{reference}
\end{equation*}
Similarly, for some forms, it is unknown whether they are provable in $\mathrm{ZF}^{0}$. Each one of these forms, $m$, is listed below as:
\begin{equation*}
0\qquad m\qquad (7)\qquad \mathrm{reference}
\end{equation*}
In these two cases, for those forms for which we have not found a reference in the literature we use ``This project'' as the reference.
